da-1-3.answer:
TASK DA-1-3: SPATIOTEMPORAL SINGLE-CELL ANALYSIS OF IMMUNOTHERAPY RESPONSE IN CRC
=================================================================================

DATA
----
975,275 single cells from a spatiotemporal CRC anti-PD-1 cohort (GSE236581),
annotated into 91 fine-grained subtypes and 6 major lineages, across 166 tumour /
adjacent-normal / peripheral-blood samples (plus 2 LN and 1 TN sample, excluded from
the enrichment test). Composition was computed at both the whole-cohort level and the
per-sample level; subtype identities were independently verified against the raw UMI
count matrix (36,027 genes x 975,275 cells, 1.31e9 nonzeros) using canonical markers.


1. CELL-SUBSET DISTRIBUTION BY TISSUE COMPARTMENT
-------------------------------------------------
Share of cells within each compartment (major lineage):

  Lineage     Blood    Adjacent Normal    Tumour
  T cells     67.1%        27.9%           42.5%
  Epithelium   0.4%        35.6%           28.2%
  B cells     10.3%        24.9%           17.0%
  Myeloid     12.4%         1.8%            4.2%
  ILC          9.7%         0.9%            1.9%
  Stromal      0.1%         8.9%            6.2%

- BLOOD is lymphocyte/innate-dominated: circulating CD4/CD8 naive, central-memory and
  Temra T cells (c01_CD4_Tn_CCR7, c02_CD4_Tn_SELL, c24_CD8_Temra_CX3CR1, c31_DNT,
  c04_CD4_Tcm_ANXA1), CD14+/FCGR3A+ monocytes (c49/c50), and ILC (c35_ILC_FCGR3A).
  It has essentially no epithelium (0.4%) and almost no stroma (0.1%).

- ADJACENT NORMAL tissue is epithelial + lymphoid, dominated by the normal colonic
  programme: coloncytes (c84_Coloncyte_CA2, c85_Coloncyte_SLC26A3), goblet cells
  (c87_Goblet_MUC2), plus large T (27.9%) and B/plasma (24.9%, dominated by
  c46_PlasmaB_IGHA1) populations. Myeloid (1.8%) and ILC (0.9%) are scarce.

- TUMOUR is epithelial + T-cell rich, with expanded stroma and myeloid relative to
  normal: T cells 42.5%, epithelium 28.2% (switched from normal coloncytes/goblet to
  the NEOPLASTIC c91_Epi_Tumor and proliferative c90_Epi_MKI67), B cells 17.0%,
  stroma 6.2%, myeloid 4.2%, ILC 1.9%. The tumour is where the "tumour-specific"
  immune + stromal niche concentrates.


2. CELL TYPES SPECIFICALLY AND HIGHLY ENRICHED ONLY IN THE TUMOUR
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Ranked by tumour-specificity index (= fraction of all cells of that type that reside
in tumour). Every type below is statistically significant (Mann-Whitney U on
per-sample fractions; Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p < 0.05 vs BOTH adjacent normal
and blood), present in the overwhelming majority of the 58 tumour samples (74-100%),
and its molecular identity is confirmed by marker expression in the raw counts.

TIER 1 - essentially tumour-exclusive (84-99% of the cells of that type are in tumour):

  c23_CD8_Tex_LAYN          - CD8 terminal-exhausted T cell (PD-1/PDCD1+, TIM-3/HAVCR2+,
                               TOX+, LAG3+, TIGIT+, LAYN+). 11,455 tum / 536 normal / 14 blood.
                               tumour_index 0.951; log2FC vs blood ~14.
  c79_Fibro_FAP             - FAP+ POSTN+ COL1A1+ cancer-associated fibroblast (myCAF).
                               2,807 / 35 / 0. tumour_index 0.987.
  c64_Mph_SPP1              - immunosuppressive SPP1+ CCL3+ VEGFA+ tumour-associated
                               macrophage. 983 / 13 / 3. tumour_index 0.984.
  c70_Endo_COL4A1           - activated/angiogenic endothelium (COL4A1+, VWF+,
                               PECAM1+, ENG+). 2,442 / 68 / 3. tumour_index 0.970.
  c09_CD4_Th1_CXCL13_HAVCR2 - CXCL13+ PDCD1+ HAVCR2+ CD4 Th1/Tfh-like T cell (drives
                               tertiary lymphoid structures). 3,265 / 123 / 3. index 0.961.
  c63_Mph_CCL20             - CCL20+ CXCL8+ CXCL3+ inflammatory macrophage. 1,002 / 72 / 6.
                               tumour_index 0.925.
  c13_CD4_Treg_TNFRSF9      - activated/effector FOXP3+ CTLA4+ TNFRSF9(4-1BB)+ Treg.
                               8,100 / 1,097 / 19. tumour_index 0.872.
  c07_CD4_Th17_CTSH         - Th17-polarised CD4 T cell (RORC/IL17A/IL26 context).
                               3,349 / 591 / 4. tumour_index 0.840.
  c62_Mph_S100A8            - S100A8/A9+ LYZ+ inflammatory monocyte-macrophage.
                               1,513 / 317 / 25. tumour_index 0.809.
  c55_pDC_GZMB              - GZMB+ plasmacytoid dendritic cell (LILRA4+/IL3RA+/IRF7+/
                               TCF4+/CLEC4C+). 521 / 74 / 2. tumour_index 0.866.
  c91_Epi_Tumor             - neoplastic tumour epithelial cell (KRT8+, KRT18+, EPCAM+).
                               21,377 / 4,684 / 80. tumour_index 0.808 (largest single
                               tumour-enriched population).

TIER 2 - strongly tumour-enriched but with a recognisable normal/blood counterpart:
  c27_CD8_MAIT_SLC4A10 (KLRB1+ZBTB16+ MAIT, 0.775), c47_PlasmaB_IGHG1 (IgG1+ plasma cell,
  0.772), c12_CD4_Treg_KLRB1 (CD161+ Treg, 0.735), c81_Pericyte_RGS5 (0.759),
  c34_ILC_NR4A2 (0.708), c20_CD8_Tem_GZMK (GZMK+ effector-memory CD8; 0.706 but large
  normal normal counterpart), c65_Mph_APOE (TREM2+APOE+ lipid-associated TAM, 0.681),
  c08_CD4_Tfh_CXCL13_IL6ST (0.674), c29_T_MKI67 (proliferating T, 0.650).


3. BIOLOGICAL INTERPRETATION
---------------------------
The tumour microenvironment is characterised by a neoplastic epithelium plus an
immunosuppressive, immune-excluded niche of three cooperating compartments:

  (a) EXHAUSTED / REGULATORY T-CELL COMPARTMENT - terminally exhausted CD8 (PD-1/
      TIM-3/TOX/LAYN, tumour-reactive), CXCL13+ PD-1+ CD4 Th1/Tfh cells that organise
      tertiary lymphoid structures, and activated FOXP3+ CTLA4+ 4-1BB+ (and CD161+)
      regulatory T cells that blunt anti-tumour immunity. These are hallmarks of
      chronic antigen stimulation in a tumour under immunotherapy pressure.

  (b) IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE MYELOID COMPARTMENT - SPP1+ TAMs, CCL20+/CXCL8+ inflammatory
      macrophages, S100A8/9+ inflammatory monocytes, TREM2+APOE+ lipid-associated
      macrophages, and GZMB+ pDCs. Together these promote an immune-suppressive,
      pro-angiogenic milieu.

  (c) PRO-TUMOURAL STROMAL COMPARTMENT - FAP+ myofibroblastic CAFs (matrix remodelling
      + T-cell exclusion), activated COL4A1+/VWF+ angiogenic endothelium, and RGS5+
      pericytes.

The decisive finding for the "ONLY in the tumour" framing is that these Tier-1 types are
essentially ABSENT from peripheral blood (a handful of cells; several have 0-3 cells in
blood) and from adjacent normal colon. They are local, de-novo adaptations of the tumour
microenvironment, not circulating cell types that merely infiltrate. In contrast, the
circulating naive/memory T cells, monocytes, and normal colonic enterocytes/goblet/IgA
plasma cells dominate blood and normal tissue but are NOT tumour-specific.


4. LIMITATIONS
--------------
- Composition is RELATIVE (fraction of captured cells), not absolute cell density. Blood
  is heavily over-sampled (417k cells) and solid-tumour dissociation under-recovers
  stroma/myeloid, so tumour stromal/myeloid fractions are likely underestimated.
- No causal claim about immunotherapy response: the tumour-specific fraction did not differ
  significantly between CR and non-CR patients (aggregate p=0.455; individual types p>=0.068;
  Spearman with tumour regression ratio |rho|<=0.13, p>=0.33). The cohort is small (n=22,
  12 CR/7 PR/3 SD, mostly MSI/dMMR) and tumour samples are confounded by patient and
  treatment timepoint.
- "Tumour-exclusive" is relative to blood + adjacent normal only. LN (2) and TN (1) samples
  were too few to test; these states may also occur in other non-tumour niches/metastases.
- Cell types were taken from the study's SubCellType labels (marker-verified here, but not
  independently re-clustered). The broad conclusions map to canonical, cross-study cell
  states and are robust to clustering resolution.
- No spatial resolution: co-localisation (e.g. TLS structure, Treg-TAM proximity) cannot be
  assessed from dissociated single cells.
da-1-3.notes: The analysis is strong in subtype table construction, enrichment metric, ranking, annotation, and sourcing, but misses baseline-only filtering and lacks explicit translational therapeutic discussion.

da-1-4.answer:
QUESTION
For each patient, calculate the correlation between the tumor regression ratio and the baseline proportion of cell subtypes. Is the correlation positive or negative? What does this imply?

METHOD
For each of the 22 patients (P01-P26) in the CRC anti-PD-1 cohort (GSE236581), I used the baseline (pre-treatment, Treatment = I) tumor cells (105,959 cells total; 1,161-8,084 cells per patient) and computed the per-patient proportion of each cell subtype (6 major lineages and 91 fine-grained subtypes, taken from the study's own cell annotations in GSE236581_CRC-ICB_metadata.txt). Each per-patient subtype proportion was then correlated (Pearson and Spearman, n = 22) against that patient's Tumor Regression Ratio from clinical.xlsx.

DIRECTION OF THE CORRELATION

The correlation is POSITIVE for antigen-experienced / activated immune (T-cell) subtypes and NEGATIVE for differentiated normal epithelial (goblet / colonocyte) subtypes. No coarse major-lineage correlation was significant, and no subtype survived multiple-testing (Benjamini-Hochberg FDR) correction; the strongest findings are exploratory (unadjusted p < 0.05) and robust to bootstrap, permutation, and leave-one-out checks.

Headline correlations of baseline proportion with Tumor Regression Ratio (Pearson, n = 22):
  - CD4 regulatory T cell TNFRSF9 (c13_CD4_Treg_TNFRSF9):  r = +0.50,  p = 0.017   (Spearman rho = +0.47)
  - CD8 exhausted T cell LAYN   (c23_CD8_Tex_LAYN):        r = +0.47,  p = 0.026   (Spearman rho = +0.51)
  - Endothelial FABP5           (c68_Endo_FABP5):          r = +0.45,  p = 0.036
  - CD4 Temra GZMB              (c10_CD4_Temra_GZMB):      r = +0.41,  p = 0.059
  - Goblet MUC2                 (c87_Goblet_MUC2):         r = -0.39,  p = 0.075   (Spearman rho = -0.46)
  - Colonocyte CA2              (c84_Coloncyte_CA2):       r = -0.35,  p = 0.113
  - Tumor epithelial            (c91_Epi_Tumor):           r = +0.28,  p = 0.20

At the major-lineage level (none significant): ILC r=+0.19, T r=+0.18, Stromal r=-0.13, Epi r=-0.11, Mye r=-0.06, B r=-0.05.

WHAT THIS IMPLIES (biological / clinical interpretation)
1. Positive set (immune/activated T cells): patients whose baseline tumor already contained a higher proportion of antigen-experienced/inflamed T-cell states - specifically CD8 exhausted/dysfunctional T cells (LAYN+) and activated CD4 regulatory T cells (TNFRSF9/4-1BB+) - went on to show GREATER tumor regression after anti-PD-1 therapy. This is the familiar "hot"/pre-inflamed tumor phenotype: a pre-existing T-cell response is a strong predictor of checkpoint-inhibitor response (Tumeh 2014; Hugo 2016; Sade-Feldman 2018). The co-occurrence of TNFRSF9+ Tregs with response reflects an overall inflamed microenvironment rather than a beneficial role of Tregs themselves.

2. Negative set (differentiated normal epithelium): higher baseline proportions of goblet (MUC2+) and colonocyte (CA2+) lineages - i.e. a tumor dominated by differentiated non-malignant colonic epithelium rather than malignant/immune-infiltrated tissue - were associated with LOWER tumor regression. By contrast, the malignant tumor-epithelial compartment (c91_Epi_Tumor) trended POSITIVE with regression, indicating that more extensive tumor-cell content/immune infiltrate tracked with response while normal-differentiated epithelium tracked with non-response.

3. Net implication: baseline tumor immune infiltration (especially exhausted/activated T cells) is positively associated with anti-PD-1 tumor regression, whereas a baseline composition enriched for differentiated normal colonic epithelium is negatively associated with it. These are correlational, exploratory associations in a small (n = 22) mixed MSI/MSS cohort and do not establish causation.

LIMITATIONS
- n = 22 patients, 91 subtypes tested; after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction NO subtype is significant (smallest adjusted p ~ 0.73). Findings are exploratory/unadjusted.
- Correlation, not causation; no adjustment for MSI/MMR status (16 dMMR/MSI, 6 pMMR/MSS), treatment regimen, tumor site, or cell-capture depth. Direction was preserved within the dMMR/MSI subgroup (n=16) but no longer significant.
- Proportions are compositional; per-subtype univariate correlations are not mutually independent.
- Cell subtypes come from the study's own annotations; the raw expression matrix was not used for re-clustering. TRR is a clinical pathology index whose exact formula is not provided.
- The separate validation cohort (SP*/RP*) has no per-cell counts or TRR in the provided files and could not be used.
da-1-4.notes: Strong predictive workflow with correct baseline/tumor filtering, count-matrix construction, proportion normalization, and correlation analysis. Main gaps are the lack of rare/zero-variance filtering and incomplete highlighting of negative FAP/APOE candidates in the final interpretation.

da-3-4.answer:
FINAL ANSWER

Question: Is tumor mutational load associated with patient response to anti-PD-1 (pembrolizumab) therapy?

Primary result (pre-treatment WES, Hugo et al. 2016 / GSE78220, n = 38; 21 responders [R] and 17 non-responders [NR] by irRECIST):

Tumor mutational load, measured as total non-synonymous SNVs (TotalNonSyn) from exome sequencing, was HIGHER on average in responders than non-responders, but the difference was NOT statistically significant.

Summary statistics:
- Median TMB: R = 495 (IQR 313–807) vs NR = 281 (IQR 232–621); mean 817.9 (SD 918.7) vs 536.8 (SD 489.6).
- Mann-Whitney U (Wilcoxon rank-sum) test, two-sided: U = 214.0, p = 0.304 (one-sided R > NR, p = 0.152).
- Correlation metrics: point-biserial r = 0.186 (p = 0.264); Spearman rho = 0.171 (p = 0.304); rank-biserial (Cliff's delta) = 0.199.
- Association metric: univariate logistic-regression odds ratio = 1.06 per +100 non-synonymous SNVs (95% CI 0.95–1.19, p = 0.279).
- Discrimination: ROC AUC = 0.599 (chance = 0.5), permutation p = 0.148.
- Effect size: Hedges' g = 0.363 (small-to-moderate).

CONCLUSION: In this cohort, tumor mutational load is NOT significantly associated with anti-PD-1 response (all p > 0.15). The observed weak positive trend (higher TMB in responders) is small and was driven largely by two high-TMB responders (Pt4 = 3,985 and Pt27 = 2,297): after excluding them, the association fully disappeared (Mann-Whitney p = 0.568, AUC = 0.557). A top-quartile TMB split also showed no enrichment among responders (Fisher OR = 1.30, p = 1.0).

Robustness across alternative definitions of mutational load (all Mann-Whitney p >= 0.17, all AUC < 0.64):
- All SNVs including silent/non-coding (Total): p = 0.168
- Expression-filtered non-synonymous SNVs (TotalNonSyn_Exp): p = 0.628
- Indel burden: p = 0.171
- HLA class-I neoepitope burden (Binder): p = 0.411; StrongBinder: p = 0.318
- Neoepitope fraction of TMB: p = 0.60 (Binder) / 0.93 (StrongBinder)
- Mutation spectrum (six SNV classes): no fraction significant after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR (min adjusted p = 0.239 for A>C transversions)

Whether the association exists in the broader literature:
The observed direction (higher TMB in responders) is consistent with the widely reported biology linking mutation-derived neoantigens and high TMB to better immunotherapy response, but the effect in this specific 38-patient melanoma cohort is weak and NOT statistically significant.

What is instead strongly associated with response in this cohort:
- IPRES transcriptional signature (IPRES-high = 9/17 non-responders vs 1/21 responders; Fisher OR = 0.044, p = 0.0019). In a multivariate model (TMB + driver + IPRES), TMB remained non-significant (p = 0.563) while IPRES remained significant (p = 0.005).
- Specific recurrent gene mutations, not aggregate TMB. S1E gene-level recurrence: responder-enriched genes (FDR-adjusted p < 0.05) include FREM1, OR13C5, FMO1, UTRN, LPHN3, MUC12, ZNF534, SP140L, ITGA9, AMER3, ABCA7, OR10J1, and BRCA2; non-responder-enriched genes include TRPM2 and CLEC14A.

Key limitations: n = 38 (limited power; a modest true effect cannot be excluded — the OR 95% CI includes meaningful effects); mutational load is a non-synonymous SNV count and is a proxy for, not identical to, a standardized mutations/Mb TMB; no purity-normalization of mutation counts; single-arm observational data preclude causal inference; response is a coarse binary irRECIST outcome.

Boxplot / ROC / scatter figure: analysis/derived/tmb_response_figure.png

Primary statistical tests used: Mann-Whitney U (two-sided, primary) with point-biserial and Spearman correlation, plus logistic regression (OR), ROC AUC with permutation test, Cliff's delta and Hedges' g effect sizes, and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction for the exploratory spectrum comparisons.
da-3-4.notes: The agent's work satisfies all criteria at the highest level: correct data identification and loading, appropriate and justified statistical test, complete implementation and reporting, thorough descriptive statistics, contextual interpretation, and reliable sourcing.

da-3-5.answer:
MUTATION ENRICHMENT IN ANTI-PD-1 RESPONDERS (R) VS NON-RESPONDERS (NR) — Hugo et al. 2016 melanoma WES cohort (GSE78220)

COHORT: 38 pre-treatment melanoma patients (21 Responders, 17 Non-responders). Response per irRECIST (CR/PR/SD = R; PD = NR).
METHOD: Gene-level mutation recurrence. A patient counts as "mutated" in a gene if they carry at least one non-synonymous call in that gene (from Supplementary Table 1D, 25,393 variant calls / 9,877 genes). Genes recurrent in >=25% of a group (>=6 of 21 R, >=5 of 17 NR) with at most 1 mutation in the opposite group were screened (36 genes, matching Supplementary Table 1E exactly). Enrichment was tested per group against a fixed background prevalence (n=469 melanoma panel, Hodis 2012 + TCGA 2015) using a two-sided Fisher exact test, then Holm-Bonferroni (Holm step-down) multiple-testing correction. This reproduced Table S1E exactly (p-values match to ~1e-9; adjusted p-values to ~1e-8).

SIGNIFICANT GENES ENRICHED IN RESPONDERS (Holm-adjusted FDR < 0.05) — 13 genes:
  Gene    HitsR/nR  HitsNR/nNR  Raw p      Adjusted p (Holm)
  MUC12   6/21      1/17         2.9e-09    1.05e-07
  OR13C5  7/21      0/17         5.0e-06    1.75e-04
  FREM1   10/21     1/17         3.2e-05    1.09e-03
  ZNF534  6/21      1/17         5.6e-05    1.83e-03
  UTRN    7/21      0/17         6.2e-05    1.98e-03
  FMO1    7/21      0/17         6.2e-05    1.98e-03
  SP140L  6/21      0/17         1.9e-04    5.55e-03
  ITGA9   6/21      0/17         1.9e-04    5.55e-03
  AMER3   6/21      1/17         2.4e-04    6.72e-03
  LPHN3   7/21      1/17         3.5e-04    9.51e-03
  ABCA7   6/21      0/17         4.9e-04    1.26e-02
  OR10J1  6/21      0/17         6.0e-04    1.51e-02
  BRCA2   6/21      1/17         1.8e-03    4.37e-02

  Key specific responder mutations:
  - OR13C5 M185I (recurrent hotspot in 3 responders: Pt2, Pt3, Pt8); also D302N, E180K, H56Y, I78S, P79L.
  - FREM1: T526P, D590N, D922N, D1092N, H1103Y, P1527L, P2131L, P340S, R482C, K1280K.
  - MUC12: S4452L (2 patients), E306K, E68K, P708S, P898L, E3343K, S4089L, E5047K, T3296I, R3975W, Q4114* (nonsense).
  - BRCA2 (clinically notable): E2115K, H2361Y, H2537Y, P2505S, S2522F, V950L (R-side); S1792F is NR-only.
  - UTRN: E737K, D2395E, G1513R, G3394V, P853S, S2861F, S3379L; FMO1: D286N, D456N, G330R, G479E, G50S, P79L, S159F.

SIGNIFICANT GENES ENRICHED IN NON-RESPONDERS (Holm-adjusted FDR < 0.05) — 2 genes:
  Gene    HitsR  HitsNR/nNR  Raw p      Adjusted p (Holm)
  CLEC14A  0/21  5/17        7.9e-04    2.86e-02
  TRPM2    1/21  6/17        1.3e-03    4.70e-02

  Key specific non-responder mutations:
  - CLEC14A (4 missense + 1 truncating): E325K, E230K, E159K, R252C, and W93* (nonsense). 0 of 21 responders carry any.
  - TRPM2 (5 missense + 1 splice): V30S, E1219K, E1117K, S947F, T1025M, E829K, plus a splice-site disruption (Pt20). Single responder R909W.

INTERPRETATION:
- Responders are enriched for mutations in long, high-burden "bystander" genes (MUC12, FREM1, UTRN, FMO1, SP140L, ITGA9, ZNF534, OR13C5, etc.), consistent with higher overall tumor mutation burden (TMB) -> more neoepitopes -> better PD-1 response. BRCA2 (loss of homologous-recombination/DNA-repair; FDR 0.044) is the most clinically informative responder-enriched gene.
- Non-responders carry a smaller but specific recurrent signal: CLEC14A (a C-type lectin involved in endothelial/vascular adhesion) and TRPM2 (a Ca2+ channel in oxidative-stress and immune signaling). These are candidate resistance mechanisms, not established drivers.
- OR13C5 M185I is the strongest truly recurrent, position-specific mutation (3 responders).

LIMITATIONS:
- Very small cohort (21 vs 17); gene-level counts are only 0-10 per arm, so odds ratios are uncertain (MUC12 OR is infinite due to 0 background hits).
- Significance is reported within the authors' recurrence screening framework (>=25% of a group, <=1 in the opposite group). If Holms-Bonferroni were applied across ALL 9,877 genes without this screen, NO gene reaches FDR<0.05 (best raw direct R-vs-NR p ~0.010). Treat the result as recurrent-gene enrichment within the study's framework, not a genome-wide driver discovery.
- Most significant genes show heterogeneous (non-recurrent) amino-acid changes across patients; only OR13C5 M185I recurs at a single position. The signal is a gene-level burden, not a single shared lesion.
- Correlation, not causal; no functional validation. Purity/ploidy vary across tumors and were not normalized.
- The exact construction of the n=469 background hit counts (BGhit) is not fully derivable from the provided background tables; the published BGhit column was used. The conclusions about which genes dominate are robust because the patient-level hits come entirely from S1D (reproduced exactly).

CONCLUSION: FREM1, OR13C5, MUC12, UTRN, FMO1, SP140L, ITGA9, ZNF534, AMER3, LPHN3, ABCA7, OR10J1, and BRCA2 are significantly enriched (FDR<0.05) in responders; CLEC14A and TRPM2 are significantly enriched in non-responders.
da-3-5.notes: The agent performs a robust independent analysis and identifies BRCA2, but deviates in data source (S1B vs S1A) and statistical framework (background-normalized Holm rather than direct R-vs-NR BH-FDR), preventing full credit in criteria 1-3.

da-4-1.answer:
DA-4-1: NMF patient classification by tumor immune microenvironment composition

YES. Non-Negative Matrix Factorization of the patient × immune-cell-type composition matrix yields a stable, interpretable, and clinically meaningful patient classification for this anti-PD-1-treated NSCLC cohort (GSE243013, 1,254,749 immune cells, 243 patients, 51 immune subtypes).

INPUT MATRIX
- Patient × sub-cell-type proportion matrix (243 × 51), rows = patients, entries = fraction of that patient's sequenced immune cells of each subtype. Row sums = 1. Raw row-normalised proportions were used so NMF stays non-negative and the entries keep a "composition" meaning (TF-IDF and z-score variants were tested; raw proportions gave the best balance of stability, interpretability and clinical separation).

METHOD
- Consensus NMF (solver = multiplicative update) over k = 2...8 (50 random initialisations per k). Rank chosen by the joint criterion of cophenetic correlation of the consensus matrix (stability, Brunet 2004), silhouette in latent space (separation, no degenerate factor), and statistical association with pathological response.
- k = 4 was selected as OPTIMAL: median response-association p = 1.1e-05 and median continuous-rate KW p = 7.1e-07 across 40 independent fits (strongest among compact models), well-balanced non-degenerate factors, and biologically coherent programmes. Higher k (6-8) gained little and lost separation (silhouette dropped from 0.58 to 0.43-0.48); lower k (2-3) was coarser and far less associated with response.

FOUR-FACTOR PATIENT CLASSIFICATION (final k=4 model)
  F0  n=35  NK / cytotoxic-FGFBP2 programme   (NK_CD16hi_FGFBP2, CD8T_NK-like_FGFBP2)
              responder fraction 77.1%, mean pathological response rate 0.874
  F1  n=19  Myeloid / MARCO-macrophage programme (Mφ_MARCO, Mφ_VCAN, cDC2_CD1C)
              responder fraction 42.1%, mean rate 0.589
  F2  n=78  B-cell / tertiary-lymphoid programme (Bm_PDE4D, Bm_TNFSF9, Bm_TNF)
              responder fraction 66.7%, mean rate 0.848
  F3  n=111 Treg / exhausted-T programme (CD4T_Treg_FOXP3, CD8T_Tem_GZMK+GZMH+, CD8T_Tex_CXCL13)
              responder fraction 39.1%, mean rate 0.670

  (Responder = MPR + pCR; 242 patients had a known response label.)

STATISTICAL VALIDATION
- chi2(factor × MPR/pCR/non-MPR, 3-category) = 26.97, p = 1.5e-04, dof = 6.
- chi2(factor × responder-vs-non, MPR+pCR vs non-MPR) = 23.48, p = 3.2e-05, dof = 3.
- Kruskal-Wallis(pathological_response_rate | factor): H = 27.69, p = 4.2e-06.
- Responder fraction gradient: 77.1% (F0) > 66.7% (F2) > 42.1% (F1) > 39.1% (F3).
- The response label itself tracks the rate (Responder mean 0.987 vs non-responder 0.454, MWU p = 8.5e-42; internal consistency check).
- Most discriminating subtypes across factors (one-way ANOVA): Bm_PDE4D (F=103.8, p=4.9e-43), Mφ_MARCO (F=95.3, p=1.3e-40), NK_CD16hi_FGFBP2 (F=91.2, p=2.3e-39), CD8T_NK-like_FGFBP2 (F=88.4, p=1.7e-38), Mφ_CXCL2 (F=83.0, p=7.8e-37).
- Robustness: association persists after excluding patients with <500 cells (p=1.6e-03) and <1000 cells (p=3.7e-03), though it weakens as power falls. Factors are not explained by gender (p=0.147) or smoking (p=0.882); factor × cancer-type is weakly significant (p=4.9e-03).

INTERPRETATION
The optimal patient taxonomy (k=4) resolves the tumour immune microenvironment into four coherent archetypes: a cytotoxic-NK/FGFBP2 "hot" programme and a B-cell/tertiary-lymphoid programme (both responder-enriched), and an immunosuppressive MARCO-macrophage programme and a Treg/exhausted-T programme (both non-responder-enriched). This ordering is consistent with the established onco-immunology literature (NK/cytotoxic infiltration, B cells and tertiary lymphoid structures favour checkpoint response; MARCO+ macrophages and Foxp3+ Treg/exhausted CXCL13+ CD8 T cells associate with resistance) and provides a biologically meaningful, response-stratified patient grouping.

LIMITATIONS
- Compositional only (relative immune-cell frequencies; no tumour/stromal compartment, so "enrichment" can also reflect depletion of other types).
- Correlational, single-cohort, no survival endpoint (no PFS/OS in the data); cannot imply causality or a treatment-predictive biomarker for future patients.
- Confounded covariates (male-skewed 216/243, LUSC-dominant 180/243, >=5 different anti-PD-1 agents, imbalanced stage).
- Result depends on the row-normalised-proportion preprocessing choice; small groups (F1, n=19) have wide uncertainty.

Reproducibility: scripts analysis.py and final_analysis.py; results and figures in nmf_output/ (model_selection.csv, factor_summary.csv, factor_interp_top8.csv, patient_factor_assignment.csv; model_selection.png, factor_composition_heatmap.png, factor_response_bars.png, loading_heatmap.png, responder_fraction.png).
da-4-1.notes: The agent performed a coherent NMF pipeline but lost points on the primary matrix preprocessing (no filter/scaling) and the final single-initialisation fit; rank sweep, biological interpretation, and source reliability were strong.

da-4-6.answer:
Q: What proportion of non-MPR patients have high Texp cell levels that predict favorable
recurrence-free survival despite lack of pathological response?

ANSWER
======
Approximately 41% (~40.6% = 26/64) of the evaluable non-MPR patients who had a measurable
Texp (progenitor-exhausted / TCF7+CD8+ T-cell) level have a HIGH Texp feature. By the
whole-cohort median split (Texp.in.Tex.relevant*10 > 8.367), these high-Texp non-MPR patients
show clearly favorable recurrence-free survival despite lacking a pathological response:

  * Recurrence rate: 15.4% (4/26) in high-Texp non-MPR vs 44.7% (17/38) in low-Texp non-MPR.
  * Log-rank test (RFS): p = 0.011
  * 24-month RFS probability: 0.836 in high-Texp non-MPR vs 0.501 in low-Texp non-MPR.
  * Cox proportional-hazards: HR = 0.42 per 1-unit increase in log-scaled Texp
    (95% CI 0.28-0.63, p = 2.3e-05), i.e. ~58% lower recurrence hazard per unit.
  * Their survival is statistically indistinguishable from that of the pathological-response
    (MPR) group (log-rank p = 0.41), confirming "favorable despite non-MPR."

Denominator note: 70 non-MPR patients total, of which 64 had a measured Texp feature
(6 missing). 26/64 = 40.6%; if the 6 missing are kept in the denominator, 26/70 = 37.1%.
Both are reported; the evaluable-cohort fraction (40.6%, ~41%) is the primary answer.

Threshold sensitivity: the result is robust to the cutoff. Top-50% split -> 50.0% high
(p = 0.0004); upper third -> 32.8% (p = 0.031); top quartile -> 25.0% (p = 0.18). The
~40% figure sits within a 25-50% range of "high Texp" non-MPR proportions that all retain
a favorable-survival signal (top quartile is the least powered).

Interpretation: In this anti-PD-1-treated NSCLC cohort, ~2 in 5 non-MPR patients carry a
high abundance of progenitor-exhausted (Texp) CD8+ T cells. Despite not achieving a major
pathologic response, this subgroup has a much lower risk of recurrence, approximating the
outcome of MPR responders. High Texp therefore identifies a "non-responder-but-good-outcome"
subset. Limitation: this is an observational per-patient summary; only 22/70 non-MPR patients
recurred, so the survival comparisons are underpowered and the high-Texp subgroup is small
(n=26). Texp level is a proxy for intratumoral progenitor-exhausted CD8+ T cells and cannot by
itself establish causation; and 6 non-MPR patients lacked a Texp value.
da-4-6.notes: The agent performed a largely correct survival stratification but deviated from the rubric by using a whole-cohort median cutoff, omitting the overall 3-group log-rank and Cox group contrasts, and providing incomplete comparability/limitations.

  patient-specific; these 14 are a genuine, non-random signal.

* The strongest candidates are Tex-ENRICHED (exhaustion-specific), tested with Fisher's exact test
  vs the 19.1% global expanded-Tex background:
    - CASSLAGGDEQYF (rank 1, P70/P71): 73% of its expanded cells are Tex, odds=11.2, p=1.3e-100
    - CASSPTGTGLEGYTF (rank 3, P70/P71): 80% Tex, odds=16.9, p=2.4e-20

  was used as the primary definition.

  outcomes: P70 (nPR/LUAD), P71 (pCR/LUAD), P199 (pCR/LUSC), P200 (MPR/LUSC), P391 (nPR/LUSC),
  P482 (pPR/LUSC). None of the carriers are duplicated cellIDs, and they differ in age, PD-1 agent
  and response, so the sharing is real cross-patient sharing, not a technical duplicate.

* Caveat: 11 of 14 candidates are shared by the single pair P199/P200, whose expanded-Tex
  repertoires overlap unusually strongly (Jaccard ~0.61). Most candidates therefore have only
  2-patient evidence, concentrated in this pair.

MOST ACTIONABLE TCR-T CANDIDATES (recommend for further validation)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
 #1 TRAV8-1/TRAJ9/CAVKNTGGFKTIF + TRBV27/TRBJ2-7/CASSLAGGDEQYF  (P70/P71; largest, most Tex-skewed)
 #3 TRAV24/TRAJ35/CALIIGFGNVLHC + TRBV4-3/TRBJ1-2/CASSPTGTGLEGYTF (P70/P71; most Tex-specific, 80%)
 #2 TRAV12-3/TRAJ28/CAMSDLGAGAGSYQLTF + TRBV5-5/TRBJ1-1/CASSPGPGGTEAFF (P199/P200)

LIMITATIONS
-----------
These candidates are identified by shared sequence + expansion + exhaustion enrichment only. The data
contain no antigen/epitope or HLA restriction, so the specific target cannot be named here, and the
TCRs are not proven tumor-reactive (they could include bystander/viral-specific clones). No in vitro
or clinical validation is possible from these tables; and no single candidate reaches >=3 patients
under the strict full-chain definition. The P199/P200 concentration further limits independent
cross-patient support for most candidates.
da-4-7.notes: The analysis correctly builds a sequence-based public TCR search across patients, but it fails the required per-patient >=10-cell filter entirely, uses a broader exhausted subset than terminal-Tex, and lacks concrete preclinical-validation criteria.

QUESTION: Which proteins are promising drug targets for pancreatic cancer (PDAC) by considering BOTH (a) significant overexpression in PDAC tumors vs normal tissue AND (b) dependency in cancer cell lines based on CRISPR knockout screens?

CORE ANSWER
=================================================================
Using the CPTAC pan-cancer proteogenomic druggability dataset (mmc2/mmc3, Table S3A), the integrated indicator is the PDAC column of Table S3A. Per the dataset Information sheet, for a gene PDAC = 1 means the protein is "significantly overexpressed in tumor vs normal of that cancer cohort (adj. p <= 0.01) AND is also a gene dependency by CRISPR KO from DepMap in matched cancer cell line lineages (adj. p <= 0.01)". This is EXACTLY the conjunction the question asks for.

COUNT SUMMARY
- 5,262 candidate protein-coding genes in Table S3A.
- 1,431 genes satisfy BOTH conditions in PDAC (PDAC == 1: overexpressed in tumor vs normal AND a CRISPR dependency).
- Of these, 222 are assigned a druggability tier (Tier 1-5), i.e. they are validated or potentially druggable targets. 1209 of the 1431 have no drug tier and are therefore not (yet) actionable drug targets.
- Tier breakdown of the 222 druggable PDAC targets: Tier 1 = 34, Tier 2 = 32, Tier 3 = 61, Tier 4 = 73, Tier 5 = 22.

TIER SEMANTICS (validated from Tables S2A/S2B):
Tier 1 = targets of approved, cancer-indication drugs (highest, most clinically mature druggability). Tier 2 = targets of approved drugs (non-cancer specific). da-6-2.answer:
TEMPORAL DYNAMICS OF EXERCISE TRAINING RESPONSE IN VASTUS LATERALIS (SKM-VL)
=========================================================================
Analysis of 766 training-regulated genes (transcripts) in rat vastus lateralis
skeletal muscle over 1w / 2w / 4w / 8w of endurance training, males vs females.
(FDR = Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted timewise p-value < 0.05; per sex x timepoint.)

TOP-LINE ANSWER
---------------
Gene expression in SKM-VL responds to endurance training in a STRONGLY
SEX-DIMORPHIC and DYNAMIC (time-dependent) way:

1. FEMALES respond EARLY, BROADLY and PROGRESSIVELY.
   - 616 of 766 genes (80.4%) are significantly regulated in females at >=1
     timepoint (FDR<0.05). Counts: 1w=90, 2w=234, 4w=461, 8w=507.
   - The response ACCUMULATES with training duration, peaking at 4w-8w.
   - Predominant temporal shapes: a progressive rise into 4w-8w (largest
     cluster, ~251 genes) and a broad multi-window response (~173 genes),
     plus a transient EARLY wave of cell-cycle / proliferation genes
     (Kif22, Top2a, Aspm, Cenpf, Mki67, Prc1 -> peak ~2w) and early
     connective-tissue genes (Meox1, Col11a1, Tnmd -> peak 1w-2w, UP).

2. MALES respond LATE, NARROWLY and in an 8w-CONCENTRATED switch.
   - Only 275 of 766 genes (35.9%) respond in males; counts: 1w=27, 2w=28,
     4w=33, 8w=240. Males are almost SILENT through 1w-4w (<35 genes).
   - 222 of 275 male-responsive genes (80.7%) are significant ONLY at 8w.
   - Dominant male archetypes: a sharp 8w up-switch (e.g. Sln, Cfi, F2,
     Prodh1, Lipg) and an early-up-then-late-down reversal; 329 male genes
     flip the sign of their logFC between 1w and 8w (vs only 142 in females).
   - A male-specific DOWN-regulation of extracellular-matrix / collagen
     remodelling genes runs across 1w-4w (Col1a1, Col5a1, Col6a1, Col11a1,
     Lox, Emilin3, Ltbp2, Fbln1, Cilp) and is largely absent/opposite in
     females.

3. SHARED vs SEX-SPECIFIC.
   - 176 genes are regulated in BOTH sexes; 440 are female-only; 99 are
     male-only; 51 are training-regulated overall (training_q<0.05) but do
     not reach FDR<0.05 at any single sex x timepoint.
   - Of male-responsive genes, 64% are also female-responsive; of
     female-responsive genes only 28.6% are also male-responsive.
   - DIRECTION IS OVERWHELMINGLY CONCORDANT where shared: 169 of 176 shared
     genes move the SAME direction in both sexes; only 7 are discordant
     (Col11a1, Tnmd, Iqgap2, Ndrg1, Hsc70-ps2, + two unnamed). So the sexes
     share the DIRECTION of the adaptive program but differ in TIMING and
     BREADTH (females earlier/broader, males delayed/late-only).

4. STATISTICAL ROBUSTNESS of the sex asymmetry.
   - McNemar exact test (matched 766 genes): female-vs-male 1w significance
     p = 4.2e-09; 8w significance p = 6.1e-38.
   - Chi-square test on when genes are first detected: chi2=329.06, p = 5.1e-71.
   - Male 8w effects are also LARGER in magnitude (median |logFC| 0.417 vs
     female 0.314; Mann-Whitney p = 1.9e-09).

5. BIOLOGICAL SIGNATURE.
   - Both sexes ultimately up-regulate the oxidative/metabolic program:
     CKMT1 (mitochondrial creatine kinase; F 4w/8w up, M 8w up), SLC2A4/
     GLUT4 (8w up in both), and oxidative-phosphorylation enzymes Cycs,
     Cox4i1, Cox5b, Uqcrc1, Idh2 (female 4w/8w up; rising in males), plus
     LPL (female 4w/8w up). Immediate-early stress genes (FOS, EGR1, NR4A3)
     are SUPPRESSED with training (FOS down in females across all windows).
   - This is consistent with a mitochondrial / oxidative adaptation and a
     dampened acute-stress program, but the female version is deployed
     earlier and more broadly.

CONCLUSION
----------
In vastus lateralis, endurance training drives a dynamic, time-resolved
transcriptional program whose predominant pattern is SEX-DIMORPHIC:
females mount a broad, progressive, early-starting response (largest group
rising into 4w-8w, with an early proliferative/connective wave), while males
remain transcriptionally near-silent through 4w and then undergo an abrupt,
large-magnitude, 8w-concentrated switch (notably remodelling ECM/collagen
and up-switching genes such as Sln and Cfi). Where both sexes respond, they
do so in the same direction (169/176 concordant) but on different schedules
-- the adaptive metabolic program is shared, while its timing and breadth
are sex-specific.

LIMITATIONS
-----------
- The table only lists features already passing the source study's global
  combined training FILTER (training_q<0.05); canonical markers absent here
  (Myod1, Myog, Myh1/2/4/7, Ppargc1a/PGC-1alpha) cannot be ruled out as
  responsive, only as below that cut-off.
- Only differential statistics (logFC/p/z) are provided, not raw counts or
  replication variance, and no explicit sex x training interaction test exists.
- Transcripts only (SKM-VL); no acetylome/proteome/metabolome of this tissue,
  and no cell-type deconvolution from bulk data.
- 9.4% of genes (72) map to no current rat symbol (several are the largest
  effects), and 1w/2w/4w/8w are independent training-duration groups, not a
  longitudinal within-animal time course.
da-6-2.notes: The analysis is carefully done and biologically rich but misses the core 4-timepoint directional completeness and 4-state encoding required by the rubric, instead using any significant timepoint and overall direction; categories exist but are based on ever-responsive status.

da-6-5.answer:
Answer to "To what extent does endurance training elicit coordinated molecular responses across different organs, and which tissues exhibit the most similar changes?"

Based on the MoTrPAC rat endurance-training differential results (279,002 training-regulated feature rows; 9,800 transcript genes across 19 tissues):

CONCLUSION — Coordination is real but CONCENTRATED, not universal.
Across all tissues, the aggregate coordination is only modestly above chance: feature-gene overlap is ~1.4% above expectation (16,412 shared gene-pairs observed vs. 16,185 expected, Monte Carlo p=0.012), and shared features move in the same direction 52.8% of the time vs. 50.0% under a sign-permutation null (p=0.001). A gene is significantly regulated in ~1.9 tissues on average, and 49.3% of regulated genes appear in >=2 tissues. So endurance training does induce a coordinated multi-organ program, but it is dominated by a SUBSET of biologically related organs rather than being a uniform whole-body response. A large majority of tissue pairs are near-chance (median overlap ~0.97x expected).

MOST SIMILAR TISSUES (ranked):
1. SKM-GN (gastrocnemius) vs. SKM-VL (vastus lateralis) — the clear winner. Highest shared-gene count enrichment (4.93x expected, hypergeometric FDR<1e-4), highest Jaccard (0.196), and by far the strongest directional concordance: 96.3% of 218 shared genes move in the SAME direction, with Pearson r=0.89 and Spearman rho=0.90. They cluster together first in the dendrogram.
2. BLOOD vs. SPLEEN — 74.6% same-direction among 338 shared genes (r=0.58), an immune/hematopoietic co-response.
3. LUNG vs. SPLEEN — 71.3% same-direction (r=0.64).
4. LUNG vs. SMLINT — 69.9% same-direction (r=0.39).
5. HEART vs. SKM-VL — 69.7% same-direction (r=0.37), the muscle-cardio axis.
6. HEART vs. SKM-GN — 65.5% same-direction (r=0.36).
7. ADRNL vs. BAT — 947 shared genes, 65.0% same-direction.

CROSS-OMIC SUPPORT: The coordinated core is the set of metabolic/effector organs — skeletal muscle, heart, liver, plasma, and adipose (BAT/WAT-SC). Metabolomics shows liver-heart-plasma-muscle metabolite responses strongly shared and directionally concordant (LIVER-PLASMA r=0.63, HEART-PLASMA r=0.55, HEART-SKM-GN r=0.42, LIVER-SKM-GN r=0.54). Proteomics mirrors this (HEART-LIVER r=0.61, HEART-SKM-GN r=0.38). Most striking, the heart-liver protein ACETYLOME is 80% correlated (r=0.80 across 100 shared sites) — a coordinated acylation switch in two highly oxidative organs. Chromatin (ATAC) and methylation responses are more tissue-local and weakly concordant; circulating analytes (immunoassay) are led by the adrenal-plasma endocrine axis.

TEMPORAL DYNAMICS: Coordination is NOT monotonic and consolidates at the late stage. Mean directional concordance across all pairs dips from 1w (0.551) to 4w (0.517) and partially recovers at 8w (0.532). The muscle pair SKM-GN/SKM-VL strengthens steadily to ~0.96 same-direction by 8w; BLOOD-SPLEEN and ADRNL-BAT dip at 4w then rebound to ~0.90 at 8w; LUNG-SMLINT transiently anti-coordinates at 4w (0.25). The coordinated muscle/circulatory/adipose-hepatic adaptation is most entrained at the 8-week stage — consistent with a chronic-exercise remodelling response that takes weeks to establish.

BOTTOM LINE: Endurance training elicits a genuine but tissue-specific coordinated molecular response. The two skeletal muscles (SKM-GN and SKM-VL) are by far the most similar in their response (near-identical, ~96% same-direction, r~0.89), followed by a blood-spleen (immune) axis and a muscle-cardio axis. Metabolomics and the heart-liver acetylome corroborate a coordinated systemic metabolic/energy-adaptation across muscle, heart, liver, plasma, and adipose tissue. Coordination grows with training duration and is strongest at 8 weeks.

WHAT THIS CANNOT SAY: These are pre-filtered, training-regulated summary statistics, so overlap is measured among features already deemed significant per tissue (not the whole genome), and no causal/mechanistic or clinical-magnitude claims can be made. PTM (ubiquitinome, acetylome-only-2-tissues), methylation, and ATAC coverage is sparse, and no pathway/GO functional assignment was possible from the supplied gene IDs alone.
da-6-5.notes: The agent's work is strong on coverage identification, feature filtering, de-duplication, per-assay similarity computation, and interpretation, but it fails to perform the required cross-assay aggregation into a single tissue-pair score.

da-8-1.answer:
DA-8-1 — Bread-spiker hypertension-associated metabolites

QUESTION

positive correlation with systolic blood pressure (SBP) within the 'Bread-spiker'

METHOD SUMMARY

da-8-2.answer:
INTERACTION EFFECT SIZE BETWEEN BASELINE INSULIN RESISTANCE AND THE PROTEIN-vs-FIBER PRELOAD EFFECT ON PEAK GLUCOSE

DATA & ANALYTIC DEFINITION
- Mitigator challenge: the same rice meal preloaded with protein ("Rice+Protein") vs fiber ("Rice+Fiber"). 23 participants; per-subject peak glucose computed per replicate then averaged per condition.
- Per-subject response magnitude: delta_peak = Peak(Rice+Fiber) - Peak(Rice+Protein). Positive = protein preload lowered the peak (a larger peak-glucose reduction with protein); negative = protein preload raised the peak.
- Baseline insulin resistance (IR) status from SSPG (insulin suppression test, the direct reference measure), clinical cut-off SSPG >= 150 mg/dL = insulin-resistant.
- n = 19 of 23 subjects had SSPG; 4 with missing SSPG were excluded.

PRIMARY RESULT (2 x 2 interaction, mitigator x IR):
  Peak glucose cell means (mg/dL):
    Insulin-sensitive (SSPG<150, n=15): Fiber=164.77, Protein=152.62 -> delta = +12.16
    Insulin-resistant  (SSPG>=150, n=4): Fiber=153.60, Protein=170.91 -> delta = -17.31

  RAW INTERACTION (difference in deltas, NonIR - IR) = +29.46 mg/dL
    = protein preload lowers peak glucose ~29 mg/dL more in insulin-sensitive than in insulin-resistant individuals.

  STANDARDIZED EFFECT SIZES:
    Cohen's d = 1.49   (pooled SD; Glass's delta = 1.46)
    Partial eta^2 = 0.29  -> Cohen's f = 0.64
    R^2 of delta_peak ~ IR model = 0.291

  STATISTICAL SIGNIFICANCE:
    Mixed-design 2-way ANOVA interaction: F(1,17) = 6.99, p = 0.017
    Welch t-test (NonIR vs IR delta): t = 2.82, p = 0.036
    Mann-Whitney U: p = 0.027
    Continuous: Pearson r(SSPG, delta_peak) = -0.541, p = 0.017; Spearman rho = -0.502, p = 0.029
    Bootstrap 95% CI: raw interaction = 11.5 to 47.0 mg/dL; Cohen's d = 0.63 to 2.91

INTERPRETATION (crossover interaction)
In insulin-sensitive individuals protein preload reduces the post-rice glycemic peak relative to a fiber preload (+12.2 mg/dL), whereas in insulin-resistant individuals protein preload is associated with a HIGHER peak than fiber (-17.3 mg/dL). The effect is a heterogeneity/moderator effect, not an overall average effect: the whole-cohort mean delta across all 23 subjects was +5.74 mg/dL (one-sample t p = 0.215) and neither main effect in the mixed ANOVA was significant (mitigator p = 0.207, IR p = 0.889). Mechanistically consistent with protein preload augmenting insulin/incretin output: in insulin-sensitive people this lowers the peak, while in an insulin-resistant state the amplified insulin demand is not compensated, so the peak is not suppressed (or is higher). SSPG captures this whole-body insulin-stimulated glucose disposal axis, which is why the effect is strong with SSPG but absent with the HOMA-IR surrogate (HOMA-IR >= 2.5: IR delta = +5.60 vs NonIR +5.79, interaction = +0.19, p ~ 0.99, d = 0.01).

ROBUSTNESS
- Post-ingestion peak (t>=0): interaction = +29.76 mg/dL, Cohen's d = 1.50, p = 0.017 (unchanged).
- Adjusting for age, BMI, or fasting glucose: IR coefficient stays ~ -28 mg/dL (p ~ 0.028-0.032).
- Median-SSPG split: interaction maintained (above-median delta = -4.2, below = +15.1, d = 0.91, p = 0.064).
- iAUC-based magnitude: same direction, interaction = +1629 (mg/dL*min), d = 0.84, but p = 0.156 (not significant).

LIMITATIONS
- Only 4 insulin-resistant participants (n=4) -> large but imprecise effect (wide bootstrap CI for d). Small sample.
- Interaction is specific to the SSPG-defined IR; it vanishes with HOMA-IR. Missing SSPG for 4/23 subjects (excluded).
- iAUC metric gives same direction but not significant. No causal claim; observational between-subject contrast.
- Olink proteomics (only 20 samples) not usable to test protein-level mediation.

ANSWER: The interaction effect size between baseline insulin resistance (SSPG >= 150) and the protein-vs-fiber preload effect on peak glucose is 29.46 mg/dL (difference in peak-glucose reduction), a large effect (Cohen's d = 1.49; partial eta^2 = 0.29, Cohen's f = 0.64) that is statistically significant (mixed-ANOVA interaction p = 0.017; Welch t p = 0.036; Mann-Whitney p = 0.027). The direction is a crossover: protein preload lowers the peak in insulin-sensitive individuals (+12.2 mg/dL) but is associated with a higher peak in insulin-resistant individuals (-17.3 mg/dL) relative to fiber preload.
da-8-2.notes: The agent's analytical pipeline is mostly traceable and references are sound, but it deviates from the required IR classification strategy and peak baseline adjustment, leading to inflated and statistically significant interaction results rather than the expected non-significant small interaction.

da-8-3.answer:
DA-8-3: Individual Variations in Glycemic Responses
====================================================

Using the metabolomics quantification data and the participant phenotypic classifications,
identify the top 10 differentially abundant metabolites between the 'potato-spiker' and

Each participant's food-specific glycemic response was quantified as the incremental area
under the CGM glucose curve (iAUC, 0-120 min above the meal's own baseline) for the base

responses are only moderately correlated (r=0.67), the phenotype was defined by the
food-specific contrast: delta = z(potato) - z(grape). The top tertile of delta within the
metabolomics-covered participants were called POTATO-SPIKERS and the bottom tertile
GRAPE-SPIKERS (9 vs 9, no overlap, mean potato iAUC 4877 vs 2410; mean grape iAUC 1717 vs 2825).

Mann-Whitney p=0.031; HOMA-IR 2.94 vs 1.83) with lower beta-cell function (DI 1.32 vs 1.76),

HIGHER in potato-spikers unless indicated.

  C16:0 AC (L-Palmitoylcarnitine): a-path (group->metab) p=0.015, b-path (metab->SSPG) = +102.6,
      indirect a*b = +37.6, MEDIATED = 42.6% of the group effect (Sobel p=0.19, permutation p=0.11).
  C16:0 AC(1) (L-Palmitoylcarnitine): a*p=0.010, b=+108.2, a*b=+41.6, MEDIATED = 47.2% (perm p=0.089).

Beta-cell function (DI, total effect c = -0.44):
  C16:0 AC (L-Palmitoylcarnitine): a-path p=0.015, b-path = -0.851, a*b = -0.31,
      MEDIATED = ~70.5% of the group effect (permutation p=0.060).

All other top-10 lipids explain <20% of the effect on SSPG and show weak/inconsistent
mediation on DI. A mean-z composite of the six acylcarnitine species was sharply higher in
potato-spikers (mean z +0.616 vs -0.191, MWU p=0.011, Cohen's d=0.96), confirming the
phenotype difference, but was not itself correlated with the clinical indices across the
full cohort (|r|<0.11), meaning the acylcarnitines are a robust phenotype/mechanism marker
but their role as a continuous driver is underpowered at this sample size.

CONCLUSION
Palmitoylcarnitine (C16:0 / L-Palmitoylcarnitine) is the specific lipid species within the
top-10 that most plausibly mediates the potato-spiker excess in insulin resistance (42-47% of
the SSPG difference) and the lower beta-cell function (up to ~70% of the DI difference),
consistent with lipotoxic acyl-lipid accumulation under fatty-acid oxidation overload.

STATISTICAL CAVEATS
- No metabolite survived BH-FDR q<0.05 (min q=0.845); the top-10 is a discovery ranking, not
  FDR-confirmed. The mediation indirect effects have wide bootstrap CIs that include 0 and
  Sobel/permutation p-values of 0.06-0.19, so NONE reaches the conventional alpha=0.05.
- The analysis is cross-sectional and hypothesis-generating, not causal; the potato-spikers
  were also older (63.8 vs 54.8 y, p=0.042) and sex-distributions differed, which are partial
  confounders. Findings are limited by the small n (9/9) and by missing SSPG/DI in some
  participants (mediation n=16).
da-8-3.notes: The differential-abundance and statistical-testing portions are solid, but the spiker classification deviates from the required median-split peak method and the required per-lipid phenotype correlations are missing, lowering phenotyping and mediation-integration scores.

da-9-1.answer:
QUESTION
--------
For patients receiving nivo/chemo (anti-PD-1 + chemotherapy), what circulating
T cell populations at baseline could serve as associative biomarkers for
1-year overall survival?

ANSWER
------
The baseline circulating T-cell population most strongly and robustly
associated with favorable 1-year overall survival in the nivo/chemo cohort
(anti-PD-1 nivolumab + gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel, NO CD40 agonist) of the
PRINCE (PICI0002) trial is:

    Tbet+ TCRgd+ T cells  (as a fraction of total gd T cells)

Quantitative result (primary nivo/chemo cohort, N=27 with baseline biomarker
+ OS: 14 one-year survivors vs 9 who died within a year):
  * Per-SD hazard ratio (Cox proportional hazards) = 0.361
      (95% CI 0.195-0.668), p = 0.0012, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR-adjusted
      p = 0.0081.
  * Survival-proportional-hazards assumption satisfied (PH p = 0.84).
  * Median-split Kaplan-Meier logrank p = 0.025 (high gd-Tbet vs low).
  * After adjusting for age and ECOG performance status: HR = 0.343,
      p = 0.0007 (effect strengthens).
  * Independent of the correlated Tbet+ T-cell population (multivariate:
      gd-Tbet+ HR = 0.377, p = 0.0074; Tbet+ T cells HR = 0.913, p = 0.82).

Interpretation: HIGHER baseline Tbet+ gd T cells (a type-1 / IFN-gamma-
programmed, innate-like effector T-cell subset) is associated with a LOWER
hazard of death -> better 1-year survival under anti-PD-1 + chemotherapy.
This is mechanistically consistent with a pre-existing type-1 effector T-cell
program that PD-1 blockade can reactivate.

Secondary (suggestive but NOT FDR-significant / not adjustment-robust, so
reported as weaker candidates only):
  * NKT cells (% of leukocytes): Cox HR = 0.422 (p = 0.026, Cox FDR = 0.090);
      age/ECOG-adjusted HR = 0.249 (p = 0.0047). Higher baseline NKT ->
      better 1-year OS. Co-correlated with Tbet+ TCRgd+ (rho = 0.49).
  * Tbet+ T cells (% of CD3+): logrank p = 0.0115, but age/ECOG-adjusted
      p = 0.088 (not significant) and fully explained by Tbet+ TCRgd+.
  * Ki-67+ T cells: direction opposite (per-SD HR = 1.679, p = 0.11), not
      significant; values (mean 0.93, range 0.68-1.0) are biologically
      implausible for a proliferation marker, so treated as an artifact.
  * HLA-DR+ T cells, HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD4 and CD8 T cells: no association
      (all Cox p >= 0.21).

Sensitivity check: in ALL nivolumab recipients (including the full
nivolumab + CD40-agonist combination arm, N=51 with baseline biomarker + OS),
Tbet+ TCRgd+ T cells remained the only FDR-significant population
(HR = 0.628, p = 0.0079, Cox FDR = 0.0395), confirming the signal is a
genuine anti-PD-1-associated effect and not an artifact of cohort selection
or of the CD40-agonist arms.

Limitations (this is ASSOCIATIVE only): single center-group trial, small
evaluable N (~27), wide confidence intervals, no external validation; the
available data are population FRACTIONS with no absolute counts, so the
driver (numerator vs denominator) cannot be separated; results may not
generalize beyond PDAC / this regimen; the strong positive correlation among
the type-1 T-cell readouts means they are not independent discoveries.

Net: The best-supported "answer" is the baseline Tbet+ TCRgd+ (type-1
programmed gd) T-cell population. A plausible supplementary theme, with
weaker support, is that a broader baseline IFN-gamma-producing innate
T-cell programme (NKT, Tbet+ T cells) also trends favorably.
da-9-1.notes: The agent performed a thorough analysis with correct data loading and feature selection, and its computed log-rank p-values match the expected significant features, but deviations in measurement-scale filtering, reporting of all significant features, and some methodology/reporting details prevent full marks.

da-9-7.answer:
ANSWER — PRINCE trial chemoimmunotherapy biomarkers (DA-9-7)

Question: Do circulating immune-cell frequencies correlate with serum protein levels on-treatment at C2D1?

SHORT ANSWER
No. In the PRINCE (PICI0002) dataset, no circulating immune-cell frequency is significantly correlated with any
on-treatment serum protein at C2D1 after multiple-testing correction.

DETAIL
At C2D1 (cycle 2, day 1), the analyzable joint panel is restricted to 4 CyTOF circulating cell populations
(CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells, Conventional DC, HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD4 T cells, HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD8 T cells)
and 4 Olink serum proteins (CXCL9, CXCL10, IFN-gamma, Soluble PD-1). Correlating cell frequency vs protein at the
patient level (73 patients had both a C2D1 cell measurement and a C2D1 protein measurement; n = 65 per pair for the
B-cell/T-cell populations and n = 73 for Conventional DC), using Spearman's rank correlation across all 16 pairs:

- Strongest pair: CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells vs CXCL9, rho = -0.233, p = 0.062 (nominal only).
- Second: CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells vs CXCL10, rho = -0.222, p = 0.076 (nominal only).
- All other pairs: |rho| <= 0.16, p > 0.19.

After Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, the smallest adjusted p-value is about 0.54 (Bonferroni-adjusted ~0.99-1.00),
so no pair remains significant. Bootstrap/Fisher 95% confidence intervals for the two leading B-cell-chemokine
associations include (or sit immediately at) zero: B cells vs CXCL9 CI = [-0.453, 0.006]; B cells vs CXCL10
CI = [-0.424, -0.000].

Robustness checks all agree with the null:
- Partial correlation controlling for the randomized treatments (APX005M and/or nivolumab): largest = CD4 T cells vs
  Soluble PD-1 (partial rho = 0.257, p = 0.039), but FDR-adjusted p = 0.51; the B-cell-chemokine trends persist but
  stay weak (partial rho = -0.21, -0.21) and non-significant after correction.
- Arm-stratified Spearman (A1/GEM/NP/nivo, B2/GEM/NP/APX005M, C2/GEM/NP/nivo/APX005M): no direction-consistent,
  corrected-significant association; the few nominal per-arm signals (e.g. CD4 T vs IFN-gamma in arm C2, rho = -0.63,
  p = 0.003) are single exploratory cells in a 24-test grid and are inconsistent across arms.
- Change-from-baseline (delta = C2D1 - C1D1) correlation (3 overlapping cell populations x 4 proteins, n = 53):
  largest = CD4 T cells vs IFN-gamma (rho = -0.178, p = 0.20), not significant; no pair survives.

Biological interpretation: the on-treatment circulating cell populations measured at C2D1 are mostly activated T-cell
markers (HLA-DR+ non-naive CD4/CD8), a dendritic-cell compartment (Conventional DC), and a specific B-cell subset
(CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells), whereas the on-treatment serum proteins form an IFN-gamma/chemokine program
(CXCL9, CXCL10, IFN-gamma, which are strongly inter-correlated here: CXCL9-CXCL10 rho = 0.77) plus soluble PD-1.
These two compartments are not tightly linked: blood T-cell activation frequency is a compartmental read-out and does
not scale linearly with the systemic cytokine/chemokine burden, and soluble PD-1 is a distinct axis (only weakly
correlated with the IFN-gamma chemokines; e.g. vs CXCL9 rho = 0.40, vs IFN-gamma rho = 0.20). The only coherent
direction is a weak inverse trend between CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B-cell frequency and CXCL9/CXCL10, which is biologically
plausible (this B-cell subset is not an IFN-gamma-producing cell; an inverse relation could reflect divergent
differentiation) but is hypothesis-generating at best and is not statistically robust.

Limitations: only 4 cell populations and 4 proteins were available at C2D1 (the wider panels were measured only at
baseline/C1D15), n ~ 65-73 is small and under-powered to detect modest |rho| < ~0.3 after controlling for 16 tests,
the data are cross-sectional (no causal inference), treatment heterogeneity and compositional (relative-frequency)
structure of CyTOF proportions are not fully modeled, and the CyTOF MSI epitope data are C1D15-only and could not be
used for the C2D1 question.

Conclusion: on-treatment at C2D1, circulating immune-cell frequencies do NOT significantly correlate with serum
protein levels in the PRINCE dataset. The observed inverse B-cell versus CXCL9/CXCL10 trend is a weak,
nominal-only, hypothesis-generating signal that does not survive multiple-testing correction.
da-9-7.notes: The agent performed a careful C2D1 harmonisation and pooled Spearman analysis, but over-included a fourth CyTOF population, did not apply per-arm FDR, and consequently missed the required Arm C2 significant finding; source reliability is strong.

da-10-1.answer:
DA-10-1 — ML Screening of Membraneless Organelle Participants
FINAL ANSWER
============================================================

PART 1 — AMINO-ACID COMPOSITION: PS-SELF (SaPS) vs PS-PART (PdPS)
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Using the human benchmark subsets (hSaPS, n=59 self-assembling; hPdPS, n=96
partner-dependent; both exclusively Homo sapiens), the mean residue
composition differs in a consistent, interpretable way. Values are fraction of
the protein's residues that are that amino acid; Δ = mean(hSaPS) − mean(hPdPS);
p is a two-sided Mann–Whitney U test (Bonferroni threshold for 20 residues =
0.0025).

ENRICHED in PS-Self (self-assembling):
  Gly  hSaPS 0.0924 vs hPdPS 0.0668  Δ = +0.0255   p = 3.2e-4  (significant)
  Gln  hSaPS 0.0591 vs hPdPS 0.0499  Δ = +0.0092   p = 0.063
  Pro  hSaPS 0.0802 vs hPdPS 0.0712  Δ = +0.0090   p = 0.072
  Ser  hSaPS 0.0913 vs hPdPS 0.0844  Δ = +0.0070   p = 0.141
  Tyr  hSaPS 0.0292 vs hPdPS 0.0252  Δ = +0.0040   p = 0.507

DEPLETED in PS-Self (i.e., enriched in PS-Part):
  Leu  hSaPS 0.0693 vs hPdPS 0.0855  Δ = −0.0162   p = 4.6e-4  (significant)
  Lys  hSaPS 0.0550 vs hPdPS 0.0692  Δ = −0.0142   p = 0.0026  (marginal)
  Glu  hSaPS 0.0659 vs hPdPS 0.0795  Δ = −0.0137   p = 1.3e-3  (significant)
  Arg  hSaPS 0.0580 vs hPdPS 0.0695  Δ = −0.0115   p = 0.086
  Ile  hSaPS 0.0337 vs hPdPS 0.0389  Δ = −0.0052   p = 0.107

After Bonferroni correction, G, E, and L are individually significant (Lys
marginal). The pattern is highly directional and conservative: self-assembling
proteins are richer in the disorder-promoting, low-complexity residues
(Gly/Pro/Ser/Gln, plus Tyr) that drive sticker-and-receptor self-condensation,
and poorer in charged (Lys, Glu, Arg) and hydrophobic (Leu, Ile) residues
typical of folded, RNA/nucleic-acid-binding and nuclear-transport domains whose
condensation is conferred by binding partners.

The same pattern is reproduced on the cross-species SaPS (n=128) vs PdPS
(n=214) sets: Gly (+0.0286), Pro (+0.0129), Ser (+0.0096), Gln (+0.0079),
Thr (+0.0070) enriched; Leu (−0.0162), Lys (−0.0131), Glu (−0.0113),
Ile (−0.0090) depleted (Bonferroni-significant: G, P, Q, C, H, I, E, K, L).

Order-disorder context: mean intrinsic-disorder fraction (from IDR ranges)
is hSaPS 0.326 > hPdPS 0.267 > hNoPS 0.138 (hSaPS vs hPdPS, p = 0.066) —
self-assembling proteins are intrinsically more disordered.


PART 2 — PREDICTOR PERFORMANCE (AUROC; AUPRC in parentheses)
------------------------------------------------------------
Classification tasks against the non-PS human background (hNoPS). Higher score
= more phase-separation-like for all descriptors. AUPRC is low because the
positive class is ~1% of the proteome (prevalence hSaPS 0.7%, hPdPS 1.1%).

(a) PS-SELF, hSaPS (n=59) vs hNoPS (n=8801):
  PLAAC        AUROC 0.831  (AUPRC 0.120)   -- best
  PScore       AUROC 0.813  (AUPRC 0.133)
  catGRANULE   AUROC 0.813  (AUPRC 0.062)
  FuzDrop*     AUROC 0.779  (AUPRC 0.019)   -- weakest
  (for reference: SaPS-8fea 0.987, SaPS-10fea 0.990)
  The three classic predictors are statistically indistinguishable (paired
  bootstrap AUC-difference CIs span 0); all are above the FuzDrop-IDR proxy,
  whose deficit is marginal.

(b) PS-PART, hPdPS (n=96) vs hNoPS (n=8801):
  catGRANULE   AUROC 0.726  (AUPRC 0.029)   -- best
  PScore       AUROC 0.689  (AUPRC 0.030)
  FuzDrop*     AUROC 0.689  (AUPRC 0.022)
  PLAAC        AUROC 0.640  (AUPRC 0.029)   -- worst
  (for reference: PdPS-8fea 0.984, PdPS-10fea 0.990)
  catGRANULE significantly beats PLAAC (paired bootstrap, P=0.002); PScore
  significantly beats PLAAC (P=0.978); catGRANULE beats PScore (marginal).

RANKING SUMMARY:
  * Self-assembling (SaPS):  PLAAC ≈ PScore ≈ catGRANULE > FuzDrop(IDR proxy)
  * Partner-dependent (PdPS): catGRANULE > PScore ≈ FuzDrop(IDR proxy) > PLAAC
  * PLAAC is the best detector of PS-Self but the WORST detector of PS-Part.
  * catGRANULE is the most balanced/best detector of PS-Part.
  * All four general predictors underperform the class-specific 8/10-feature
    classifiers (AUROC 0.98–0.99), i.e. they are only moderately good at
    recovering a specific PS class from the human proteome.

*NOTE ON FuzDrop: the provided sequence_prediction_filtered.xlsx contains NO
FuzDrop score column, and the PScore/catGRANULE/PLAAC "_rnk" columns are
entirely empty. Fetching the published FuzDrop tool (PyPI/GitHub) was denied by
the environment and the task forbids reading the source paper. FuzDrop was
therefore evaluated via a transparent, data-derived PROXY: fraction of residues
in intrinsically disordered regions (IDRfrac), which is strongly correlated
with the other predictors (Spearman rho vs PScore = 0.52, vs PLAAC = 0.40,
vs catGRANULE = 0.38) and ranks the groups in the same order (hSaPS > hPdPS >
hNoPS). Its AUROC here reflects IDR content, not the published FuzDrop score,
so published FuzDrop AUCs will differ quantitatively.

LIMITATIONS
-----------
- Composition and (IDR-based) predictor differences are descriptive; small
  positive sets (n=59, 96) mean many single residues are not significant after
  multiple-testing correction, and causality cannot be inferred.
- AUROC is a ranking metric only; at ~1% prevalence the AUPRC (0.02–0.13) shows
  none of these predictors is a deployable high-precision classifier without a
  chosen operating threshold.
- Predictors were evaluated on the same curated positives/background used to
  derive the (class-specific) features, so the 8/10-feature AUCs (0.98–0.99)
  are optimistically biased; no independent validation set exists.
- FuzDrop was not run as published (only the IDR-fraction proxy); a true
  FuzDrop comparison is required for a fully quantitative conclusion.
- The from-scratch DeLong AUC-comparison test produced a degenerate result, so
  all predictor-vs-predictor significance is from a paired bootstrap (500 iters),
  which is valid but less standard than DeLong.

CONCLUSION: PS-Self (self-assembling) and PS-Part (partner-dependent) proteins
are compositionally distinct — self-assemblers are Gly/Pro/Ser/Gln-rich,
disorder-rich and depleted in charged/hydrophobic residues — and this signature
is detectable by general phase-separation predictors, but the best descriptor
is type-dependent: PLAAC for self-assembling, catGRANULE for partner-dependent,
with all four only moderately good against the human non-PS proteome.
da-10-1.notes: The agent performed strong data loading, dataset construction, summarization, and human proteome comparison, but missed key required analyses: fold-change versus NoPS, IDR-based amino-acid ordering, and predictor evaluation on curated SaPS/PdPS vs NoPS sets. Amino-acid composition normalization also used per-protein averages instead of pooled global fractions.

da-10-3.answer:
DA-10-3 — ML Screening of Membraneless Organelle (MLO) Participants
FINAL ANSWER

QUESTION
Evaluate whether PS predictors screen MLO-participant datasets consistently
better than a membrane-bound organelle control, using a fixed non-PS (hNoPS)
background as the negative set.

HEADLINE CONCLUSION
Yes. Predictors screen MLO-participant datasets consistently and
significantly better than the membrane-bound (mitochondrial) control. The
effect is strong for the modern machine-learning classifiers (SaPS/PdPS 8- and
10-feature) and moderate for the classical single-sequence predictors
(catGRANULE, PScore, PLAAC).

METHOD (summary)
- Negative set: the fixed hNoPS background (8,801 human non-PS proteins) from
  h_combined_with_flags.xlsx.
- Positives: membership flags from
  List_of_proteins_for_comparing_MLO_enrichment.xlsx ("Training proteins
  removed" sheet, the unbiased hold-out set that excludes the SaPS/PdPS
  predictor training proteins). 5 MLO datasets (OpenCell nuclear punctae,
  DACT1-particulate proteome, G3BP1 proximity labeling, PhaSepDB
  high-throughput, Amyloid fiber-forming proteins) vs 1 membrane-bound control
  (Proteomics of human mitochondri).
- Scores: PScore, PLAAC, catGRANULE, SaPS-8fea, PdPS-8fea, SaPS-10fea,
  PdPS-10fea from sequence_prediction.xlsx (Homo sapiens rows, 20,375 proteins).
- Metric: ROC AUC separating each dataset's positives from the hNoPS
  background (threshold-free, robust to imbalance). Direction validated by AUC
  of each predictor vs hNoPS on the labelled hSaPS/hPdPS classes (all AUC > 0.5;
  SaPS-8fea 0.987, SaPS-10fea 0.990, PdPS-8fea 0.984, PdPS-10fea 0.990 on their
  own classes), confirming higher score = more PS-like.

KEY RESULTS
1) Per-dataset AUC (7 predictors x 5 MLO datasets = 35 cells):
   30/35 MLO cells (85.7%) exceed the corresponding membrane-control AUC;
   25/35 (71.4%) exceed 0.5 (better than random).
2) Per-predictor MLO-mean minus membrane AUC:
   PScore +0.054, PLAAC +0.015, catGRANULE +0.088, SaPS-8fea +0.143,
   PdPS-8fea +0.166, SaPS-10fea +0.217, PdPS-10fea +0.199.
   The SaPS/PdPS 8- and 10-feature classifiers beat the membrane control on
   ALL 5 MLO datasets each (5/5); PScore and catGRANULE beat it on 4/5; PLAAC on 3/5.
3) Pooled MLO (2,799 positives) vs pooled membrane (1,121 positives),
   overlap-excluded: deltaAUC (MLO - membrane) positive for all 7 predictors
   with bootstrap 95% CI excluding 0 in every case:
   PScore +0.083 [0.058, 0.111], PLAAC +0.044 [0.018, 0.071],
   catGRANULE +0.121 [0.096, 0.147], SaPS-8fea +0.167 [0.142, 0.192],
   PdPS-8fea +0.181 [0.154, 0.208], SaPS-10fea +0.172 [0.145, 0.200],
   PdPS-10fea +0.180 [0.155, 0.206].
4) Significance (7 paired predictors): Wilcoxon signed-rank W=28.0, p=0.0078;
   one-sample t-test p=0.0023. Pooled: Wilcoxon p=0.0078, t-test p=2.9e-4.

REPRESENTATIVE MLO PARTICIPANTS (scored above background)
OpenCell nuclear punctae: BRD2 (P25440), MED14 (O60244), MED17 (Q9NVC6).
G3BP1 proximity labeling (stress granules): NESTIN (P48681, SaPS-10fea 0.903),
ENPL (P14625, SaPS-10fea 0.841).
Amyloid fiber-forming: ODAM (A1E959), GLUCAGON (P01275, SaPS-10fea 0.701).

BIOLOGICAL INTERPRETATION
Phase separation is a real, detectable biophysical property, and it is enriched
among membraneless-organelle participants relative to a stably membrane-bound
organelle (mitochondrion). MLO proteomes (nuclear punctae, stress granules,
amyloid/PS condensates, PhaSepDB high-throughput) are enriched for proteins with
intrinsically disordered regions and prion-like domains that drive
liquid-liquid phase separation, whereas the mitochondrial proteome is dominated
by folded, membrane-embedded and globular enzymes with little phase-separating
propensity. The fact that the self/partner classifiers (SaPS/PdPS) discriminate
MLO sets best, and that PdPS (partner-dependent) classifiers score highest on
G3BP1 stress-granule and DACT1 sets, is consistent with these MLO proteomes
containing proteins that assemble either by themselves (SaPS) or via RNA/partner
interactions (PdPS) - exactly the mechanistic axis these predictors were built to
capture.

LIMITATIONS
- Correlational screening only; AUC does not establish mechanism or that MLO
  function depends on phase separation.
- All AUCs are relative to the single fixed hNoPS background; absolute values
  would change with a different negative set (none available in the files).
- Positive sets are small and imbalanced (62 Amyloid to 2,415 PhaSepDB vs ~8,800
  negatives); the Amyloid set is the only MLO dataset near random for some
  predictors (catGRANULE 0.471, SaPS-8fea 0.461).
- Only one membrane organelle (mitochondrion) is used as control; results may not
  generalise to all membrane-bound organelles.
- Dataset-level replication is low (5 MLO vs 1 membrane), so the dataset-level
  permutation test is underpowered (p=0.166); the significant results come from
  the paired per-predictor tests and the pooled protein-level comparison.
- PhaSepDB AUC is computed on 1,712 of 2,415 positives (those with a human score).
- PScore/DeepPhase have substantial missing values; the classic-predictor *_rnk
  columns in the source file are empty, so ranks could not be used.

CONCLUSION: The predictors perform consistently better on MLO-participant
datasets than on the membrane-bound organelle control. The most consistent and
largest advantages come from the SaPS-10fea / PdPS-10fea predictions
(deltaAUC ~ +0.17 to +0.22; 5/5 MLO datasets beat the control for each).
da-10-3.notes: The agent performed a rigorous and complete analysis, correctly handling inputs, labels, missing data, AUC computation, group comparisons, and source grounding, with all conclusions supported by the computed evidence.

da-11-1.answer:
KIR+CD8+ T CELLS AND PATHOGENIC CD4+ T CELLS IN CELIAC DISEASE (GSE193442)
=========================================================================
Task DA-11-1 — top signaling pathways, beyond MHC-I, predicted to mediate the
suppressive function and cytotoxic targeting of KIR+CD8+ T cells against
gliadin-specific CD4+ T cells.

SUMMARY OF WHAT THE DATA SHOW
-----------------------------
Single-cell RNA-seq of 6 active-celiac-disease mucosal biopsies and 4 healthy
controls (10 samples, 72,177 cells; 67,286 cells x 18,632 genes after QC).
Leiden clustering recovered intestinal T/NK/myeloid-like cell states. A distinct
KIR+CD8+ cytotoxic T-cell population was identified (CD8A/CD8B+, KIR3DL1/KIR2DL1/
KIR2DL3+, GZMB/PRF1/GNLY/CCL5/NKG7-high).

KEY NUMBERS
----------- 
- KIR+CD8+ T cells: 392/41,144 = 0.95% of cells in active CeD vs 3/26,142 =
  0.01% in healthy controls  -> ~95-fold enrichment in disease.
- CellChat (CellChatDB.human) confirmed MHC-I as the dominant, "established"
  interaction for KIR+CD8+ T cells (summed communication probability 1.96e-2,
  >> 20x the next pathway; driven by HLA-A/B/C/E/F -> CD8A/CD8B and the
  allele-specific HLA-A/HLA-F -> KIR3DL1, HLA-E -> CD94:NKG2E/C axes).

TOP SIGNALING PATHWAYS BEYOND MHC-I
-----------------------------------
Ranked by CellChat interaction probability for KIR+CD8+ T-cell-involved
communication (CeD), and, in the specific KIR+CD8+ T -> CD4+ T direction:

  KIR+CD8 T -> CD4 T (suppressive / cytotoxic-targeting direction; all p<0.05,
  significance-filtered by CellChat):
   1. CD99  (CD99-CD99 homophilic cell-cell contact)      prob 4.49e-5, p<0.05
   2. SELPLG (PSGL-1 - L-selectin/SELL adhesion)          prob 2.56e-5, p<0.05
   3. CypA  (PPIA/cyclophilin A - BSG/CD147/EMMPRIN)      prob 1.35e-5, p<0.05
   4. MHC-II (HLA-DPB1/HLA-DPA1 - CD4)                    prob 2.0e-6 / 1.9e-6, p<0.05
   5. IL16  (IL16-CD4)                                    prob 6.86e-7, p<0.05
