da-19-3.answer:
QUESTION: To map RUNX1 genomic targets that mediate AI-10-49 therapeutic effects, how does RUNX1 chromatin occupancy change upon CBFbeta-SMMHC inhibition?

SHORT ANSWER: RUNX1 chromatin occupancy expands dramatically and genome-wide in human inv(16) ME-1 AML cells treated with the CBFbeta-SMMHC inhibitor AI-10-49, driven overwhelmingly by newly GAINED RUNX1 binding sites (including at the MYC promoter), not by loss of binding. Thus CBFbeta-SMMHC inhibition recruits/restores RUNX1 onto active chromatin across many targets, and specifically onto the MYC promoter.

QUANTITATIVE FINDINGS (RUNX1 ChIP-seq, DMSO vs AI-10-49, MACS2 peaks):

1) Peak-count expansion:
   - RUNX1 DMSO: 1,329 peaks.
   - RUNX1 AI-10-49: 9,169 peaks.
   - ~6.9x more RUNX1-bound regions; occupied genome rises from 0.33 Mb to 3.18 Mb (~9.6x).

2) Unified differential regions (DMSO ∪ AI, merged non-overlapping; n=9,266):
   - Gained (AI only): 7,950 (85.8%).
   - Shared (bound in both): 1,219 (13.2%).
   - Lost (DMSO only): 97 (1.0%).
   => The change is a GAIN / redistribution, not a loss of RUNX1 occupancy.

3) Occupancy signal (sum of MACS2 signalValue):
   - DMSO total 7,730 -> AI total 81,896 (a 10.6x increase).
   - Mean peak signal per bound region: DMSO 5.87 -> AI 8.93.
   - At the 1,219 loci bound in BOTH conditions, RUNX1 signal is significantly increased (paired Wilcoxon signed-rank W=11,295, p=5.1e-189; mean AI/DMSO signal ratio 2.64x).

4) Where the new binding occurs:
   - 48.5% of gained RUNX1 regions fall at promoters (<=2 kb of a TSS); 17.0% proximal (2-10 kb); 31.9% distal (10-100 kb).
   - 91.4% of gained RUNX1 regions overlap an active H3K27ac-marked peak (mean H3K27ac signal DMSO 16.1 -> AI 13.7), i.e. RUNX1 is recruited to an already-active regulatory landscape.

5) RUNX1 target genes whose occupancy changes (strongest gains, protein-coding, newly bound with no DMSO peak; log2fc from signalValue):
   - ZBTB16 (PLZF): DMSO 0 -> AI 93.1 (8 regions), log2fc +6.56.
   - FOSL2: 0 -> 76.1 (4), +6.27.
   - KLF13: 0 -> 66.7 (6), +6.08.
   - SGK1: 0 -> 53.8 (4), +5.78.
   - BCL2: 0 -> 42.7 (6), +5.45.
   - BCL2L1: 0 -> 20.7 (2), +4.44.
   - MCL1: 0 -> 7.4 (1), +3.08.
   - ERG: 0 -> 40.0 (5), +5.36.
   - MEF2C: 0 -> 30.2 (2), +4.96.
   - MYC: 0 -> 4.1 (1), +2.35.
   - MYB: 0 -> 10.3 (1), +3.50.
   - GATA2, TAL1, SMAD7, FOS, HIF1A, VEGFA, NFKB1/RELA, ETS2 also newly gain RUNX1 occupancy.
   Genes already bound and intensified: RUNX1 itself (23.6 -> 163.0, +2.74), CBFA2T3 (+2.82), RUNX3 (+2.30), ETV6 (+2.77), SMAD7 (+3.68).

6) Mechanistically most direct finding - MYC:
   - In DMSO, NO RUNX1 peak is detected within ~40 kb of MYC (chr8:128,748,694, hg19, +strand).
   - With AI-10-49, a RUNX1 peak appears at chr8:128,747,329-128,747,624 (signalValue 4.11, -log10q 5.92), only 350 bp upstream of the MYC TSS.
   - The MYC promoter is H3K27ac-marked (active) in BOTH conditions (peak chr8:128,746,429-128,752,167, signalValue 15.06, -log10q 178 in DMSO; chr8:128,746,568-128,751,919, signalValue 15.27, -log10q 77 in AI-10-49).
   => Approximately 7,000 genes (6,082 protein-coding) newly gain RUNX1 binding, and MYC specifically gains a new promoter-proximal RUNX1 site, providing a chromatin-level basis for the drug's disruption of MYC regulation.

BIOLOGICAL INTERPRETATION: The CBFbeta-SMMHC fusion (inv(16), core-binding-factor AML) sequesters/alters RUNX1. Inhibiting the fusion with AI-10-49 releases RUNX1 and it re-occupies many active (H3K27ac+) promoters and enhancers, increasing RUNX1 occupancy genome-wide and specifically at the MYC promoter. This is consistent with the therapeutic disruption of MYC chromatin dynamics and the observed apoptosis phenotype, with the strong gains at anti-apoptotic (BCL2/BCL2L1/MCL1), stress-response (FOSL2, SGK1, ZBTB16/PLZF), and blood/lineage (ERG, MEF2C, GATA2, TAL1, MYB) genes.

LIMITATIONS: Only MACS2 narrowPeak files (no read-depth/FE bigwig or BAM counts) were provided, so signal was compared using the signalValue enrichment metric rather than normalized coverage; each condition has only one ChIP-seq replicate (no replicate-based differential binding, e.g. DiffBind/DESeq2); and no RNA-seq expression or ATAC-seq peak files were present, so the direct link from RUNX1 occupancy to gene-expression change and to chromatin accessibility change cannot be established from these data alone. Peak-to-gene mapping for distal peaks uses the nearest-TSS as a fallback, so distal assignments are approximate (the MYC assignment was verified directly against the GENCODE transcription record).
da-19-3.notes: The agent strongly performed RUNX1 data extraction, differential peak computation, and quantitative reporting, but the genomic feature enrichment analysis did not meet the full four-class precedence and statistical testing requirements, and source reliability has a minor citation weakness.

       (binomial test down vs up, n = 62,899: p < 1e-300).
   - log2FC distribution: mean -0.27, median -0.26.
   - 3,829 peaks with log2FC <= -1; 406 with log2FC <= -1.5; 40 with log2FC <= -2.

3) OTHER LEUKEMIA-/HEMATOPOIESIS-RELEVANT REGIONS WITH REDUCED H3K27ac (summed log2FC):
   GATA3 (-1.74), MN1 (-1.72), PBX3 (-1.74), HOXA9 (-1.30), BMI1 (-1.00),
   MLLT3 (-0.78), KIT (-0.67), FLT3 (-0.63), LMO2 (-0.47), ETV6 (-0.49),
   SPI1 (-0.35).
   Notable representative peaks (DMSO -> AI reads, log2FC):
     GATA3 chr10:8,095,535-8,099,347 (726->181, -1.86)
     MN1   chr22:28,196,598-28,198,695 (1049->239, -2.03)
     HOXA9 chr7:27,210,522-27,214,396 (2065->850, -1.30)
     KIT   chr4:55,524,034-55,528,514 (1422->743, -0.96)

4) RUNX1-ASSOCIATED REDUCED ENHANCERS (CBFβ-SMMHC/RUNX1 axis):
   417 distal enhancers showing reduced H3K27ac (log2FC < -0.5) are also bound by
   RUNX1 in DMSO. The MYC enhancer chr8:128,928,731-128,931,071 is one of these,
   tying the H3K27ac loss directly to RUNX1/CBFβ-SMMHC occupancy.

INTERPRETATION:
AI-10-49 disrupts CBFβ-SMMHC/RUNX1-dependent enhancer activity, producing a global
loss of H3K27ac and a marked loss at MYC and its RUNX1-bound distal enhancer. This is
consistent with loss of the RUNX1-driven MYC enhancer network that maintains leukemia,
supporting MYC chromatin disruption as the therapeutic mechanism.

LIMITATIONS:
- Only single H3K27ac DMSO and AI-10-49 samples were available (no replicates), so
  no per-peak statistical FDR was computed; results are based on library-size-normalized
  log2 fold-changes plus a genome-wide asymmetry (binomial) test.
- Peak-to-gene assignment used nearest TSS (no HiChIP/3C data), so enhancer-target
  connectivity is approximate.
- RUNX1, ATAC-seq and RNA-seq were only available as narrowPeak calls or not at all,
  so they support co-localization but not differential read-counting or expression
  confirmation.
da-19-4.notes: The analysis correctly handled input/condition mapping and differential quantification, but it failed to address the required ME1/ME2/BDME anchor definition and decline calls, and lacked per-region statistical significance testing, so it does not meet the full task.

da-19-6.answer:
YES — AI-10-49 treatment leads to a global change in chromatin accessibility, and the dominant effect is a global DECREASE / contraction of open chromatin in ME-1 inv(16) AML cells, not an increase and not "no change."

Evidence from the ATAC-seq data (MACS2 peak calls; DMSO = GSM2715541/42, AI-10-49 = GSM2715543/44):

1. Fewer peaks despite deeper sequencing. Per-sample MACS2 peak counts: DMSO rep1 = 67,066, rep2 = 64,929; AI-10-49 rep1 = 48,706, rep2 = 53,141. Yet the AI-10-49 libraries were sequenced ~1.7x deeper: mean ~4.27 million fragments (4.14M, 4.40M) vs DMSO ~2.49M (2.52M, 2.46M). Deeper sequencing produced fewer peaks.

2. Library-normalised peak yield falls ~55%. DMSO yields a mean ~26,528 peaks per million fragments vs AI-10-49 ~11,931 (ratio 0.450). Genome-wide accessible span normalised to library size also shrinks (~0.31% -> ~0.28% of the genome).

3. Significant, asymmetric repertoire reorganisation. A pooled universe of 103,177 accessible regions is: 28,787 shared (27.9%), 11,817 lost/DMSO-only (11.5%), 7,935 gained/AI-only (7.7%), 54,638 reproducible in neither replicate (53.0%). Fisher exact test odds ratio = 16.77, p < 1e-300. Net change = 7,935 gained - 11,817 lost = -3,882 regions (losses exceed gains ~1.5x).

4. The surviving accessible sites are stronger and wider. AI-10-49 median peak width = 118 bp vs 103 bp (Mann-Whitney p < 1e-300); median fold-enrichment signal = 6.80 vs 5.32 (p < 1e-300). On matched shared regions, AI-10-49 signal exceeds DMSO in 70.7% of loci (Wilcoxon p < 1e-300).

5. Preferentially the weaker/peripheral sites close. Regions lost in AI-10-49 have a DMSO median signal of 4.72, significantly below the 7.76 of stably-shared DMSO regions (p < 1e-300); newly gained regions are likewise weaker (AI median 5.90) than stable sites (8.87).

Interpretation: CBFβ-SMMHC inhibition by AI-10-49 disrupts the leukemogenic chromatin program, causing a global retraction of the accessible (nucleosome-free) landscape toward a smaller core of high-signal sites, with a net loss of open-chromatin regions. This is a directional, net-loss reorganisation rather than a balanced remodelling or a uniform increase.

Limitations: Only ATAC-seq peak-call outputs are present (no BAM/bigwig, and no RNA-seq or ChIP-seq H3K27ac/RUNX1 count or peak matrices), so I cannot link the accessibility changes to gene expression, H3K27ac, or RUNX1 binding, confirm whether the regions are MYC-proximal/RUNX1-bound, or assign them to promoters vs enhancers. With n=2 replicates per condition, "robust" calls rely on both-replicate agreement and I cannot run a variance-based differential accessibility test; a batch/tagmentation difference between conditions cannot be excluded. The ~55% yield difference and net-loss asymmetry are nonetheless robust across the overlap thresholds tested.
da-19-6.notes: The agent performed a thorough analysis of ATAC-seq peak calls with correct sample assignment and a defensible peak-level comparison. However, it fell short of a fully rigorous region-level accessibility quantification workflow by not computing per-sample read coverage or log2 fold-changes, instead relying on peak overlap and signal metrics. All other criteria, including directional counts, global conclusion, biological interpretation, limitations, and source reliability, were met at the highest level.

da-20-1.answer:
BiomniBench-DA Task DA-20-1: Baseline transcriptional signatures of four primary human cell types
==================================================================================================

Short answer: The four primary cell types have DISTINCT (non-overlapping) baseline transcriptional signatures, not overlapping ones. Fibroblasts and skeletal-muscle myoblasts are the most similar pair; melanocytes are the most distinct/isolation cell type.

EVIDENCE (bulk 3'-end RNA-seq of 192 DMSO baseline samples, 48 per cell type; 18,422 protein-coding/expressed genes after QC):

1) CELL TYPES ARE CLEARLY SEPARABLE (distinct):
   - Silhouette score = 0.755 in gene-z-scored log-CPM PCA space (PC1-10); label-permutation null mean = -0.050, permuted p = 0.002. Separation is far beyond chance.
   - The separation survives batch control: within the single low-saturation batch (B_lo) silhouette = 0.769; within the high-saturation batch (B_hi) silhouette = 0.743.
   - Canonical identity markers are essentially cell-type exclusive (mean log-CPM):
       Melanocytes (MEL):  TYR 6.85, TYRP1 8.85, DCT 6.65, PMEL 8.56, MLANA 9.16, S100B 7.41, MITF 5.47, GPR143 4.98, OCA2 4.20  (vs <= 0.4 in the other three cell types).
       Myoblasts (SkMM):    MYOD1 0.51, MYF5 1.60, DES 1.71  (expressed only in SkMM; 0 elsewhere).
       Fibroblasts (FB):    COL6A1 7.15, COL6A3 5.44, DCN 8.20, LUM 4.80  (highest in FB).
       AoSMC smooth muscle: TAGLN 3.35, CNN1 0.91, MYH11 0.07  (highest in AoSMC/mesenchyme).
   - Data-driven "exclusive" genes confirmed this: MEL = TYR, SOX10, LINC00518, DCT; FB = OLFML1, DPT; AoSMC = CSF2RB, PI16; SkMM = FHL5, GATA3, ASB5.

2) MOST SIMILAR PAIR = FIBROBLASTS and SKELETAL-MUSCLE MYOBLASTS (FB-SkMM), consistent across 4 independent metrics:
   - Fewest differentially expressed genes (|log2FC|>=1, FDR<0.05): FB-SkMM = 3,172 (vs AoSMC-SkMM 3,379, AoSMC-FB 3,801, FB-MEL 4,132, AoSMC-MEL 4,266, MEL-SkMM 4,431). Smallest all-gene mean|log2FC|: FB-SkMM = 0.576.
   - Highest expression-profile correlation (top 3,000 variable genes): FB-SkMM = 0.667 (0.672 within one batch).
   - Hierarchical clustering (avg linkage, correlation distance) merges FB and SkMM last (closest), splits MEL off first: leaf order [MEL, AoSMC, FB, SkMM].
   - Mean correlation to the other three: MEL = 0.35 (lowest, most isolated), FB = 0.54, SkMM = 0.54, AoSMC = 0.48.

Overall similarity ordering (most -> least similar):  FB-SkMM > AoSMC-SkMM ~ AoSMC-FB > FB-MEL > AoSMC-MEL ~ MEL-SkMM.

BIOLOGICAL INTERPRETATION
AoSMC, dermal fibroblasts and skeletal-muscle myoblasts are all mesoderm-derived, mesenchymal(-like) cells that share extracellular-matrix and contractile programs, while melanocytes are neural-crest-derived and are defined by a wholly different (pigmentation) program (TYR/TYRP1/DCT/PMEL/MLANA/MITF/SOX10). This explains both the clear separation of all four cell types and why the three mesenchyme-derived types cluster closer together, with fibroblasts and myoblasts most alike and melanocytes most isolated. For platform validation, the assay faithfully resolves the four primary cells into biologically coherent, well-separated groups (centroid separation ratios 5.4-6.5x within-type spread).

LIMITATION / CONFOUND (important)
The DMSO baselines split into two sequencing-QC batches that are confounded with cell type: all AoSMC and melanocytes are in a low-saturation batch (B_lo), while most fibroblasts and myoblasts are in a high-saturation batch (B_hi). PC1 correlates r = +0.80 with sequencing saturation and r = +0.55 with %rRNA removed. When these QC covariates are regressed out, the silhouette falls to 0.137. The separation, marker-gene exclusivity, and the FB-SkMM similarity all still hold within-batch and via marker genes, confirming the biological signal; but the ABSOLUTE separation magnitude is partially inflated by the batch confound, and the melanocyte-vs-others distance cannot be cleanly separated from melanocytes happening to be in the low-saturation batch. A fully crossed/batched design would be needed for unbiased absolute distances.

Scope: This analyses only the DMSO control (baseline) state at 24 h; it does not assess compound effects or single-cell heterogeneity. Results are computed from the provided data only; no source paper, figures, or supplementary material were consulted.
da-20-1.notes: The agent correctly isolated the 192 DMSO baseline samples, applied reasonable normalization and QC, and provided thorough biological interpretation with proper references, but failed to implement the required K-means clustering and TruncatedSVD pipeline, and identified FB-SkMM rather than AoSMC-SkMM as the most similar pair.

da-20-3.answer:
Brefeldin-A (BFA) acts as a secretory-pathway (ER-to-Golgi) disruptor. Consistent with this mechanism, across the four primary human cell types (aortic smooth muscle cells, dermal fibroblasts, melanocytes, and skeletal muscle myoblasts) and the six-dose series (9.5-3000 nM), BFA reproducibly SUPPRESSES a large, coherent set of MSigDB Hallmark pathways that are dominated by secreted/extracellular-matrix cargo genes, while reciprocally INDUCING the ER-stress / Unfolded-Protein-Response program.

Hallmark pathways SUPPRESSED by BFA across cell types (negative enrichment score, NES); mean NES is the average across the four cell types (each dose-averaged). All are negative in all four cell types and significantly suppressed (FDR<0.25, NES<0) in the large majority of the 24 cell-type x-dose runs (~15-23 of 24), including at the strict FDR<0.05 level:

  - Epithelial Mesenchymal Transition  (mean NES -2.24; strongest)
  - UV Response Dn                      (-1.96)
  - Apoptosis                           (-1.95)
  - Apical Junction                     (-1.92)
  - Angiogenesis                        (-1.89)
  - TGF-beta Signaling                  (-1.89)
  - Coagulation                         (-1.88)
  - KRAS Signaling Up                   (-1.85)
  - Apical Surface                      (-1.82)
  - TNF-alpha Signaling via NF-kB       (-1.79)
  - IL-2/STAT5 Signaling                (-1.68)
  - IL-6/JAK/STAT3 Signaling            (-1.67)
  - Inflammatory Response               (-1.65)
  - Interferon Gamma Response           (-1.62)
  - Hypoxia                             (-1.59)
  - Complement                          (-1.58)
  - Notch Signaling                     (-1.53)
  - Allograft Rejection                 (-1.53)
  - Hedgehog Signaling                  (-1.49)
  - Myogenesis                          (-1.41)
  - Wnt-beta Catenin Signaling          (-1.39)
  - Estrogen Response Early             (-1.35)
  - Mitotic Spindle                     (-1.34)
  - Glycolysis                          (-1.32)
  - G2-M Checkpoint                     (-1.31)
  - p53 Pathway                         (-1.24)
  - Xenobiotic Metabolism               (-1.24)
  - Estrogen Response Late              (-1.22)
  (weaker, still negative across most/all cell types: Reactive Oxygen Species Pathway, Androgen Response,
   KRAS Signaling Dn, E2F Targets, Interferon Alpha Response, Fatty Acid Metabolism)

Overall ~30 of 50 Hallmark pathways are suppressed (negative NES) with the signal robust to the ranking metric (Wald statistic, log2FC, or signed p-value all give the same leading suppressed sets).

Mechanistic reading (why this confirms BFA is a secretory disruptor):
  1. The suppressed transcriptome is exactly the secretory cargo: GO cellular-component enrichment of the 483 leading-edge genes is dominated by extracellular matrix (p=5.5e-38), endoplasmic-reticulum lumen (p=5.8e-22), secretory granule lumen (p=5.2e-09), and Golgi membrane/lumen (p=1.1e-07 / 3.5e-07). Canonical secreted/ECM genes are dose-dependently down-regulated (e.g. COL1A1, COL3A1, FBN1, SERPINE1, TIMP1, VIM, TAGLN all reach log2FC about -1 to -3 at >=95 nM), accompanied by the corresponding signalling modules (TGF-beta, EMT, coagulation, complement, angiogenesis, inflammation, cytokine/chemokine).
  2. Reciprocally, BFA strongly INDUCES the Unfolded Protein Response / ER-stress program (mean NES +2.29, FDR<0.05 in ~23/24 runs) as well as mTORC1 signaling (+1.91). UPR markers are massively up-regulated (HSPA5/GRP78, HSP90B1/GRP94, HERPUD1, DNAJB9, DDIT3/CHOP, CHAC1, ATF3, ATF4, ATF6, SEC61A1), the expected consequence of blocking ER-to-Golgi export and accumulating misfolded/unsecreted protein in the ER.
  3. The signature is BFA-specific: the unrelated positive controls Dexamethasone (glucocorticoid receptor agonist) and Trichostatin A (HDAC inhibitor) do NOT suppress this secreted/ECM/EMT-inflammatory module (their mean NES on these pathways is near zero or positive) and neither induces the UPR. Dexamethasone only weakly hits Cholesterol Homeostasis/Apical Junction/G2-M/E2F; Trichostatin A instead suppresses cell-cycle sets (G2-M, E2F, Myc Targets V1, Mitotic Spindle).
  4. The response is dose-dependent: essentially flat at 9.5 nM, switching on sharply by 28.5-95 nM and saturating by 300-3000 nM, with large programs in BOTH directions (thousands of genes up and down) - ruling out a non-specific global repression.

Limitations: these data are mRNA-level DESeq2 contrasts, so they are consistent with - but do not directly visualize - a block in protein secretion/trafficking. The magnitude of suppression differs by cell type (strongest in aortic smooth muscle cells, weakest in melanocytes), and the literal "Protein Secretion" Hallmark set is itself only weakly induced (mean NES +0.90) because it contains trafficking/sorting machinery rather than the depleted secreted cargo.

Headline answer: BFA suppresses Epithelial Mesenchymal Transition, Angiogenesis, TGF-beta Signaling, Coagulation, Apoptosis, Complement, Inflammatory Response, TNF-alpha/NF-kB, IL-6/JAK-STAT3, IL-2/STAT5, Hypoxia, Glycolysis, the ECM/secreted-cargo programs, and many other Hallmark pathways across all four cell types, while inducing the Unfolded Protein Response and mTORC1 signaling - together confirming BFA's mechanism as a secretory-pathway (ER-to-Golgi) disruptor.
da-20-3.notes: The agent performed a comprehensive and well-documented GSEA analysis, but used a non-standard ranking metric and did not provide the exact per-condition quantitative validation details for the three target pathways as required by the rubric.

da-20-4.answer:
QUESTION: To inform tissue-specific safety and efficacy assessments, does dabrafenib show consistent or divergent transcriptional responses across the four primary cell types (AoSMCs, skeletal muscle myoblasts, dermal fibroblasts, melanocytes)?

ANSWER: Dabrafenib produces a CONSISTENT PHARMACODYNAMIC CORE with PARTIAL, DOSE- AND CELL-TYPE-SPECIFIC DIVERGENCE. The response is consistent in direction at the pathway level across all four cell types, but it is only moderately correlated at the full-transcriptome level, and melanocytes diverge the most — including a qualitative divergence at the highest dose.

WHAT IS CONSISTENT (shared across all four primary cell types):
- All four cell types respond to dabrafenib in a dose-dependent manner (thousands of differentially expressed genes, FDR<0.05; e.g. AoSMC 9,733 at 300 nM; melanocytes 9,439 at 3000 nM; dermal fibroblasts 8,959 at 3000 nM; myoblasts 5,203 at 3000 nM).
- At the pathway level the direction is concordant: cell-cycle/proliferation programs are SUPPRESSED in all four (Hallmark E2F_TARGETS NES ~ -1.7 to -3.6; G2M_CHECKPOINT; MITOTIC_SPINDLE), and the integrated-stress-response / ATF4-UPR program is INDUCED in all four (UNFOLDED_PROTEIN_RESPONSE NES +1.6 to +2.7). This is a shared cytostatic + stress-response signature.
- There is a reproducible set of consistently-regulated genes (398 genes at 300 nM, 1,060 at 3000 nM) that are direction-concordant in all four cells (same direction 71-85% of the time). Up in all four: PSAT1, TRIB3, ATF5, NNMT, MTHFD2, SLC7A5, SLC7A11, PCK2, DDIT3, SOD2 (ATF4/one-carbon/antioxidant program). Down in all four: RRM2, CDC20, UBE2C, CDK1, PLK1, MYBL2, CCND1 (cell-cycle/E2F/G2M program).
- The on-target MAPK/BRAF-feedback signature (DUSP6, DUSP4, ETV4/5, SPRY2/4, EGR1, JUNB, FOS) is induced in all four cell types at low-to-mid dose, strongest in fibroblasts and myoblasts.

WHAT IS DIVERGENT (cell-type-specific, and largest for melanocytes):
- The full-transcriptome response is only MODERATELY correlated across cell types. Mean pairwise Pearson r = 0.29 (300 nM) and 0.32 (3000 nM); Spearman rho = 0.21-0.29. This is far above chance (permutation null r ~ 0.000, p<0.005) but far from identical. DE-gene set overlap is low (mean pairwise Jaccard ~ 0.19-0.28). Note: the four cell types are themselves hugely distinct at baseline (14-16k DE genes between any pair), so a "moderate" drug correlation actually sits on top of large lineage differences.
- Melanocytes are the strongest outlier:
  1. At 3000 nM they are the "odd one out": 1,384 genes (6.4%) are opposite in sign to the other three cell types, vs. 335-832 (1.6-3.9%) for AoSMC/SkMM/dermal fibroblasts. 83% of this divergence is melanocytes DOWN-regulating genes that go UP elsewhere, including lineage/pigmentation-related transcripts (MC1R, RASGRP3, SEMA3E, CD36, FABP3).
  2. Melanocytes are the least correlated with the other three cell types at every dose (e.g. at 3000 nM: melanocyte-dermal fibroblast r=0.14, melanocyte-myoblast r=0.20, vs. dermal fibroblast-myoblast r=0.47).
  3. Melanocytes are least self-consistent across dose (r=0.38 between their own 300 and 3000 nM responses, vs. 0.60-0.60 for the other three).
  4. At 3000 nM melanocytes show a QUALITATIVE pathway switch not seen elsewhere: MYC_TARGETS (NES +2.76), OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION (+2.51), MTORC1 (+2.44) and UPR (+2.72) all strongly UP (FDR<0.001), while their cell-cycle suppression recedes (E2F_TARGETS -1.66 vs -2.5 to -3.6 elsewhere). The other three cell types never up-regulate MYC or oxidative-phosphorylation programs at any dose.
  5. Notable: the shared ISR genes GDF15, CHAC1, SESN2 are strongly up in AoSMC/dermal fibroblasts/myoblasts but only weakly (non-significant) in melanocytes at 3000 nM.

CLINICAL INTERPRETATION FOR SAFETY/EFFICACY:
- Consistent part: the shared cell-cycle-arrest + ATF4/ISR + MAPK-feedback core suggests dabrafenib's transcriptional pharmacodynamic effect is largely conserved across tissues, supporting a common on-target/cytostatic mode of action. In an efficacy context, a compound that triggers a similar mechanism in multiple primary tissues has some trans-tissue predictability for its primary transcriptional effect.
- Divergent part: the amplitude and composition of the response are cell-type-specific, and melanocytes are qualitatively different at the highest dose (MYC/OXPHOS/mTORC1/UPR up with receding cell-cycle suppression). This means a single tissue's transcriptional signature is only partially transferable to other tissues, and the melanocyte stress/metabolic response at high dose is a specific, tissue-restricted behavior relevant to tissue-specific safety/tolerability assessment.

LIMITATIONS (why this must be viewed cautiously):
- Single 24 h timepoint (no kinetics).
- Bulk 3'-end RNA-seq (Drug-seq/GDPx2) at n_mapped-UMI resolution; no single-cell resolution; 3'-end bias.
- No mutation/BRAF/NRAS status and no protein/phospho or viability measurements, so "on-target inhibition vs. paradoxical MAPK activation" and actual cytotoxicity cannot be directly established. As primary (likely wild-type BRAF) cells, dabrafenib may act partly via paradoxical RAF activation rather than simple on-target inhibition.
- Negative controls are all at 0.0625% DMSO while dabrafenib doses are at 0.0625/0.1875/0.625% DMSO; the design is plate-blocked/vehicle-tier-matched, but a residual vehicle effect at the highest dose cannot be fully excluded and specifically affects the high-dose (3000 nM) results.
- Outlier removal (90/960 samples, 9.4%) used the cohort's voom+IQR rule; results were directionally robust but should be confirmed with an independent method.

BOTTOM LINE: Consistent at the level of the shared pathway/program (cell-cycle suppression + ISR/ATF4 activation + MAPK-feedback, present in all four cell types), but DIVERGENT in amplitude and in the specifics — with melanocytes showing the greatest divergence, including a qualitative high-dose switch (MYC/OXPHOS/mTORC1/UPR) and melanocyte-specific down-regulation of lineage/pigmentation-associated genes.
da-20-4.notes: The agent performed a robust differential expression and GSEA analysis but did not follow the specific required protocol (DESeq2/apeglm, volume-matched DMSO) and omitted interpretation of the three target Hallmark pathways (KRAS, EMT, MYOGENESIS), resulting in lower scores on core pathway interpretation criteria.

da-24-3.answer:
TASK DA-24-3 — Shared genetic factors among neonatal metabolites

QUESTION
Use the GWAS summary data to find shared genetic factors among different metabolites.

ANSWER (summary of findings)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
I analysed the discovery and replication GWAS summary statistics (20,474 SNPs
x 13 metabolites/ratios, identical SNP panel for every trait) plus the per-sample
metabolite abundance matrix (8,737 samples x 74 metabolites/ratios). Using the
genome-wide significance threshold p < 5e-8, I found 592 significant SNP-trait
pairs forming 11 independent loci across 12 of the 13 traits (ORN/CIT has none).
The key result is that shared (pleiotropic) genetic factors are CONCENTRATED and
STRUCTURED, not diffuse — they map to a handful of canonical metabolism genes.

1) THE MAIN SHARED GENETIC FACTOR = the ACADM locus on chr1p31.1 (75.6-76.0 Mb).
   It is genome-wide significant for FOUR traits simultaneously:
     C6 (medium-chain acylcarnitine), C8, C8/C2, and the ratio (C3DC+C4-OH)/C10.
   Exact-SNP sharing (hypergeometric test, M=20,474 SNPs):
     - C6 & C8:     51/54 shared SNPs (p = 5.5e-150), effect directions 100% concordant
     - C8 & C8/C2:  51/51 shared SNPs (p = 2.2e-154)
     - C6 & C8/C2:  51/54 shared SNPs (p = 5.5e-150)
     - ratio & C6/C8/C8/C2: ~51 shared SNPs (p = 1.5e-119 to 3.2e-120), directions 100% OPPOSITE
   The shared lead SNP chr1:75727547:A:G DECREASES C6 (beta=-0.0019, p=2.9e-13),
   C8 (-0.0027, p=2.1e-10) and C8/C2 (-0.00017, p=6.3e-10) while INCREASING the
   ratio (+0.084, p=2.5e-11) — reproduced in replication (C6 p=1.9e-13, C8 p=8.9e-17,
   C8/C2 p=2.4e-19, ratio p=4.0e-12). ACADM is medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase,
   the central enzyme of medium-chain fatty-acid beta-oxidation; reduced MCAD activity
   is the classic cause of elevated C6/C8/C10 acylcarnitines (MCAD deficiency).

2) A SECOND SHARED LOCUS = chr5q13 (50.1-50.5 Mb), shared by C10:1 and C6DC
   (5 SNPs, p = 3.1e-10, concordant direction). This region sits near the
   acyl-CoA synthetase / carnitine-transferase cluster.

3) Cross-trait genetic (SNP-level z) correlation confirms a tight positive
   acylcarnitine module and no sharing with unrelated traits:
     C6-C8 r=0.81, C10:1-C8:1 r=0.53, C4-C6 r=0.51, C10:1-C8 r=0.49,
     C8-C8/C2 r=0.49, C10:1-C6 r=0.47, C10:1-C6DC r=0.44, C4-C8 r=0.41,
     C6DC-C8 r=0.40;  PRO-TYR r=0.33 (amino acids).
   Strong negative, anti-correlated: ratio vs C8/C2 r=-0.52, vs C8 r=-0.26,
   vs C6 r=-0.18. All other pairs are near zero.

4) Replication: 11/15 trait-level loci replicate at p<5e-8 and 14/15 have the same
   effect direction. The shared ACADM locus replicates for all four traits. The full
   discovery vs replication z-correlation matrices agree (Pearson r=0.966, mean
   abs diff=0.073). The C6-C8 genetic correlation reproduces at 0.844.

5) Shared genetic factors track shared metabolite levels: genetic (z) correlation and
   metabolite-abundance (log2) correlation agree at Pearson r=0.95 across all 66 trait
   pairs (e.g. C6/C8: 0.81 genetic vs 0.71 metabolic; ratio vs C8/C2: -0.52 vs -0.47).

6) Genes at the single-trait loci are likewise canonical metabolism genes:
   C4 -> ACADS (short-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase, chr12q24);
   C6DC -> CPT2 (carnitine palmitoyltransferase-2, chr1p32);
   C4DC+C5-OH -> CRAT (carnitine acetyltransferase, chr9q34);
   C8:1 -> ACSM1/ACSM2A/ACSM2B/ACSM3/ACSM5 (medium-chain acyl-CoA synthetases, chr16p13);
   PRO -> PRODH (proline dehydrogenase, chr22q11.2);
   TYR -> HPD (4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase, chr12q24);
   C10:1 -> CYP4A11/CYP4B1 (fatty-acid omega-hydroxylases, chr1p33).

CONCLUSION
The neonatal metabolites do NOT each have independent genetic control. The dominant
shared genetic factor is the ACADM (medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase) locus on
chr1p31.1, which pleiotropically regulates the medium-chain acylcarnitines C6 and C8,
the ratio C8/C2, and inversely the ratio (C3DC+C4-OH)/C10. A second shared locus
(chr5q13) couples C10:1 with C6DC. The remaining loci act mostly on single metabolites
via short-chain (ACADS), carnitine-transfer (CPT2, CRAT, ACSM), proline (PRODH) and
tyrosine (HPD) metabolism. Because genetic sharing mirrors metabolite co-variation
(r=0.95), these acylcarnitines should be treated as a correlated, co-regulated trait
family rather than independent traits — of direct relevance to newborn screening for
fatty-acid oxidation disorders (MCAD deficiency).

CAVEATS
Only 13 of ~75 metabolites and 20,474 SNPs were analysed; no LD reference panel was
available, so "shared locus" was defined by 1 Mb distance-clumping and LD-free Z-score
correlation rather than true LD/colocalization. Z-score correlation is a proxy for
genetic correlation and cannot exclude cohort overlap; no effect-size meta-analysis was
run. ORN/CIT showed no genome-wide signal (possible lack of power). Candidate genes are
the strongest known candidates, not proven causal genes.
da-24-3.notes: The agent performed robust shared-locus and correlation analyses but did not implement inverse-variance meta-analysis or colocalization, resulting in low scores on the relevant criteria.

da-25-1.answer:
DA-25-1 — TCGA (PRAD) Pathogenic/Oncogenic mutations & clinical T-stage association
=====================================================================================

SUMMARY
-------
Using the TCGA-PRAD matched mutation (MAF) + clinical + mRNA files, the analysis
defines "pathogenic/oncogenic" mutations as protein-altering (non-silent) variant
classes, excluding sequencing artifacts (isArtifactMode != 1) and low-support
calls (variant allele fraction > 5%), and restricts the ranking to a cancer-gene
set (COSMIC Cancer Gene Census annotations in the file, supplemented with
established prostate/pan-cancer drivers such as SPOP, FOXA1, etc.). 20,642
qualifying mutations were retained across 498 TCGA-PRAD tumors.

Q1. TOP MUTATED (PATHOGENIC/ONCOGENIC) GENES
---------------------------------------------
Top 20 mutated driver genes (number and % of tumors carrying at least one
protein-altering mutation):

  1. TP53    (52 tumors, 15.1%)
  2. SPOP    (49 tumors, 14.2%)
  3. FOXA1   (27 tumors,  7.8%)
  4. KMT2C   (26 tumors,  7.6%)
  5. KMT2D   (24 tumors,  7.0%)
  6. ATM     (20 tumors,  5.8%)
  7. CHEK2   (16 tumors,  4.7%)
  8. PTEN    (13 tumors,  3.8%)
  9. KDM6A   (12 tumors,  3.5%)
 10. ZMYM3   (11 tumors,  3.2%)
 11. PIK3CA  (11 tumors,  3.2%)
 12. NOTCH2  (11 tumors,  3.2%)
 13. CTNNB1  (10 tumors,  2.9%)
 14. ZFHX3   (10 tumors,  2.9%)
 15. APC     ( 9 tumors,  2.6%)
 16. CDK12   ( 9 tumors,  2.6%)
 17. ARID2   ( 9 tumors,  2.6%)
 18. MED12   ( 8 tumors,  2.3%)
 19. CHD1    ( 8 tumors,  2.3%)
 20. BRCA2   ( 8 tumors,  2.3%)

Percentages are over the 344 tumors that carry at least one driver mutation.
TP53 and SPOP are the dominant drivers of primary prostate cancer, followed by
FOXA1, the KMT2C/KMT2D (MLL-family) histone methyltransferases, the DNA-repair
genes ATM/CHEK2/BRCA2/CDK12, and the PI3K pathway (PTEN, PIK3CA). A naive count
of ALL mutated genes is dominated by long passenger genes (TTN, FRG1B, MUC16,
SYNE1, NBPF1), which is why the ranking must be restricted to cancer genes.

Q2. VISUALIZING THE RESULTS
-----------------------------
Yes. Two figures were generated (in the analysis/ folder of this workspace):
  * top_drivers_oncoplot.png  — (A) bar chart of top-20 driver mutation
    frequency; (B) an oncoplot matrix (patients x genes) showing each tumor's
    mutation profile, sorted by mutation count.
  * tmb_tstage.png            — (A) boxplot of tumor mutational burden by
    pathologic T stage; (B) clinical-T-stage vs TMB scatter.
This is the cBioPortal "oncoprint" style (mutations/copy number/expression in a
single matrix). An interactive OncoPrinter/cBioPortal view would present the
same information.

Q3. DOES ANY GENE ASSOCIATE WITH CLINICAL T STAGE (GENOMICS LEVEL)?
--------------------------------------------------------------------
* Single-gene mutation status: NO gene is statistically associated with
  clinical T stage after multiple-testing (FDR) correction. Only nominal,
  underpowered signals exist (MYCBP2 p=0.008; SMAD4 OR=10.1 p=0.019; CHEK2
  OR=3.41 p=0.039; TP53 OR=2.22 p=0.054) — all non-significant after BH-FDR
  (minimum q=0.44). There were only 55 advanced (T3/T4) cases among 406
  staged patients, so the cohort is underpowered. The same is true for
  PATHOLOGIC T stage (TP53 OR=2.84, p=0.0025 nominal; q=0.25). TP53 is the
  most biologically plausible candidate but does not survive correction.

* Aggregate genomics level (tumor mutational burden, TMB = # protein-altering
  mutations per tumor): TMB is significantly HIGHER in advanced pathologic T
  stage (pT3/pT4 median 26 vs pT1/pT2 median 22; Mann-Whitney p=9.7e-06;
  Spearman rho=0.219, p=9.3e-07). TMB is NOT significantly associated with
  CLINICAL T stage (p=0.24; Spearman p=0.16), consistent with clinical T being
  a pre-treatment, incompletely recorded field (93/500 missing).

* Expression level: 122 genes are differentially expressed between T3/T4 and
  T1/T2 clinical stage (FDR<0.05), dominated by a cell-cycle / DNA-replication /
  proliferation signature (TYMS, FEN1, PLK1, CDK1, TOP2A, AURKB, RRM2, UBE2C,
  MCM2/10, RAD51, EZH2, NEK2, KIAA0101, TICRR, SPAG5 upregulated; FAM107A, DPT,
  SRD5A2, IGF1, CPA1 downregulated). This is a gene-EXPRESSION, not mutation,
  association.

BOTTOM LINE
-----------
1) Top Pathogenic/Oncogenic mutated genes in TCGA-PRAD: TP53, SPOP, FOXA1,
   KMT2C/KMT2D, ATM, CHEK2, PTEN, KDM6A, PIK3CA, ZMYM3, NOTCH2, CTNNB1,
   ZFHX3, APC, CDK12, ARID2, MED12, CHD1, BRCA2.
2) Yes — visualize as a frequency bar chart plus oncoplot (cBioPortal oncoprint
   style); figures generated as top_drivers_oncoplot.png and tmb_tstage.png.
3) At the single-gene level NO gene robustly associates with clinical T stage
   (all nominal hits fail FDR; cohort underpowered). At the genome level, tumor
   mutational burden is significantly elevated in advanced PATHOLOGIC T stage
   (pT3/pT4) but NOT in clinical T stage. Strong associated cell-cycle /
   proliferation expression signature seen at the transcriptomic level.

LIMITATIONS: the MAF has no explicit OncoKB oncogenicity column (definition is
operational and partly curator-defined); copy-number and fusion drivers (PTEN
deletion, TMPRSS2-ERG) are absent from a small-variant MAF; single-gene T-stage
tests are underpowered; clinical-vs-pathologic T differ; correlation not
causation. Full detailed analysis: see trace.md.
da-25-1.notes: The agent performs a largely rigorous analysis with a defensible oncogenic proxy and proper statistical methods, but it diverges from the reference in key areas: it misses the original tumor-sample count, uses clinical T as primary instead of pathologic T, omits expected top genes/frequencies, and critically reports no FDR-significant TP53 association for pathologic T stage, which is inconsistent with the expected result.

da-26-2.answer:
DA-26-2 — Patient-specific biomarkers predicting TCGA patient-level DepMap scores in BRCA

QUESTION
Using CCLE cancer cell line expression and DepMap (essentiality) scores in cell lines and patients, identify which biomarkers are statistically significant in BRCA when predicting TCGA patient-level DepMap scores, specifically those present in patient data but that do not manifest in cell line models.

DATASET USED (BRCA subset of the translational cancer dependency map)
- 1,099 TCGA BRCA patients (expression + patient-level PREDICTED DepMap scores)
- 35 CCLE breast cancer cell lines with BOTH expression and measured CRISPR essentiality
- 140 biomarker genes present and variable in BOTH patients and breast cell lines
- 1,965 dependency-target genes shared by both panels (275,100 biomarker-target pairs tested)

METHOD
For each (biomarker, dependency-target) pair I correlated biomarker expression with the dependency score across samples, in patients and cell lines separately (Pearson + Spearman; Spearman is primary because many biomarkers are bimodal/right-skewed). To avoid the severe power mismatch between the two panels (n=1,099 patients vs n=35 cell lines), I called an association "patient-specific" only if ALL of: (1) significant in patients (Benjamini-Hochberg FDR < 0.05) with a meaningful effect size (|Spearman rho| >= 0.25); (2) weak and non-significant in cell lines (|rho| < 0.30, raw p >= 0.05); and (3) the two correlations differ significantly between panels (Fisher-z heterogeneity test p < 0.05, patient correlation stronger).

RESULTS
2,123 patient-specific (biomarker, target) pairs (0.77% of all tested) involving 56 biomarkers (42 protein-coding, 14 non-coding).

TOP PROTEIN-CODING BIOMARKERS THAT ARE SIGNIFICANT IN BRCA PATIENTS BUT DO NOT MANIFEST IN CELL LINES
- A2ML1  — 229 patient-specific targets; max |rho| = 0.51 (vs LDB1, p ~ 3e-74); also associates with ESR1, CDK4, TRPS1, SPDEF, FOXA1-network. Cell-line rho on these targets ~0.11 median, opposite sign, non-significant.
- ABCA13 — 174 targets; max |rho| = 0.48 (vs ZNF559); cell-line rho ~0.11.
- ABAT   — 159 targets; max |rho| = 0.59 (vs TXNRD1, p ~ 4e-104; also GTF2H2, CYB5B); cell-line rho ~0.08.
- AAAS   — 108 targets; max |rho| = 0.49 (vs TMEM82; also ESR1, DERL1); cell-line rho ~0.11.
- ABTB2  — 101 targets; max |rho| = 0.44 (vs SSB; also CDK4, FOXA1, SOX9); cell-line rho ~0.11.
- AAGAB  — 65 targets; max |rho| = 0.45 (vs IRS4); cell-line rho ~0.12, opposite sign.
- ABCC11 — 57 targets; max |rho| = 0.48 (vs WSB2); cell-line rho ~0.10.
- ABCB1  — 72 targets; max |rho| = 0.39 (vs BRIP1); cell-line rho ~0.16.

(Also prominent are NON-CODING biomarkers AC005355.2, AC009303.2, AC005863.1, AC009495.2 — all long non-coding RNAs.)

TOP NON-CODING (present in patients, ABSENT from cell-line expression entirely)
Many long non-coding RNAs are measured in TCGA patients but are not read on the CCLE platform at all. Of 260 biomarkers absent from CCLE expression, 115 are reliably detected in >=30% of BRCA patients and all 115 have at least one significant patient-level association; the strongest are AC005152.3 (SOX9, |r|=0.72), AC007255.8 (FOXA1, |r|=0.70), AC004967.7, AC011330.13. ~98% of these are lncRNAs/antisense/rRNA — a transcriptome-platform coverage gap, not a validated discordant dependency.

DIRECTION OF THE PATIENT-SPECIFIC SIGNAL
For these patient-specific pairs the cell-line correlations are near zero (median |rho| 0.08-0.16) and frequently OPPOSITE in sign to the patient correlation (e.g. A2ML1 patient rho -0.05 -> cell-line +0.02; AAGAB patient +0.10 -> cell-line -0.03), which is the operational signature of "present in patients but not manifest in cell line models."

KEY INTERPRETATION
- The strongest patient signal is enriched for luminal / oestrogen-receptor-network and proliferation targets (ESR1, FOXA1, CDK4, TRPS1, SPDEF, SOX9, TXNRD1, GTF2H2, EZH2, AKT2, RAD51B). This indicates that much of the "patient-specific" biomarker signal tracks molecular subtype (esp. luminal/ER-positive) and proliferation, contexts only poorly represented by a small pool of established breast cell lines.
- ABAT is a mitochondrial GABA-transaminase with a role in cancer metabolism; its association with TXNRD1 (thioredoxin reductase) points to an in-vivo redox/metabolic dependency. A2ML1 is a secreted serpin-like protease inhibitor associated with stromal/EMT and luminal identity. ABCA13/ABCC11/ABCB1 are ABC efflux transporters linked to drug resistance and subtype differences.

LIMITATIONS
1. Patient-level "DepMap scores" are MODEL PREDICTIONS, not measured phenotypes; the predicted dependency is ~a near-deterministic function of the same expression features used as biomarkers (R^2 ~0.91 for FOXA1). Much of the patient correlation is therefore structural/co-linear with the predictor, not independent causality.
2. Severe power mismatch (n=1,099 vs n=35) makes naive "patient-significant, cell-line-not-significant" mostly a power artifact; mitigated here with effect-size thresholds and a Fisher-z heterogeneity test, but cell-line estimates remain noisy (median |rho| ~0.13).
3. Predicted dependency has ~25x LOWER variance than measured essentiality (median variance ratio ~0.041), which attenuates and reshapes patient correlations, limiting quantitative comparability with cell lines.
4. No PAM50/subtype or purity variable is available in the metadata subset, and the classic subtype markers (ESR1, FOXA1, GATA3, TP63) are targets, not measured biomarkers, so I could not formally adjust for subtype/purity. Several top hits (ABAT r=0.52, AAGAB r=0.65, AAAS r=0.48, ABCC11 r=0.38) are strongly co-linear with a global-expression axis and may be subtype/purity surrogates rather than specific drivers; A2ML1 (r=-0.13) and ABCA13 (r=-0.03) are NOT global-axis-driven and are the most "specific" hits.
5. The 314 biomarkers absent from CCLE expression are ~98% non-coding loci — a platform coverage difference. Their strong patient correlations cannot be validated/falsified in cell lines.
6. Correlation is not causation; no gene here was validated by perturbation/CRISPR assays in this work.

HEADLINE ANSWER
The biomarkers that are statistically significant in BRCA at predicting TCGA patient-level DepMap scores but do NOT manifest in CCLE breast cell-line models are, in order of extent/strength: the protein-coding genes A2ML1, ABCA13, ABAT, AAAS, ABTB2, AAGAB, ABCC11, ABCB1, ABCD4, AASDH, A2M, ABCC12, ABCC10, AARS, ABHD2 — plus the long non-coding RNAs AC005355.2, AC009303.2, AC005863.1, AC009495.2 (and, strictly "present only in patient data," many other lncRNAs not measured in cell lines at all). The strongest single associations are ABAT->TXNRD1 (rho=0.59) and A2ML1->LDB1/ESR1 (rho=0.51/0.49).
da-26-2.notes: The agent performed a thorough alternative statistical analysis with correct data loading, BRCA filtering, and robust comparison, but did not implement the required Normality Likelihood Ratio Test, compute SSD, perform distribution classification, integrate a druggable gene list, or identify PTPN11.

da-26-4.answer:
SYNTHETIC-LETHAL (SL) PARTNER DISCOVERY FOR BRCA
==================================================

Question: Predict synthetic-lethal partners for loss-of-function (LOF) events in
BRCA by combining (1) lasso regression linking molecular features to patient-level
predicted dependency, (2) mutual-exclusivity testing against the mutation matrix,
(3) paralog and protein-protein-interaction (PPI) priors, and ranking by
translational relevance.

------------------------------------------------------------------
COHORT & MODEL
------------------------------------------------------------------
- Complete-case cohort: 35 BRCA cell lines that have CRISPR essentiality (CCLE DepMap),
  expression (CCLE), and damaging LOF mutation data.
- Driver set: 159 genes = canonical BRCA tumour suppressors/DNA-repair genes UNION
  genes with recurrent LOF (>=2 of 35 lines). Top drivers by LOF frequency: TP53 (26),
  MUC16/PTEN (6), NF1 (5), BRCA1 (4), ARID1A (3), BRCA2/CDH1/GATA3 (2).
- Dependency targets: 1,965 genes that appear in BOTH the CCLE DepMap and the
  patient-level (TCGA) predicted DepMap matrices.
- Translation: 1,099 TCGA-BRCA patients have a predicted dependency profile; the
  patient-level predicted essentiality of each target scores translational relevance.

------------------------------------------------------------------
METHOD (all components used)
------------------------------------------------------------------
1. LASSO (LassoCV, 5-fold): per target, dependency(T) ~ driver mutation status +
   z-scored driver expression. Negative beta on a driver-mutation feature = loss of
   driver increases dependency on T (SL signal). 7,972 nonzero coefficients across
   1,069 targets; 4,465 negative.
2. PER-PAIR ASSOCIATION: delta = mean_dep(LOF) - mean_dep(WT), Mann-Whitney U p,
   Welch t p, Cohen's d; 239,730 pairs tested, 48.5% with delta<0, 2,273 with p<0.01.
3. MUTUAL EXCLUSIVITY (mutation matrix): (a) driver-driver Fisher exact test over 35
   lines -> alternative tumour-suppressor events are mutually exclusive (MUC16|PTEN,
   NF1|PTEN, BRCA1|PTEN, BRCA1|NF1, TP53|TYRO3); (b) driver-target exclusivity, but
   most targets are not themselves LOF-mutated, so this is under-powered (only
   TP53->NBN met the liberal threshold).
4. PARALOG PRIOR: Ensembl within-species paralogs + curated paralog families
   (p53, SWI/SNF-ARID, PTEN/tensin, PI3K, Fanconi/HR, RAS-GAP, ERBB). Flagged
   BRCA1->FANCI, ARID1A->SMARCA4, ARID1A->PBRM1, PTEN->TNS3.
5. PPI PRIOR: STRING (0.400). High-confidence edges: BRCA1->RBBP8 (0.999),
   PTEN->PIK3CB (0.984), BRCA1->MCM10 (0.849), PTEN->PXN (0.774), PTEN->ACTB (0.720).
6. TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE: mean patient predicted dependency and fraction of 1,099
   TCGA-BRCA patients with predicted dependency < -0.5 for the target.
7. INTEGRATION: composite SL_score = weighted z-score sum of lasso beta, delta,
   Cohen's d, -log10 p, paralog prior, STRING score, mutual-exclusivity segregation,
   and patient essentiality (+ a small bonus for p<0.05).

------------------------------------------------------------------
TOP-RANKED SYNTHETIC-LETHAL CANDIDATES (ranked by SL_score)
------------------------------------------------------------------
 1. BRCA1 (LOF) -> FANCI          (Fanconi/HR; delta -0.256, p=0.0046; patient ess 0.00)
 2. GMCL2      -> PRPS1           (delta -0.796, p=0.0003)
 3. PTEN (LOF) -> PXN             (delta -0.382, p=0.0010; STRING 0.77; patient ess 0.82)
 4. PTEN (LOF) -> PIK3CB          (delta -0.437, p=0.0005; STRING 0.98)
 5. JAKMIP3    -> KATNB1          (delta -0.629, p=0.0034; patient ess 0.81)
 6. BRCA1 (LOF) -> MCM10          (delta -0.386, p=0.00008; STRING 0.85)
 7. BRCA1 (LOF) -> RBBP8          (delta -0.359, p=0.016; STRING 0.999; patient ess 1.00)
 8. LRP1B      -> SUGT1           (delta -0.644, p=0.0003; patient ess 0.997)
 9. ARID1A (LOF) -> SMARCA4       (SWI/SNF paralog family; delta -0.294, p=0.053)
10. JAKMIP3    -> KIAA0100        (delta -0.487, p=0.0003)
11. NF1 (LOF)  -> PPP2R1A         (delta -0.444, p=0.069; STRING 0.27; patient ess 0.999)
12. JAKMIP3    -> NR2C2AP         (delta -0.512, p=0.0006; patient ess 0.73)
13. JAKMIP3    -> COPS7A          (delta -0.496, p=0.0003)
14. PTEN (LOF) -> ACTB            (delta -0.351, p=0.062; STRING 0.72; patient ess 0.99)
15. BRCA1 (LOF) -> USP9X          (delta -0.422, p=0.011; STRING 0.46; patient ess 1.00)
16. ARID1A (LOF) -> PBRM1         (SWI/SNF paralog family; delta -0.161, p=0.140)
17. PTEN (LOF) -> FERMT2          (delta -0.521, p=0.0033; patient ess 0.92)
18. JAKMIP3    -> PRPS1           (delta -0.678, p=0.0095)
19. PTEN (LOF) -> ITGAV           (delta -0.553, p=0.014; STRING 0.25; patient ess 0.75)
20. BRCA1 (LOF) -> CIP2A          (delta -0.366, p=0.009; STRING 0.64)

Validation hits (known SL axes where the target is measured, confirming method):
   ARID1A -> SMARCA2 (SWI/SNF paralog; delta -0.147, p=0.045)
   BRCA1  -> RAD50   (HR; delta -0.163, p=0.023)

------------------------------------------------------------------
BIOLOGICAL / CLINICAL INTERPRETATION
------------------------------------------------------------------
- BRCA1-loss dependencies concentrate on DNA-repair / replication-fork-rescue /
  homologous-recombination genes (FANCI, MCM10, RBBP8, USP9X, CIP2A). This is the
  same "parallel repair pathway" logic that underlies PARP-inhibitor sensitivity in
  BRCA1/2-mutant breast cancer and is the most clinically actionable cluster.
- ARID1A-loss dependencies fall on other mSWI/SNF components (SMARCA4/BRG1, PBRM1),
  the canonical SWI/SNF paralog/co-subunit synthetic-lethal axis.
- PTEN-loss dependencies are PI3K-pathway and cytoskeletal/adhesion genes (PIK3CB,
  PXN, FERMT2, ACTB, ITGAV) - consistent with PTEN-null survival-signalling rewiring.
- NF1-loss dependency on PPP2R1A reflects RAS-MAPK/PP2A crosstalk.

------------------------------------------------------------------
WEIGHT OF EVIDENCE & LIMITATIONS
------------------------------------------------------------------
- The SL_score integrates two independent statistical measures (lasso + per-pair
  association), the mutation-matrix mutual-exclusivity test, paralog and STRING-PPI
  priors, and patient-level translatability.
- Cohort is small (35 cell lines) and driver mutations are sparse; no pair survives
  strict Bonferroni correction over ~240k tests, so the ranking is a list of
  hypothesis-generating candidates, NOT validated biology.
- The target-level mutual-exclusivity test is under-powered because dependency targets
  are rarely themselves LOF-mutated; patient "essentiality" is from the model-predicted
  dependency, and the driver genes are not in the 529-gene patient expression feature
  set, so a direct patient SL contrast could not be made.
- Absence of a STRING score does not imply absence of interaction (partial coverage).

Conclusion: the strongest, most biologically coherent synthetic-lethal partner
discoveries for BRCA are (1) BRCA1-loss -> FANCI / MCM10 / RBBP8 / USP9X (DNA-repair
and replication-fork dependencies), (2) ARID1A-loss -> SMARCA4 / PBRM1 (SWI/SNF
paralog/co-subunit), and (3) PTEN-loss -> PIK3CB / PXN / FERMT2 / ACTB / ITGAV
(PI3K and adhesion/cytoskeletal dependencies). These should be prioritised for
experimental follow-up and as candidate therapeutic targets.
da-26-4.notes: The agent performed a comprehensive analysis with appropriate methods (lasso, mutual exclusivity, paralog/PPI integration), but some required refinements or reporting elements were missing, such as dual-threshold filtering, iterative mutual-exclusivity prioritization, significance thresholds, sequence-based paralog filters, canonical paralog pair reporting, and observed-vs-expected co-occurrence tables.

da-1-3.answer:
FINAL ANSWER — DA-1-3: Cell-subset distribution across tumor, adjacent normal, and peripheral blood, and the subsets specifically enriched only in the tumor microenvironment

COHORT ANALYZED
975,275 cells, 169 samples, 22 patients from the CRC anti-PD-1 cohort (GSE236581): 58 tumor samples (279,886 cells), 52 adjacent-normal samples (260,294 cells), 56 peripheral-blood samples (417,162 cells), pooled across treatment stages I-IV (2 LN and 1 TN sample, 17,933 cells, excluded from statistics as unreplicated). 91 annotated cell subsets in 6 lineages. All statistics below use per-sample subset proportions; inference uses per-patient averages (22 patients, all three tissues available for every patient), paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across the 91 subsets.

1) COMPARTMENT COMPOSITION (mean % of cells per sample; lineage level)
- Peripheral blood: T cells 64.4%, myeloid 14.1% (CD14 monocytes alone 7.4%), B cells 10.7%, ILC 10.1%, epithelial 0.6%, stromal 0.2%. Dominant subsets: naive/central-memory CD4 (c01_CD4_Tn_CCR7 10.6%, c02_Tn_SELL 6.4%, c04_Tcm_ANXA1 5.8%), CD8_Temra_CX3CR1 (6.7%), CD8_Temra_TYROBP (4.1%), Mono_CD14 (7.4%), Mono_FCGR3A (2.2%), ILC_FCGR3A (4.8%), NaiveB_TCL1A (4.5%).
- Adjacent normal mucosa: epithelial 37.9% (colonocytes c84 15.7%, goblet c87 6.0%), B/plasma 23.7% (IgA plasma cells c46_PlasmaB_IGHA1 17.8% - the single most normal-specific population), T cells 27.2% (dominated by tissue-resident CD8_Trm_XCL1 2.4% and CD8_IEL_CD160 2.1%), stromal 8.4% (Fibro_ADAMDEC1 2.8%, Fibro_SOX6 1.1%).
- Tumor: T cells 40.9%, epithelial 29.5%, B/plasma 16.2%, stromal 6.7%, myeloid 4.9% (highest myeloid fraction of the two tissue sites), ILC 1.8%. Most abundant subsets: c84_Coloncyte_CA2 6.0%, c46_PlasmaB_IGHA1 4.2%, c20_CD8_Tem_GZMK 3.7%, c90_Epi_MKI67 3.4%, c05_CD4_Tcm_GPR183 3.1%, c87_Goblet_MUC2 3.0%, c91_Epi_Tumor 2.7%.
- Classification of all 91 subsets by the same rule applied symmetrically: 5 tumor-specific, 5 normal-enriched (c46_PlasmaB_IGHA1, c73_Fibro_ADAMDEC1, c21_CD8_Trm_XCL1, c86_Coloncyte_BEST4, c72_Fibro_SOX6), 20 blood-enriched, 61 shared/low-abundance.

2) SUBSETS SPECIFICALLY AND HIGHLY ENRICHED ONLY IN THE TUMOR MICROENVIRONMENT
Criteria (pre-stated, all four required): median proportion >= 0.5% in tumor; fold-change >= 4 vs BOTH normal and blood; paired Wilcoxon BH-q < 0.05 vs BOTH; median <= 0.5% in BOTH normal and blood.

RANK 1 - c13_CD4_Treg_TNFRSF9 (activated tumor Treg): tumor median 2.36% (mean 2.8%) vs normal 0.28%, blood ~0 (median 0). FC 8.1x vs normal, 237x vs blood; q = 5.5e-05 and 1.3e-06. Detected in 58/58-sample terms in 98% of tumor samples and in 22/22 patients. Raw-count validation: FOXP3 68.8%, CTLA4 71.1%, TIGIT 78.5%, IL2RA 55.2%, LAYN 55.7%, TNFRSF9 42.4% - the top rung of a clean activation ladder across Treg subsets (TNFRSF9 3.3% in c11 -> 16.0% in c12 -> 42.4% in c13).

RANK 2 - c23_CD8_Tex_LAYN (terminally exhausted CD8 T cells): tumor median 1.63% (mean 3.9%) vs normal 0.06%, blood ~0. FC 23.0x / 164x; q = 1.4e-04 / 1.3e-06; 22/22 patients. Validation: LAYN 36.8%, CXCL13 53.9%, HAVCR2 37.7%, PDCD1 35.0%, ENTPD1 32.3%, GZMB 88.3% with GZMK only 33.0% (vs circulating c19_CD8_Tem_CMC1: LAYN 0.2%, GZMK 81.2%).

RANK 3 - c27_CD8_MAIT_SLC4A10 (tissue/tumor-resident MAIT cells): tumor median 1.13% (mean 1.9%) vs normal 0.21%, blood ~0. FC 5.1x / 114x; q = 7.2e-04 / 1.3e-06; 22/22 patients; present in 100% of tumor AND normal samples (a mucosal lineage whose abundance nevertheless concentrates 5-fold in tumor). Validation: KLRB1 93.0%, SLC4A10 30.7%, ZBTB16 37.7%, with tumor-acquired activation LAYN 30.1%, PDCD1 24.1% (blood MAIT c26: LAYN 0.7%, PDCD1 2.8%).

RANK 4 - c07_CD4_Th17_CTSH (tumor Th17 cells): tumor median 0.68% (mean 1.4%) vs normal 0.13%, blood ~0. FC 4.9x / 69x; q = 5.5e-05 / 1.3e-06; 22/22 patients. Validation: KLRB1 77.6%, CTSH 45.5%, RORC 8.7%, IL17A 9.2%, IL23R 9.6%, PDCD1 33.6%.

RANK 5 - c09_CD4_Th1_CXCL13_HAVCR2 (CXCL13+ HAVCR2+ Th1-like helper T cells): tumor median 0.61% (mean 1.3%) vs normal 0.02%, blood ~0. FC 22.9x / 62x; q = 5.5e-05 / 1.3e-06; 22/22 patients. Validation: CXCL13 68.1%, HAVCR2 19.2%, PDCD1 48.1%, CTLA4 54.2%, TIGIT 53.0%.

Together these five subsets constitute, on average, ~28% of all CD4 tumor-infiltrating T
cells (c13+c07+c09) and ~19% of all CD8 tumor-infiltrating T cells (c23) while being
essentially absent from blood (median 0%) and 5–23-fold depleted relative to the patient's
own adjacent normal mucosa. They form one coherent program: antigen-experienced, chronically
stimulated, PD-1-axis (PDCD1/CTLA4/TIGIT/LAYN/CXCL13) T-cell states that the tumor
microenvironment selectively accumulates.

3) TUMOR-ASSOCIATED BUT NOT TUMOR-SPECIFIC (important distinctions)
- c91_Epi_Tumor (malignant epithelium): tumor 2.70% vs normal 1.38% (FC only 1.95; q_vs_normal 1.8e-04) - enriched vs normal but NOT tumor-specific, because normal mucosa is epithelium-dominated by construction. Its tumor-restricted nature is qualitative, not proportional.
- Mucosa-shared populations (fail specificity because normal is equal or higher): c84_Coloncyte_CA2 (tumor 5.99% vs normal 15.73%), c87_Goblet_MUC2 (3.04% vs 6.00%), c46_PlasmaB_IGHA1 (4.17% vs 17.75%), c90_Epi_MKI67 (3.40% vs 3.26%), c20_CD8_Tem_GZMK (3.69% vs 2.05%).
- Strongly tumor-skewed but below the 0.5% abundance floor (would join the list at a 0.1% floor): c70_Endo_COL4A1 (0.42%, tumor-only, FC 43), c79_Fibro_FAP (0.14%, CAF, FC 15, FAP+ 73.2%), c63_Mph_CCL20 (0.11%, FC 12), c55_pDC_GZMB (0.10%, FC 11), c62_Mph_S100A8 (0.21%, FC 5.7), c64_Mph_SPP1 (0.05%, SPP1+ 45.4%, FC 6.3), c60_cDC_LAMP3 (0.06%, LAMP3+ 95.9%, mature DC, FC 4.7). These are genuine tumor-microenvironment-restricted stromal/myeloid populations of low frequency.
- Near-misses on the FC-vs-normal criterion only: c34_ILC_NR4A2 (tumor 1.22% vs normal 0.41%, FC 3.0) and c08_CD4_Tfh_CXCL13_IL6ST (0.68% vs 0.29%, FC 2.3) - tumor-enriched mucosal states rather than tumor-specific ones.

4) ROBUSTNESS
- Results hold restricted to pre-treatment samples only (stage I): c13 2.64%, c23 1.62%, c27 1.43%, c07 0.71%, c09 0.48% - so the calls are not an on-treatment artifact.
- Unpaired Mann-Whitney U agrees with the paired Wilcoxon for all five calls.
- Every called subset is detected in the tumor of 22/22 patients (c64_Mph_SPP1 21/22).
- Marker evidence comes from the raw UMI matrix (streamed 19 GB MatrixMarket parse, 65-gene panel), with cell/gene alignment independently verified: per-cell column UMI sums match metadata nCount_RNA for 975,227/975,275 cells (max |diff| 18); an EPCAM single-gene sweep places 91.0% of EPCAM+ cells in annotated epithelium (per-sample r = 0.958); positive controls pass (LYZ 99.7% in c49_Mono_CD14, MUC2 95.8% in c87_Goblet_MUC2, MKI67 78.1% in c29_T_MKI67, IGHA1 93.0% in c46_PlasmaB_IGHA1, FAP 73.2% in c79_Fibro_FAP).

5) LIMITATIONS
Cell-type labels are the data release's annotations (no re-clustering); blood-vs-tissue differences partly reflect sampling/dissociation (blood draw vs colonoscopy/surgery), which is why tumor-specificity calls rest on immune subsets recoverable from all compartments; proportions are compositional and fold-changes vs blood use a +1e-4 pseudocount on medians (blood FCs of 62-237x mean "median blood fraction = 0"); the 0.5%/4x/q<0.05 thresholds are conventional and the near-miss list quantifies sensitivity; no response-stratified (CR/PR/SD) or causal claims are made here.

SUMMARY SENTENCE
The tumor microenvironment is distinguished from both adjacent normal mucosa and peripheral blood by the selective accumulation of activated/exhausted, PD-1-axis T-cell states - activated TNFRSF9-hi Tregs (c13, median 2.36% of tumor cells), exhausted LAYN+CXCL13+ CD8 T cells (c23, 1.63%), tumor-resident MAIT cells (c27, 1.13%), Th17 cells (c07, 0.68%), and CXCL13+HAVCR2+ Th1-like helpers (c09, 0.61%) - each 5-23x enriched over adjacent normal and essentially absent from blood (22/22 patients, BH-q < 1e-03), with lower-frequency tumor-restricted stromal/myeloid populations (FAP+ CAF, SPP1+ and CCL20+ macrophages, LAMP3+ mature DC, COL4A1+ endothelium) below the 0.5% abundance floor.
da-1-3.notes: The analysis is rigorous and well-documented but does not restrict to baseline only, and its abundance threshold excludes expected myeloid/stromal tumor-specific subpopulations from the top list, causing several B-level ratings.

da-1-4.answer:
FINAL ANSWER — DA-1-4: Correlation between tumor regression ratio and baseline cell-subtype proportions (GSE236581, n = 22 CRC ICB patients)

METHOD (one correlation per subtype across patients; "for each patient" supplies the per-patient values that enter each correlation)
- Baseline = pre-treatment biopsies (Treatment stage "I", confirmed "Pre"/"Baseline" in clinical.xlsx); primary compartment = tumor (105,959 cells; one baseline tumor sample per patient; median 4,789 cells/patient).
- For each patient, SubCellType proportions were computed from the 91 annotated clusters; each subtype's per-patient proportion vector was correlated with the per-patient Tumor Regression Ratio (TRR, -0.026 to 1.000; 12 CR, 7 PR, 3 SD) using Spearman rank correlation (plus Pearson, BH-FDR over 91 tests, and MSI/MSS-adjusted partial Spearman as sensitivity analyses).

DIRECTION OF THE CORRELATIONS — BOTH SIGNS OCCUR, IN A BIOLOGICALLY COHERENT PATTERN

POSITIVE correlations (higher baseline proportion -> more regression -> better response):
- c23_CD8_Tex_LAYN (exhausted CD8 T cells): rho = +0.506, p = 0.016 (MSI-adjusted p = 0.019); present in all 22 patients (3,832 cells). Most robust association.
- c13_CD4_Treg_TNFRSF9 (activated/tumor-antigen-experienced Treg): rho = +0.470, p = 0.027 (adjusted p = 0.035); all 22 patients (3,498 cells).
- Combined tumor-reactive T fraction (Tex + TNFRSF9+ Treg): rho = +0.477, p = 0.025.
- c68_Endo_FABP5 (endothelium): rho = +0.502, p = 0.017; c82_SMC_MYH11 (smooth muscle): rho = +0.536, p = 0.010 (few cells: 64/139 — directional support only).
- All-tissue baseline adds tertiary-lymphoid-structure populations: c44_GCB_MKI67 rho = +0.589 (p = 0.004), c43_GCB_LRMP +0.470, c08_CD4_Tfh_CXCL13 +0.440, c46_PlasmaB_IGHA1 +0.405.

NEGATIVE correlations (higher baseline proportion -> less regression -> poorer response):
- c87_Goblet_MUC2 (normal-like goblet epithelium): rho = -0.464, p = 0.030 (adjusted p = 0.033; 5,985 cells, 21/22 patients).
- Aggregated normal-like epithelium (goblet + colonocytes + enterocytes etc.): rho = -0.486, p = 0.022.
- c84_Coloncyte_CA2: rho = -0.351; c45_PlasmaB_TXNDC5: rho = -0.353; B-lineage subtypes overall skew negative (2/10 positive).
- Malignant epithelium itself is NOT correlated (rho = +0.184, p = 0.41); major-lineage proportions are all non-significant (T +0.22, Epi -0.20, others ~0).

Of 91 subtypes, 6 reach nominal p < 0.05 (5 positive, 1 negative); none survive FDR < 0.05 across 91 tests (min q = 0.36) at n = 22. Direction split across the 62 well-detected subtypes: 33 positive vs 29 negative (sign-test p = 0.70). Associations are unchanged after MSI/MSS adjustment and leave-one-out (all headline LOO ranges exclude 0).

WHAT THIS IMPLIES
1. Sign of the immune signal is POSITIVE: tumors that regress most under anti-PD-1 therapy are those whose BASELINE microenvironment is already enriched for terminally differentiated exhausted CD8 T cells (LAYN+ Tex) and activated TNFRSF9+ Tregs — i.e., a pre-existing, chronically antigen-stimulated ("hot"/pre-primed) T-cell response. PD-1 blockade re-invigorates pre-primed tumor-reactive T cells rather than recruiting new ones, so baseline Tex/Treg content marks an inhibitable infiltrate and predicts pathological regression.
2. Sign of the normal-epithelial signal is NEGATIVE: biopsies dominated by normal-like mucosal epithelium (goblet cells, colonocytes) — effectively a "colder", less immune-dominated or lower-tumor-content biopsy — regress least.
3. Positive GCB/Tfh/plasma-cell correlations point to pre-existing tertiary lymphoid structures as an additional response-favoring feature.
4. Clinical implication: baseline tumor-biopsy cell-subtype composition (high Tex + activated Treg, low normal-like epithelium) is a candidate pretreatment predictor of regression under ICB. No such signal exists in baseline blood in this cohort, so the predictor is tumor-local.

LIMITATIONS
- Only 22 patients (no PD; 3 SD); correlations are nominally significant only and do not survive multiple-testing correction; effect sizes |rho| ~ 0.5 need larger cohorts for confirmation.
- Observational associations; residual confounding by regimen (mono vs chemo-combination), MSI, TMB, stage beyond the MSI adjustment performed.
- Proportions are compositional: the positive-immune/negative-normal-epithelium pattern is partly one axis (immune fraction vs epithelial dilution), and biopsy tumor-cellularity was not available to separate tumor content from biology.
- Rare subtypes (SMC_MYH11, Endo_FABP5) have unstable estimates; raw UMI matrix not reprocessed (provided annotations taken as given).

Files: analysis trace in trace.md; per-patient table per_patient_summary.csv; full correlation tables results_subcelltype_tumor_baseline.csv (91 subtypes), results_subcelltype_tumor_baseline_filtered.csv (62), results_majorcelltype_tumor_baseline.csv; figure fig_subtype_vs_TRR.png.
da-1-4.notes: The analysis is rigorous in baseline filtering, count matrix construction, normalization, merging, and batch correlation, but falls short on rare/zero-variance filtering completeness, top negative candidate identification, and the specificity of negative-correlation biological interpretation. Source reliability is strong.

da-3-4.answer:
FINAL ANSWER — Tumor mutational load (TML) vs anti-PD-1 response, GSE78220 melanoma WES cohort (Hugo et al., Cell 2016)

QUESTION: Is tumor mutational load associated with patient response to anti-PD-1 therapy?

BOTTOM LINE
Higher mutational load is directionally associated with response (responders carry ~1.8x the median mutation burden of non-responders, and median burden decreases monotonically across irRECIST categories: complete response 678 > partial response 465 > progressive disease 283), but the association is NOT statistically significant in this cohort of 38 patients. Mutational load alone is not a sufficient predictor of response: the R and NR distributions overlap heavily.

COHORT AND METRIC
- n = 38 patients (Pt1-Pt38) with WES and response annotation; 21 responders (R: 7 complete + 14 partial response) and 17 non-responders (NR: progressive disease), per the S1B "Response" column, which matches irRECIST-derived labels with 0 discordances.
- Mutational load = TotalNonSyn + TotalIndelNonSyn (non-synonymous SNV + non-synonymous indel counts from sheet S1B); cross-validated against sheet S1D per-mutation calls (Spearman rho = 0.995, p = 5e-37).
- Primary analysis cohort: pre-treatment biopsies, n = 34 (20 R, 14 NR); full 38-patient cohort reported in parallel.

PRIMARY STATISTICAL TEST (as required, named)
Two-sided Mann-Whitney U test (Wilcoxon rank-sum), chosen because mutation burden is a right-skewed count variable (range 73-4,004) with small, unequal group sizes.
- Pre-treatment cohort (n=34): R median TML = 490 (IQR 316-711) vs NR median = 273 (IQR 166-612); U = 172.0, p = 0.270.
- All 38 patients: R median = 497 (IQR 317-811) vs NR median = 283 (IQR 233-623); U = 214.0, p = 0.304.
- SNV-only burden (TotalNonSyn) gives identical ranks: p = 0.270 / 0.304.

ASSOCIATION / CORRELATION METRICS
- Rank-biserial correlation: 0.23 (pre-treatment, n=34); 0.20 (all 38).
- Common-language effect size / AUC of TML as response classifier: 0.61 (pre-treatment); 0.60 (all 38) — a random responder has higher burden than a random non-responder ~61% of the time (0.50 = no association).
- Spearman rho (TML vs binary response): 0.195, p = 0.269 (pre-treatment); 0.171, p = 0.304 (all 38).
- Point-biserial correlation: r = 0.169, p = 0.34 (pre-treatment); r = 0.187, p = 0.26 (all 38).
- Univariate logistic regression: OR = 1.39 per doubling of TML (95% CI 0.83-2.32; likelihood-ratio p = 0.20) pre-treatment; OR = 1.38 (95% CI 0.84-2.26, p = 0.20) all 38.
- Dichotomized at the cohort median (TML = 474): response rate 65% (11/17) high-burden vs 53% (9/17) low-burden; Fisher exact p = 0.728.

SENSITIVITY CHECKS (conclusion unchanged)
- Welch t-test on raw counts: t = 1.07, p = 0.30 (pre-treatment); t = 1.21, p = 0.23 (all 38). On log2 counts: p = 0.23 / 0.21. Exome-normalized burden: p = 0.56 / 0.61.
- Excluding the two hypermutated responders (Pt4 = 4,004; Pt27 = 2,313 mutations) weakens the trend (Spearman rho = 0.12, p = 0.50): the association is substantially carried by extreme responders.
- TML is uncorrelated with technical covariates (purity rho = -0.05, p = 0.79; mean coverage rho = -0.05, p = 0.77; % bases >=15x rho = 0.11, p = 0.53), so the negative result is not a power/coverage artifact.
- Predicted strong-binding neoepitopes (StrongBinder) show the same direction and non-significance: R median 112 vs NR median 83, Mann-Whitney p = 0.27.
- Subgroup note: BRCA2-mutant tumors (n = 7) were responders in 6/7 (86%) cases vs 15/31 (48%) for BRCA2-wild-type, consistent with a DNA-repair-deficiency hypermutation route, but unadjusted and too small to test.

INTERPRETATION
The direction of every estimate agrees with the neoantigen hypothesis of checkpoint blockade (higher non-synonymous burden -> more neoepitopes -> better T-cell recognition), and predicted neoepitope counts track burden. However, with n = 34-38 and heavy overlap between groups (6 of 14 non-responders exceed the responders' median burden; one responder had only 81 mutations), no metric reaches significance (all p >= 0.20), and the 95% CI for the odds ratio per doubling of TML (0.83-2.32) includes no effect. This cohort therefore shows a consistent but statistically non-significant trend toward higher mutational load in responders; it cannot establish mutational load as an independent or sufficient predictor of anti-PD-1 benefit, nor distinguish predictive from prognostic value (single-arm data), and cannot validate any TML threshold (the Youden-optimal cut of TML > 283, sensitivity 0.80 / specificity 0.57, is data-driven).

Full methods, code, and intermediate results: trace.md. Figure: figure1_tml_response.png.
da-3-4.notes: The agent's work meets full-score criteria across all six dimensions: correct data source identification and handling, justified non-parametric test selection and implementation, clear descriptive statistics, contextual interpretation, and reliable sourcing.

MUTATION ENRICHMENT IN ANTI-PD-1 RESPONDERS (R, n=21) vs NON-RESPONDERS (NR, n=17)
Hugo et al. 2016 (GSE78220) WES cohort; Supplementary Table 1D (25,393 non-synonymous somatic calls, 38 patients, 9,877 genes)

METHOD

The published recurrence design was reproduced exactly: NumHitsR/NumHitsNR for all 36 S1E genes matched my matrix 36/36 and 36/36, and all Fisher p-values were recomputed to reported precision. Each gene's mutated-patient fraction in a group was tested against its background prevalence in 469 independent melanomas (TCGA SKCM n=348 via CGAN Supplemental Table S2A "npat" + Hodis 2012 n=121 unique Tumor_Sample_Barcode with non-synonymous mutations) by one-sided Fisher exact test; multiple testing corrected by Holm step-down (this reproduces the paper's pAdjR/pAdjNR exactly, max deviation 1.4e-17). INDEPENDENT WITHIN-COHORT CHECK (R vs NR Fisher, two-sided)
FREM1 10R/1NR OR=14.5 P=0.0099; FMO1, UTRN, OR13C5 7R/0NR P=0.011; TACC2, SCN5A 9R/1NR P=0.012; TRPM2 1R/6NR P=0.031; BCLAF1/ITGAX/CLEC14A 0R/5NR P=0.012. No gene survives BH-FDR<0.05 across all 2,704 genes tested (n=38 is too small for genome-wide significance).

SPECIFIC MUTATIONS BEHIND THE TOP HITS (from S1D)
- FREM1: 11 mutated patients (10 R, 1 NR), all private dispersed variants (P1527L, H1103Y, D1092N splice, T526P, P340S, R482C, D922N, P2131L, D590N); no hotspot.
- OR13C5: 7 responders; recurrent hotspot p.M185I (chr9:107361140 C>T) in 3 patients (COSMIC-annotated); remaining variants private.
- BRCA2: 6 R + 1 NR, all missense (S2522F/rs80358985, H2361Y, E2115K, H2537Y, P2505S, V950L, S1792F) - VUS, functional HRD not established.
- TRPM2: 6 NR + 1 R, private missense/splice variants; CLEC14A: 5 NR including nonsense W93*.

FREM1 is the strongest and most robust responder-enriched gene (48% vs 6%; significant both against background and within cohort). Most other responder-enriched genes are long, UV-exposed genes (UTRN, TACC2, PKHD1, CDH23, MUC12) or olfactory receptors, consistent with responders carrying higher overall UV-mutational burden rather than selected driver events. CLEC14A and TRPM2 enrichments in non-responders have no established mechanism and need validation.

LIMITATIONS
n=38; the 36-gene candidate list was selected on the outcome (>=25% of one group, <=1 in the other), so significance is inflated (selection/circularity) and Holm correction is within-list only; no gene passes genome-wide BH-FDR in the within-cohort scan; background comparison spans different platforms and does not model gene length/trinucleotide context (MutSigCV-style correction would be required); MUC12/AMER3 lack usable background data in the provided files; associations do not establish causality or predictive value for pembrolizumab.

Reproducibility: analysis code and full intermediate results are in trace.md; software: Python 3.13.9, pandas 2.3.3, scipy 1.18.1, statsmodels 0.15.0.
da-3-5.notes: The analysis is comprehensive and mostly correct, but the explicit classification of Stable Disease as Responder conflicts with the rubric's required grouping, warranting a B for criterion 2; all other criteria are met at A level.

da-4-1.answer:
FINAL ANSWER — NMF-based patient classification of the tumor immune microenvironment (anti-PD-1-treated NSCLC, GSE243013 immune scRNA-seq)

Optimal number of patient classes: 2 (rank k = 2)

Yes. Consensus Non-negative Matrix Factorization on the patient-level immune-composition matrix identifies a single stable, two-class patient classification.

DATA PROCESSED
- 1,254,749 immune cells x 23 fields, 243 patients, 3 major lineages / 51 sub cell types.
- Cell QC (n_genes 200-6000, total_counts >= 500, pct_mt <= 10%, pct_rb <= 50%): 1,239,225 cells kept (98.76%).
- Samples with >= 500 QC-passing immune cells: 235 of 243 (584-10,960 cells each).
- Composition matrix: 235 patients x 51 cell states, row-normalized to relative frequencies (4.3% zeros).

RANK SELECTION (50 NMF restarts per rank, KL divergence, sklearn NMF solver='mu')
- k=2: cophenetic 0.991, PAC 0.099, 60% of sample pairs co-clustered in >=90% of runs -> the only stable solution.
- k>=3: cophenetic <=0.966 and PAC >=0.164; partitions fragment into unstable singletons (e.g. k=3 -> 103/57/39 + 22 fragments).
- Reconstruction error falls monotonically (11.47 at k=2 to 6.40 at k=10) and is not informative alone.
Conclusion: k = 2 is the optimal (and only reproducible) classification.

THE TWO CLASSES (final NNDSVD-initialized KL-NMF, error 12.30)
1) B/plasma-high class: 47/235 patients (20%).
   Mean B-lineage fraction 46.2% (vs 17.2%): memory B cells Bm_PDE4D (12.2% vs 4.2%), Bm_TNFSF9 (11.4% vs 3.8%), Bm_TNF (7.2% vs 2.0%), Bm_CD74 (5.2% vs 1.8%), naive Bn_TCL1A, plasma cells, GCB_RGS13.
   Lower T/NK (43.7% vs 64.0%) and myeloid (10.1% vs 18.8%) content.
2) T/myeloid-high class: 188/235 patients (80%).
   Relatively enriched in CD8T_Tm_IL7R, CD8T_Tem_GZMK+GZMH+, CD8T_Tem_GZMK+NR4A1+, CD8T_Tex_CXCL13, CD8T_Trm_ZNF683, NK_CD16hi_FGFBP2, CD4T_Treg_FOXP3/CCR8, Mφ_VCAN, Mφ_MARCO, cDC2_CD1C.
   Metagene H loadings: T/myeloid factor tops out on Bm_PDE4D (0.77), Bm_TNFSF9 (0.72), CD4T_Tn_CCR7 (0.54); B/plasma factor on CD8T_Tem_GZMK+GZMH+ (0.47), CD8T_Tm_IL7R (0.51), Plasma_cell (0.28) - the two factors are complementary ends of one B-cell-density axis.

CLINICAL VALIDATION
- Pathological response (binary, pCR excluded): MPR 12/26 (46.2%) in B/plasma class vs 32/124 (25.8%) in T/myeloid class; chi-square p = 0.038; Fisher OR 2.46 (95% CI 1.03-5.88, p = 0.056).
- Continuous pathological_response_rate: mean 0.88 vs 0.72, Mann-Whitney p = 0.0046.
- Radiological response (CR/PR/SD/PD): chi-square p = 0.0028; CR+PR fraction 2.7x higher in the B/plasma class.
- pCR vs non-MPR: 60% vs 41%, p = 0.037. 3-level test p = 0.055 (responders concentrate in the same class).
- Covariates balanced (all p > 0.08): age, sex, LUSC/LUAD, stage, smoking, chemo regimen, targeted therapy, cycles; multivariable logistic MPR ~ class + LUSC + stage + age gives adjusted OR ~ 2.4 (p = 0.058).

ROBUSTNESS
- Rank-2 structure recovered under Frobenius and KL divergence and under 200/500/1000-cell sample thresholds (B/plasma axis preserved in all); boundary patients (~24/235) change label across variants.
- Meta-analysis of the axis is consistent across every sensitivity run in direction.

INTERPRETATION
A B-cell/plasma-cell-enriched, TLS-like humoral immune microenvironment defines the responder phenotype of neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 (+ platinum doublet) NSCLC therapy, while a T/myeloid-skewed TIME with exhausted CD8 T cells (CD8T_Tex_CXCL13), Tregs and MARCO+ macrophages defines the non-responder phenotype. The B-cell/TLS-response association matches published ICB cohorts (Helmink 2020 Nature; Cabrita 2020 Nature; Petitprez 2020 Nature).

LIMITATIONS
