da-4-6.answer:
FINAL ANSWER

Approximately 50% of non-MPR patients (32 of 64 evaluable; 45.7% [32/70] if the 6 patients lacking a Texp measurement are counted in the denominator) have high Texp cell levels — i.e., a Texp fraction of the "Tex-relevant" pool above the non-MPR subgroup median (Texp.in.Tex.relevant*10 = 8.05, ~80.5% of Tex-relevant cells).

This high-Texp half of the non-MPR cohort indeed shows markedly favorable recurrence-free survival despite lacking pathological response:
- High Texp (n=32): 4/32 recurrences (12.5%); 24-month RFS 0.864 (95% CI 0.677-0.947); median RFS not reached.
- Low Texp (n=32): 17/32 recurrences (53.1%); 24-month RFS 0.416 (95% CI 0.232-0.591); median RFS 15.78 months.
- Log-rank p = 3.9e-4; Cox HR (high vs low) = 0.17 (95% CI 0.06-0.52, p = 0.0017); continuous Texp HR = 0.42 per +1 percentage point of Texp fraction (p ~ 2e-5).

Robustness: using the whole-cohort median (8.37) as the cutpoint, 26/64 = 40.6% are "high" and the survival split remains significant (log-rank p = 0.011); a log-rank cutoff scan gives a minimum p = 2.6e-7, indicating the association is monotone and not an artifact of the median cutpoint. High-Texp non-MPR patients are enriched for TIME module 1-high status (18/32 vs 9/32) and balanced across TCR type I/II (14 vs 18).

Interpretation: about half of patients without major pathological response nonetheless carry a Texp-high (progenitor-exhausted CD8 T cell-rich) tumor immune microenvironment, and these patients recur at roughly one-sixth the hazard of Texp-low non-MPR patients, so Texp levels could identify a favorable-prognosis subgroup among non-responders.

Limitations: the exact proportion depends on the chosen threshold (50% at the subgroup median vs 40.6% at the cohort median); 6/70 non-MPR patients lack the Texp feature; only 21 recurrence events are available, so multivariable adjustment (possible only in the 31 patients with numeric PD-L1 TPS, all <1%) is underpowered (adjusted HR 0.34, 95% CI 0.07-1.71, p = 0.19); and this is a single-cohort retrospective association that cannot establish causality.
da-4-6.notes: The agent handles data loading, endpoint construction, Texp scaling and within-non-MPR median stratification well, but omits the required MPR group from survival stratification, Cox contrasts, and MPR-like comparability criterion, which prevents full credit on criteria 3-5.

da-4-7.answer:
FINAL ANSWER — Expanded Tex-relevant TCR clonotypes shared across multiple patients (anti-PD-1-treated NSCLC sc atlas, GSE243013)

CONTEXT (how candidates were defined)
- 434,458 T/NK cells, 231 samples, 255,451 clonotypes. Tex compartment = CD8T_Tex_HAVCR2 (31,093 cells) + CD8T_terminal_Tex_LAYN (10,244 cells); it is the most expanded compartment (85%/82% of cells in expanded clonotypes).
- "Expanded" = dataset flag, verified identical to clonotype size >= 3 cells.
- "Shared across patients" was evaluated on TCR sequences (clonotype IDs are sample-local): primary stringency = exact TRA+TRB pair (Va|Ja|CDR3a + Vb|Jb|CDR3b), because a TCR-T product requires a defined alpha-beta pair.
- Screen: expanded clonotypes containing >=1 Tex cell (5,581 clonotypes / 34,053 cells) -> 14 exact TRA+TRB pairs found in >=2 patients (none in >=3). Full table: analysis/shared_tex_tcr_candidates.csv.

TIER 1 - SHARED ACROSS GENUINELY DISTINCT PATIENTS (best TCR-T candidates)
1) TRBV20-1 / TRBJ2-7 / CASSVGSYEQYF + TRAV12-1 / TRAJ34 / CVVNPNTDKLIF
   Samples P391 (LUSC, nPR, PRR 0.40) and P482 (LUSC, pPR, PRR 0.80); 16 cells, max clonotype 12 cells, 38% Tex (6 Tex cells); CD8 (TRBC1). The same two samples also share a closely related clonotype family (TRBV7-2/TRBJ2-7/CASSFGGYEQYF with a 1-aa-shorter TRA CDR3, CVVNTDKLIF; 16 cells, 69% Tex), i.e. a convergent Tex-cluster, not a single stochastic hit.
2) TRBV5-6 / TRBJ2-7 / CASSLVSYEQYF + TRAV6 / TRAJ44 / CALPTTGTASKLTF
   Exact pair in P199/P200; the same beta chain is expanded and Tex-relevant in 4 distinct patients overall (P74, P199, P200, P502; P74 and P502 both pCR, PRR 1.00) with different alpha partners (TRAV38-1, TRAV17). 17 cells, 65% Tex.
3) TRBV18 / TRBJ2-5 / CASSPGGGETQYF (+ TRAV29/DV5/TRAJ43/CAASFNGDNNDMRF)
   Exact pair in P199/P200; the same beta chain carries expanded Tex-relevant clonotypes in 4 patients (P121, P199, P200, P259) with 3 different alpha chains; 37 cells, 49% Tex, terminal-Tex enriched (11 LAYN+ cells). Chain-level convergence across 4 distinct patients.

TIER 2 - LARGE, HIGHLY TEX-COMMITTED CLONOTYPES SHARED ONLY BETWEEN SAMPLE PAIRS WITH REPETOIRE IDENTITY (probably the same individual sampled twice; excellent TIL/TCR-T leads for those tumours, but "cross-patient" is unproven)
- TRBV27 / TRBJ2-7 / CASSLAGGDEQYF + TRAV8-1 / TRAJ9 / CAVKNTGGFKTIF: P70/P71; 339 cells (largest Tex clonotype in the atlas), max clone 325 (P70) + 14 (P71), 73% Tex (175 HAVCR2+ Tex, 71 terminal-Tex LAYN, 37 Trm, 28 Ki-67+ proliferating). P70 LUAD nPR, P71 LUAD pCR. A hyperexpanded, exhaustion-committed, proliferating clonotype - the single strongest Tex phenotype signal in the cohort.
- TRBV4-3 / TRBJ1-2 / CASSPTGTGLEGYTF + TRAV24 / TRAJ35 / CALIIGFGNVLHC: P70/P71; 50 cells, 80% Tex (23 HAVCR2+ + 17 LAYN+ terminal Tex).
- P199/P200-pair entries (P199 LUSC pCR, P200 LUSC MPR): TRBV5-5/TRBJ1-1/CASSPGPGGTEAFF + TRAV12-3/TRAJ28/CAMSDLGAGAGSYQLTF (130 cells, 45% Tex); TRBV6-2/TRBJ1-5/CASSVSGTGFLRQPQHF + TRAV13-1/TRAJ33/CAAEMDSNYQLIW (117 cells, 32% Tex, Trm->Tex); TRBV19/TRBJ2-5/CASSMTSGPGETQYF + TRAV29/DV5/TRAJ52/CAASDNWVSSTSYGKLTF (46 cells, 50% Tex); TRBV7-9/TRBJ2-1/CASSHPTDYNEQFF; TRBV7-8/TRBJ1-1/CASSLGMANTEAFF; TRBV7-9/TRBJ2-1/CASSLRSNEQFF (52% Tex); TRBV27/TRBJ1-5/CASSLGQGEQPQHF; TRBV20-1/TRBJ2-3/CSAEPGSDTQYF; TRBV15/TRBJ2-3/CATSRDAGTGDTDTQYF.
- CAUTION for Tier 2: P199/P200 share 123 exact TCR pairs (repertoire Jaccard 0.074), P70/P71 share 29 (0.019) - 10-100x above the cohort 99.9th percentile (0.0029) - so these two "patient pairs" are most likely the same individuals; if they truly were distinct patients, these would be the most public Tex clonotypes in the cohort.

EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED (would be false positives)
- TRBV29-1/TRBJ1-4/CSVGTGGTNEKLFF: recurs in 13 patients but with 7 different alpha chains (TRAV5 with TRAJ23/30/34/37, TRAV27) and only 4% Tex cells -> public/bystander convergent chain, not a tumour-antigen receptor.
- TRBV7-9/TRBJ2-1/CASSDSLSSYNEQFF with TRAV10 alpha chains -> iNKT-like public receptor, 3/47 Tex cells.
- CDR3-beta-amino-acid-only recurrences CASSLGYEQYF (5 patients) and CASSLTLNTEAFF (3 patients): short convergent sequences recombined on different V genes - not treated as candidates.
- All TRAV1-2 (MAIT) clonotypes (19,189 cells cohort-wide) and gamma-delta/NK/ILC entries.

CLINICAL CONTEXT
Tex burden is lower in pathological responders (n=197 patients with response data: median Tex fraction 5.9% in pCR/MPR vs 8.1% in pPR/nPR, Mann-Whitney p=8.6e-4; Spearman rho=-0.205 vs Pathological Response Rate, p=3.8e-3), while the expanded fraction of Tex does not differ (p=0.97). Tier-1 candidates come from patients spanning nPR, pPR and pCR, i.e. recovered from both residual-disease and complete-response tumours.

LIMITATIONS (what cannot be concluded)
- No antigen/HLA/peptide data in these files: tumour specificity of every candidate is unproven; each requires target identification (peptide-MHC screening) and normal-tissue cross-reactivity/safety testing before TCR-T use.
- No tumour-vs-blood/normal contrast available, so tumour enrichment is inferred only from Tex commitment and clonal expansion.
- Sample-pair identity (P199/P200, P70/P71, P469/P470, P485/P486) cannot be resolved from the data; this is the main uncertainty separating Tier 1 from Tier 2.
- CDR3s are amino-acid only (no nucleotide sequences), so allele-level identity and SHM-based clonal assignment cannot be verified; single-cell capture biases affect clone sizes.
- Response associations are patient-level/ecological, not causal for any individual clonotype.

BOTTOM LINE
The only expanded, Tex-relevant TCRs that are demonstrably shared across unrelated patients in this cohort are: TRBV20-1-TRBJ2-7/CASSVGSYEQYF paired with TRAV12-1-TRAJ34/CVVNPNTDKLIF (P391/P482, with a related convergent Tex cluster), the TRBV5-6-TRBJ2-7/CASSLVSYEQYF clonotype family (4 patients, 65% Tex), and the TRBV18-TRBJ2-5/CASSPGGGETQYF family (4 patients, 49% Tex). The most striking Tex clonotypes overall - TRBV27/CASSLAGGDEQYF (339 cells, 73% Tex, proliferating) and TRBV4-3/CASSPTGTGLEGYTF (80% Tex) - are shared only between samples that appear to derive from the same individuals (P70/P71), and likewise for the nine P199/P200 pairs; they remain strong autologous TIL/TCR-T leads but their cross-patient publicity is unproven.
da-4-7.notes: The agent performs a rigorous sequence-based public TCR search with paired-chain definitions and cross-patient aggregation, but deviates from the rubric by using broader Tex subsets, ≥3-cell expansion instead of ≥10-cell per-patient filtering, incomplete candidate reporting, and limited MPR/pCR prioritisation and validation criteria.

da-5-1.answer:
FINAL ANSWER — Prioritized druggable protein targets for pancreatic cancer (PDAC)
================================================================================

CRITERIA APPLIED (both required)
--------------------------------
A gene was called a promising PDAC drug target only if it satisfied BOTH:
  (1) significant OVEREXPRESSION of the protein in PDAC tumors vs normal pancreatic tissue
      (adjusted p <= 0.01), and
  (2) DEPENDENCY in cancer cell lines from DepMap CRISPR knockout screens in matched
      pancreatic lineages (adjusted p <= 0.01).
Both criteria are pre-computed as the "PDAC" indicator column of Table S3A in mmc3.xlsx
(per the workbook's Information sheet: "significantly overexpressed in tumor vs normal of
that cancer cohort (adj. p <= 0.01) and is also a gene dependency by CRISPR KO from DepMap
in matched cancer cell line lineages (adj. p <= 0.01)"). Druggability tiers come from
mmc2.xlsx Table S2A (T1 = target of approved cancer drugs; T2 = approved non-cancer drugs;
T3 = clinical-stage/investigational; T4 = DGIdb druggable genome; T5 = in-silico surfaceome),
and drug counts from Table S2B.

FUNNEL
------
5,262 screened genes (Table S3A)
  -> 1,431 PDAC-overexpressed AND CRISPR-dependent (both adj. p <= 0.01)
  ->   353 of these also pan-cancer essential (DepMap EssentialGenes=1)
  ->   222 in a druggability tier (T1-T5)
  ->   127 actionable now (T1-T3: T1=34, T2=32, T3=61)
  ->    27 highest-confidence core (T1-T3 AND pan-cancer essential)

TIER-1 PDAC TARGETS (approved drugs exist; 34 genes) — overexpressed + CRISPR-dependent
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Essential (DepMap) targets first:
  TUBB (13 drugs, 9 with cancer indication), TOP2A (13/8), RRM2 (6/5), RRM1 (5/5),
  MTOR (27 drugs), PSMB1, DNMT1, HDAC3, KRAS, XPO1, PSMB2, TUBG1, ARL2
Non-essential but overexpressed + dependent, with strong clinical assets:
  PDGFRB (20 drugs), ERBB2 (17), MET (18), BTK (16), CSF1R (13), MAP2K2, ATIC, MAP4, SRC,
  ALOX5, IKBKB, YES1, JUN, DDR2, GART, NECTIN4, TXNRD1, DPYD, TYMP, F3, MAP1A
Example drug mappings (Table S2B): RRM1 -> gemcitabine/cladribine; TUBB -> paclitaxel,
docetaxel, cabazitaxel; TOP2A -> doxorubicin, etoposide, daunorubicin; MTOR -> everolimus,
temsirolimus; XPO1 -> selinexor; DNMT1 -> azacitidine, decitabine; PSMB1 -> bortezomib,
carfilzomib; KRAS -> sotorasib; ERBB2 -> trastuzumab, lapatinib; MET -> capmatinib,
cabozantinib, tepotinib, amivantamab.
Validation: RRM1 (gemcitabine's direct target) and TUBB (taxane target) are exactly the
two components of the standard PDAC chemotherapy backbone — the analysis independently
rediscovers standard of care.

HIGHEST-CONFIDENCE CORE (Tier 1-3 + pan-cancer essential; 27 genes)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
T1: TUBB, TOP2A, RRM2, RRM1, PSMB1, DNMT1, MTOR, XPO1, HDAC3, PSMB2, TUBG1, ARL2, KRAS
T2: TFRC, FDPS, GGPS1, FNTA
T3: CDK1, CDK7, AURKB, BCL2L1, CSNK1A1, SMS, ATP6V1A, PHB2, PIK3C3, PIP5K1A
These meet all three axes at once: PDAC tumor-overexpressed, CRISPR-dependent in matched
lines, existing pharmacology, and pan-essential knockout phenotype.

TIER 2-3 (clinical-stage / preclinical druggability; 93 genes; highlights)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
T2 (32): FDPS, GGPS1, TFRC, FNTA (essential); ACE, F2, CACNA2D1, VDR, F11, HSD11B1,
    ATP2C1, COL1A1, ITGAV, ITGA4, ITGB1, MMP7, SQLE, LDHA, ANO1, NFKB2, GANAB, PDXK, etc.
T3 (61): CDK1, AURKB, CDK7, PIK3C3, CSNK1A1, PIP5K1A, BCL2L1, SMS, ATP6V1A, PHB2 (essential);
    MAPK14, GSK3B, AKT1, AKT2, TBK1, PAK1 (dependent in 8/8 cohorts), HSP90AA1, FASN, CA9,
    CD276 (B7-H3), FAP, ADAM10, KDM5B, KDM3A, ITGA5, ITGB6, CLDN18, MST1R (RON), PTPN1, etc.

PDAC-ENRICHED SUBSET (overexpressed + dependent in <= 2 of the 8 cohorts; 100 of 222)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Relatively PDAC-selective, hence wider therapeutic window: PDGFRB, BTK, CSF1R, YES1, DDR2,
IKBKB (T1); ITGAV, ITGA4, ITGB1, MMP7, SQLE, LDHA, PDXK (T2); FAP, ADAM10, CA9, CD276,
MST1R, ITGA5, ITGB6, CLDN18, AKT1/2, GSK3B (T3); PTPN11, ITGB4, NEK6/7 (T4); FAS, LDLR,
LRP1, PODXL, CD9 (T5 surfaceome). KRAS itself has CancerTypeCount = 1 — its
overexpression+dependency intersection is unique to PDAC among the 8 cohorts.

MECHANISTIC SUPPORT (secondary, from S3C methylation / S3D CNV cis analyses)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
- 10 of the 1,431 candidates also show methylation-cis regulation in PDAC, e.g. PDXK (Tier 2,
  protein-level hypomethylation association r = -0.34, p = 1.2e-03).
- Druggable PDAC CNV-amplification drivers that are overexpressed but NOT CRISPR dependencies
  (so not on the primary list): ADAM9 (T5), EPHB4 (T3), LMTK2 (T4) — plausible antibody/ADC
  candidates that fail the dependency criterion.

BOTTOM LINE
-----------
The most promising PDAC drug targets that are BOTH significantly overexpressed in tumors vs
normal tissue AND required by PDAC cells in CRISPR knockout screens are, in priority order:
(1) the 27-gene highest-confidence core — TUBB, TOP2A, RRM1, RRM2, MTOR, PSMB1, PSMB2,
DNMT1, HDAC3, XPO1, KRAS, TUBG1, ARL2, TFRC, FDPS, GGPS1, FNTA, CDK1, CDK7, AURKB, BCL2L1,
CSNK1A1, SMS, ATP6V1A, PHB2, PIK3C3, PIP5K1A — all with existing drug pharmacology
(many already in oncology use, e.g. gemcitabine/RRM1, taxanes/TUBB, proteasome inhibitors/
PSMB1, selinexor/XPO1, everolimus/MTOR);
(2) clinically validated receptor/signaling targets PDGFRB, ERBB2, MET, BTK, CSF1R;
(3) the PDAC-enriched development candidates FAP, CD276, CA9, MST1R, ITGB6, CLDN18, ADAM10,
AKT1/2, CDK1/CDK7/AURKB inhibitors — more selective, earlier stage.
Full ranked tables: pdac_druggable_prioritized.csv (222 targets) and
pdac_overexpressed_dependent_all.csv (all 1,431 qualifying genes).

CAVEATS: rankings rely on druggability tier, essentiality and drug availability because the
provided matrix is thresholded (no fold-changes); cell-line dependency does not guarantee
patient-tumor dependency; pan-essential Tier-1/3 targets (TUBB, TOP2A, PSMB1, CDK1) carry
predictable toxicity and their value depends on therapeutic index; no survival or response
data were available, so clinical benefit is not established here.
da-5-1.notes: The agent performed a rigorous data-driven analysis with correct loading, filtering, merging, and extensive source grounding, but diverged from the rubric by prioritizing pan-essential over non-pan-essential targets and not ranking by multi-cancer validation strength; some expected pathway rationales and validation next steps were also missing.
