Overall, 42 of the 65 hit genes have at least one mapped drug in tiers 1-3 and 13 have an approved cancer-indicated drug; the remaining genes (CDK7, CDK9, CDK12, PLK1, CHEK1, WEE1, ATR, PAK1/2/6, PRKCD/PRKCI, PKN1/2, RPS6KA1/3/4, RPS6KB1, LIMK1, SLK, STK39, CAMK2G, MAPK1/14/6, MAP3K11, GSK3B, AKT1, CDK1, CDK10, MAPKAPK5, DAPK2, LMTK2, EGLN1, PI4KB, PLD1, PDE11A, PRKG1, PTPN1, USP1, MARS1, HSP90AA1/AB1, ITGA4, LTB4R, TK1, LDHA, PYGL, CAD, SLC2A1) sit in investigational or druggable-genome (Tier 4/5) space and represent therapeutic opportunities with both tumor-elevation and CRISPR-dependency evidence.

INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION BY KINASE ACTIVITY (Table S4B KSEA, adj. p <= 0.05, Z > 0)
29 of the 213 hit pairs (12 kinases) are additionally supported by significantly elevated activity of the host kinase itself in the SAME cohort: EGFR in CCRCC (Z=4.55, adj.p=3.9e-5; all six EGFR sites flagged there), CDK1_T161 in COAD/LSCC/LUAD (Z=6.5/10.5/7.2; strongest signal genome-wide, adj.p down to 1.4e-24), CHEK1 S280/S296/S317 in HNSCC/LSCC/LUAD, PLK1_T210 in HNSCC/LSCC/LUAD, ATR_T1989 in HNSCC/LSCC, ATM_S1981 in LSCC, AKT1_S124 in PDAC (Z=4.02), MTOR_S2448 in PDAC, PAK1_S174 in PDAC (Z=3.97), PRKCA_S226 in PDAC, RPS6KA1_S380 and RPS6KB1_S441/S447 in CCRCC.

BIOLOGICAL INTERPRETATION
The hits form coherent, druggable axes: (1) cell-cycle and checkpoint kinases with classic activation-loop/T-loop phosphorylations (CDK1 T161, CDK7 S164/T170, CDK9 T186, PLK1 T210, CDK12 T893, WEE1 S642, CHEK1 S280/S296/S317) - a pan-cancer dependency signature; (2) RTK/MAPK/PI3K signaling - EGFR (six sites, CCRCC-dominant), BRAF_S446, MAP2K2_T394, MAPK1_Y187, MAPK14_Y182, RPS6KA/B, AKT1_S124, MTOR_S2448, PAK1/2/6, SRC_S17; (3) DNA-damage response - ATM_S1981 (the defining ATM autophosphorylation) and ATR_T1989/S428, pointing to PARP/ATR-inhibitor strategies; (4) epigenetic and structural enzymes - DNMT1_S154, HDAC1 S421/S423 (CK2 sites that maintain HDAC1 activity), HDAC3_S424, HDAC6_S22, TOP2A S1106/S1337/S1525, PARP1_S782, XPO1_S1055; (5) metabolism and transport - LDHA_Y10, PYGL_S430, CAD_S1859, EGLN1_S125 and the single Tier-5 surfaceome hit SLC2A1_S490 (GLUT1; CCRCC+HNSCC, consistent with HIF-driven clear-cell renal carcinoma). Because each pair also carries matched-lineage CRISPR dependency, these sites are candidate phospho-biomarkers for selecting tumors likely responsive to the corresponding (existing or investigational) inhibitors.

LIMITATIONS
The joint flags are a binary upstream integration at adj. p <= 0.01 (no effect sizes or raw statistics are recoverable from S4A, so hits cannot be ranked by magnitude); dependency is measured in cell lines, not tumors; the conjunctive design hides sites that are tumor-upregulated in cohorts lacking a matched dependency (and vice versa); site numbering follows the Ensembl primary isoform and may differ from UniProt canonical numbering; ActivatingSite is a curated annotation whose mechanistic basis is literature-supported only for a subset of sites; KSEA corroboration is only possible for the 53 kinases covered by S4B; and no clinical outcome data are included, so prognostic/predictive value cannot be assessed from these tables.

Full inventory, code and per-step counts: trace.md (supporting artifacts: analysis.py, hits_long.csv, hits_with_drugs.csv, hits_ksea_supported.csv, summary_stats.txt).
da-5-3.notes: The agent's data filtering, pair generation, tier/cancer reporting, and drug annotation closely match the expected full-score outputs; the primary gap is the absence of explicit next-step validation experiments and pan-essentiality discussion, leading to a B on Criterion 5.

da-6-2.answer:
FINAL ANSWER — Temporal dynamics of the gene-expression response to 8 weeks of endurance training in rat vastus lateralis skeletal muscle (SKM-VL), males vs females (MoTrPAC differential-analysis table, task DA-6-2)

DATA BASIS. 279,002-row training-regulated feature table filtered to tissue = SKM-VL and assay = TRNSCRPT: a complete, balanced panel of 766 genes x 2 sexes x 4 timepoints (1w/2w/4w/8w), 0 missing values. Every gene in the panel is training-significant overall (training_q IHW-FDR < 0.05); "DE" below means timewise p < 0.05 at a given timepoint, i.e. when a training-regulated gene is moving.

1) OVERALL TIME COURSE - FEMALES RESPOND EARLIER AND MORE BROADLY; MALES ARE LATE-EMERGENT
- Female DE-gene counts rise monotonically: 220 (1w) -> 329 (2w) -> 501 (4w) -> 532 (8w), i.e. 70% of the panel is timewise-significant by 8w.
- Male counts start lower and dip before rising: 145 (1w) -> 134 (2w) -> 176 (4w) -> 379 (8w); half the panel.
- Onset: 220 female genes first become significant at 1w vs 145 in males, and for the 402 genes DE in both sexes the female cohort reaches significance earlier in 223 genes vs 77 for males (102 ties). 251 male genes only appear at 8w (vs 84 female).
- Effect sizes are modest and similar (median |logFC| across all gene-timepoints: female 0.25, male 0.21); the sexes differ mainly in timing/statistical strength, not magnitude (among shared genes, male max |logFC| exceeds female in only 42%).

2) SEX CONCORDANCE INCREASES WITH TRAINING DURATION
- Spearman correlation of male vs female logFC across the 766 genes: 1w rho=0.12 (p=1e-03), 2w rho=0.05 (p=0.20), 4w rho=0.57 (p=6e-67), 8w rho=0.71 (p=2e-118).
- Explicit sex-difference Wald tests (|logFC_M - logFC_F| / combined SE, BH-FDR across 3,064 tests) are maximal at 2w (184 genes p<0.05, 26 FDR<0.05) and nearly vanish at 4w/8w (2 and 3 FDR-significant).
- Interpretation: weeks 1-2 are the most sex-divergent phase; by 4-8 weeks the two sexes converge on the same directional program.

3) PREDOMINANT PATTERNS (Gaussian-mixture clustering of per-sex z-score time courses, K=5; BIC-supported shapes)
Female: (i) late-emerging up (z 1.6 -> 4.0, n=154), (ii) sustained up from 1w (z 2.9 -> 3.8, n=102), (iii) weaker late up (n=126), (iv) sustained down (z -1.6 -> -2.8, n=232, largest cluster), (v) flat (n=152).
Male: (i) early-sustained up from 1w (z 2.1 -> 1.5, n=153), (ii/iii) late-emerging up (n=127+172) and late-emerging down (n=176, z ~0 at 1-2w to -2.0 at 8w), (iv) sustained down from 2w (n=138), flat excluded.
Female-pattern x male-pattern assignment is strongly non-random (chi2=455.5, df=9, p=2e-92): genes keep the same direction across sexes but shift timing.

4) SHARED VS SEX-SPECIFIC PARTITION OF THE 766 GENES
- Shared and direction-concordant: 364 genes (48%). Of these, 54% peak at the same timepoint in both sexes, 96% have the same sign at 8w, and female vs male 8w z-scores correlate r=0.84.
- Female-specific (DE in females only): 255 genes (33%).
- Male-specific (DE in males only): 105 genes (14%).
- Shared but opposite direction: only 38 genes (5%) - sex differences are overwhelmingly quantitative (timing/amplitude), not sign reversals (examples of discordance: Tnmd, Col1a1, Tnfrsf12a, Sln, Ndrg1).
- 4 genes never reach timewise significance in either sex (training-level only).

5) THE SHARED CORE PROGRAM = MITOCHONDRIAL OXIDATIVE METABOLISM, PROGRESSIVELY INDUCED
GO:BP over-representation on leading-edge genes (g:Profiler, g_SCS q<0.05): oxidative phosphorylation p=9.0e-07; energy derivation by oxidation of organic compounds 8.5e-06; respiratory electron transport chain 2.2e-05; proton transmembrane transport 3.5e-05. Named shared up-regulated genes: Ckmt2 (female z +4.4 -> +7.9; male +1.9 -> +2.1), myoglobin Mb (F +1.7 -> +7.3; M -0.2 -> +2.2), Mt-co1, Mt-nd2, Mt-co3, Mt-atp6, Hspb6, Prdx2, Vcl, Lgi3, Mgst3, Gpd1l, Bola3. Shared down-regulated genes: Fos (F z -3.9 -> -6.9; M -2.2 -> -2.4), Hsp90b1, Hspa5, P4ha1, Gstm2, Bcat2, Adhfe1, Psap - i.e. repression of ER-stress/immediate-early and related programs while oxidative genes rise.

6) THE FEMALE-SPECIFIC PROGRAM = EARLY, STEEP MITOCHONDRIAL ENERGY INDUCTION + A SUSTAINED FEMALE DOWN-MODULE
- Female-only leading genes: mitochondrial electron-transport constituents Mt-nd3, Mt-nd4, Mt-nd5, Mt-cyb, Mt-atp8, Ndufa2, Cycs, plus Lipe (lipolysis; +0.59 logFC, z=+5.2 already at 1w), Fabp4, Dbi, Tead4, Pitx3. Enrichment: oxidative phosphorylation p=5.8e-08, ATP synthesis coupled electron transport 2.7e-07, mitochondrial complex-I/NADH-dehydrogenase assembly 4.5e-05.
- All 13 mtDNA-encoded genes in the panel are female-specific (7) or shared-with-stronger-female-signal (6); median 8w z of mtDNA genes: female +5.9 vs male +1.7.
- The largest female cluster is sustained down-regulation (n=232; centroid z -1.6 -> -2.8) containing Per2, Prkag3, Mlec, Calm2, Sort1, Nmrk2, Glul, Sh2b2 - attenuation of circadian/glycogen-sensing and related programs.

7) THE MALE-SPECIFIC PROGRAM = LATE EXTRACELLULAR-MATRIX REMODELING, MOSTLY AT 8 WEEKS
- The only enriched male-specific terms are extracellular matrix organization (p=0.016) with genes Fbln1, Fbn1, Cilp, Col1a1, Col5a1, Col5a2, Ecm2, Ltbp2, Abca8a, Abca9, Itm2a - consistently DOWN in males and essentially unchanged in females (Cilp male z -4.5 -> -5.4 vs female ~0; Fbn1 male -2.3 -> -4.1 vs female n.s.).
- Males also show a distinct early-sustained cluster (n=153; e.g. Ckmt1 logFC +4.1 at 1w) but no female-equivalent mitochondrial enrichment at early timepoints.

BOTTOM LINE. SKM-VL gene expression changes progressively, not transiently, over the 8 weeks in both sexes: a shared, direction-concordant program dominated by gradual induction of oxidative-phosphorylation/mitochondrial genes (Ckmt2, Mb, mtDNA transcripts) and repression of stress/immediate-early genes (Fos, Hsp90b1). The predominant sex difference is timing and breadth, not direction: female muscle engages the full mitochondrial oxidative program within 1-4 weeks (33% of genes are female-only, heavily OXPHOS-enriched), whereas male muscle shows a biphasic course - modest early response, a 2-week trough that is also the point of maximal statistical sex divergence, and a late 8-week emergence that includes a male-restricted extracellular-matrix-remodeling (ECM-gene repression) component (14% of genes). Only 5% of genes change in opposite directions between sexes.

CAVEATS. All conclusions are conditional on the 766-gene training-regulated panel (no non-responsive background genes are in the file, so counts/prevalence are within-panel); timewise p-values are used nominally (the table's FDR is the feature-level training_q); sample-size/batch metadata and raw data are absent, so the original model cannot be refit and "female-specific" partly reflects stronger statistical evidence in females at similar logFC; protein/metabolite layers (424 METAB + 80 IMMUNO SKM-VL rows) were excluded because the question concerns gene expression; 72/766 gene IDs are retired Ensembl identifiers without current symbols.

Supporting files: analysis/output/tables/ (DE counts, logFC matrix, per-gene cluster assignments and class labels, GO enrichment), analysis/output/figures/skmvl_temporal_dynamics.png (4-panel summary), analysis/scripts/ (all code), analysis/README.md (methods record).
da-6-2.notes: Overall the agent produced a thorough, well-documented analysis, but it did not implement the required per-gene, per-sex all-four-timepoint significance filter and 4-character directional state encoding, which also impacts shared/sex-specific pattern ranking.

da-6-5.answer:
ANSWER (Task DA-6-5): To what extent does endurance training elicit coordinated molecular responses across different organs, and which tissues exhibit the most similar changes?

VERDICT IN ONE SENTENCE
Endurance training produces a molecular response that is genuinely coordinated across organs but modular rather than global: about 30% of the 22,251 training-regulated molecular entities are regulated in two or more tissues, 79% of the 134 tissue pairs show positively correlated effect sizes (median Pearson r = +0.17), and the shared features change direction in agreement far above chance (57% same-sign, pooled binomial p ~ 1e-84) - and the most similar tissues are, in order, the two skeletal muscles (gastrocnemius and vastus lateralis, r = +0.90), the two brain regions (cortex and hippocampus, r = +0.81), and blood and spleen (r = +0.67).

DATA ANALYZED
data/paper_deg.xlsx (MoTrPAC endurance-training rat differential-analysis table): 279,002 rows = (feature x assay x tissue x sex x timepoint) statistics, 20 tissues, 9 omes (transcriptome, metabolome, proteome, phosphoproteome, acetylome, ubiquitinome, ATAC-seq, RRBS methylome, immunoassays), sexes male/female, timepoints 1w/2w/4w/8w. Every row is already significant (training_q <= 0.05, IHW FDR). Effect measure used: the study's timewise z-score (sign-consistent with logFC in 99.997% of rows), averaged over the 4 timepoints and the 2 sexes per feature; 22,251 distinct entities.

1) EXTENT OF COORDINATION
- 6,643 of 22,251 regulated entities (29.9%) are training-regulated in >= 2 tissues; 593 in >= 5 tissues; only 6 in >= 10. Each organ also retains a large organ-specific program (70% single-tissue).
- Directional coordination is highly significant: 98/132 evaluable tissue pairs have sign concordance > 0.5 (median 0.57); pooling all 21,281 shared-feature comparisons gives 56.7% same-direction (chance 50%, binomial p = 5.2e-85).
- Effect-size coordination: 106/134 pairs (79%) have Pearson r > 0 on shared features; 32 pairs remain significant after Bonferroni correction over all 134 tests; r ranges from -0.39 to +0.90.
- Overlap enrichment (conservative background = union of 22,251 entities): 60/136 pairs hypergeometric p < 0.05; strongest adrenal-driven overlaps: ADRNL-SKM-VL 2.4x, ADRNL-SPLEEN 2.0x, ADRNL-BLOOD 1.8x, ADRNL-COLON 1.7x, ADRNL-BAT 1.7x.
- So: coordination is real and widespread, but its strength is organized along organ-system lines rather than uniform; some pairs even anti-correlate (HYPOTH-SMLINT r = -0.39, BAT-SKM-VL -0.33, BLOOD-HIPPOC -0.32).

2) WHICH TISSUES ARE MOST SIMILAR (primary answer; r = correlation of mean timewise z-scores over features regulated in both tissues)
1. SKM-GN - SKM-VL (gastrocnemius vs vastus lateralis skeletal muscle): r = +0.897 (n = 237, p ~ 1e-59), sign concordance 0.94; transcriptome-only r = +0.91; holds in both sexes (female +0.79, male +0.77). The single most reproducible training response.
2. CORTEX - HIPPOC (brain regions): r = +0.807 (n = 25, p = 3e-7), concordance 0.84; adjacent neuro pairs HIPPOC-HYPOTH +0.63 and ADRNL-HYPOTH +0.59.
3. BLOOD - SPLEEN (immune compartments): r = +0.670 (n = 338 shared genes, p = 2e-45), concordance 0.73 - a shared circulating immune-cell transcriptional program.
Further high-similarity pairs: CORTEX-LUNG +0.65; CORTEX-HEART +0.60; COLON-HYPOTH +0.55; CORTEX-SMLINT +0.54; HEART-HYPOTH +0.51; KIDNEY-SKM-VL +0.51; LIVER-PLASMA +0.50 (driven by 182 shared metabolites - liver as source of the plasma metabolome shift); KIDNEY-WAT-SC +0.50; HEART-SKM-GN +0.43 (largest overlap after adrenal pairs, n = 507).

Tissue modules from hierarchical clustering (average linkage on 1 - r, cut 0.75):
- Immune module: {BLOOD, SPLEEN} (mean within-r 0.67)
- Neuro-gut module: {CORTEX, HIPPOC, SMLINT} (0.49)
- Oxidative-fitness module: {HEART, KIDNEY, SKM-GN, SKM-VL, WAT-SC} (0.40)
- Endocrine-visceral module: {ADRNL, COLON, HYPOTH, LIVER, LUNG, PLASMA} (0.34)
- BAT stands alone (large overlap counts with ADRNL/COLON but idiosyncratic direction).
Most "integrated" tissues (highest mean similarity to all others): CORTEX 0.37, HYPOTH 0.34, PLASMA 0.33, LIVER 0.32, HEART 0.31; least integrated: SMLINT 0.10, BLOOD 0.12, COLON 0.14.

3) TEMPORAL DYNAMICS OF THE COORDINATION
- Timewise-significant features follow a U-shape over training duration: 25,959 (1w) -> 25,464 (2w) -> 20,786 (4w) -> 30,888 (8w); 45% of regulated features are significant at only one of the four timepoints.
- Two temporal modes split cleanly by tissue (correlation-based clustering of the 4-point mean|z| profiles):
  * Progressive amplification (peak at 8w): BLOOD (mean|z| 1.79 -> 2.84), SKM-GN (1.72 -> 2.65), HEART (1.72 -> 2.50), BAT (1.35 -> 2.43), SKM-VL, KIDNEY, LIVER, SPLEEN, WAT-SC - the fitness/metabolic module.
  * Early transient (peak at 1-2w, then decline): SMLINT (2.06 -> 1.04), HYPOTH (2.15 -> 1.25), CORTEX (2.30 -> 1.57), HIPPOC, LUNG; ADRNL, COLON, PLASMA are mixed.
- The early and late programs are mostly different molecules: correlation of per-feature z at 1w vs 8w is only 0.30; 54% of features keep the same sign; 11,097 features are strong (|z|>=2) only at 8w vs 4,666 only at 1w. Coordination is therefore re-established in each time window rather than being one static signature.

4) REPRESENTATIVE COORDINATED MOLECULES (named via Ensembl REST ID mapping; directions from the data)
- Broadest metabolites: trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMAO) regulated in 14/20 tissues with matched early kinetics (log2FC -0.5 to -1.7 at 1-2w, normalizing by 4w); N-methylproline (13 tissues), C3-DC carnitine, ectoine, ala-ala (11 each), 5-methylcytosine rising progressively in 10 tissues (8w log2FC up to +0.69).
- Broadest genes: MT-ATP6, GHITM, BST2, NDUFA12, HMGN2 (8 tissues each); COX4I1, EPAS1/HIF-2alpha, PLA2G2A, RNF213, LCP1, PIK3CD, C3, DLST, GSN (7 tissues) - an oxidative-metabolism axis (NDUFA12, COX4I1, MT-ATP6, DLST) plus an immune axis (BST2, LCP1, PIK3CD, C3, NFAM1, TRAF3IP3) matching the BLOOD-SPLEEN module.
- Circulating immunoassay analytes change broadly: FRACTALKINE/CX3CL1 (9 tissues), TNFA (8 tissues).
- The BLOOD-SPLEEN similarity is carried by 338 concordantly positive transcripts (e.g. TINAGL1 z 3.35/1.74, MXI1 2.85/1.74, TSG101 2.68/1.97, SLC25A39 2.11/2.30).

5) ROBUSTNESS
- Transcriptome-only similarity (the one assay in almost all tissues) reproduces the ranking: SKM-GN-SKM-VL +0.91, BLOOD-SPLEEN +0.67, KIDNEY-SKM-VL +0.56, HEART-SKM-GN +0.50.
- An alternative signed effect measure (sign(logFC) x -log10 p), which additionally covers OVARY, TESTES and VENACV (no z-scores), agrees with the primary matrix (Spearman 0.98 over common pairs) and keeps the same top pairs (SKM-GN-SKM-VL +0.84, CORTEX-HIPPOC +0.77, BLOOD-SPLEEN +0.65); pairs involving VENACV/TESTES/OVARY rest on 5-20 shared features and are not interpreted.
- Sex stratification: coordination persists in each sex (median pair r female +0.23, male +0.17; SKM pair top in both), but strength is sex-modulated for some pairs (BLOOD-SPLEEN male +0.59 vs female +0.22).

LIMITATIONS
- The table lists only significant features (training_q <= 0.05), so the full tested universe is unknown; overlap enrichments use the conservative union of 22,251 entities and are lower bounds, and no "fraction of the genome affected" can be computed.
- Similarity is computed on shared significant features only; pairs with few shared features (HYPOTH-SMLINT n = 9; anything with VENACV/TESTES/OVARY) are unstable and n is reported for every pair.
- Feature IDs differ by ome (Ensembl genes vs RefSeq proteins vs metabolite names), so same-gene transcript-protein coupling could not be computed without an ID conversion resource; omes are pooled assuming z-score comparability.
- No pathway/gene-set enrichment was performed (no rat multi-ome gene-set universe provided); module interpretation rests on named molecules and cited mechanisms (Semenza 2016 on HIF-2; Holloszy 1967 on mitochondrial adaptation; Pedersen & Febbraio 2012 on myokine/endocrine cross-talk; Wang et al. 2019 on TMAO; Stanford & Goodyear 2016 on adipose remodeling).
- Timewise p-values are nominal per contrast; the timewise-significant fractions are descriptive, not FDR-controlled.
- Rats under a 1-8 week endurance protocol: extrapolation to humans, resistance exercise, or longer durations is out of scope.

BOTTOM LINE
Endurance training elicits a coordinated, multi-organ molecular response that is strongest and most similar (a) between the two skeletal muscles (r ~ 0.9), (b) between brain regions (r ~ 0.8), and (c) between blood and spleen (r ~ 0.67), organized into an oxidative-fitness module (heart, kidney, both muscles, white adipose), a neuro-gut module, an immune module, and an endocrine-visceral module; the coordination is directionally consistent (57% same-sign, p ~ 1e-84) but temporally biphasic - an early transient brain/lung/gut response at 1-2 weeks and a progressively amplifying muscle/heart/adipose/blood response peaking at 8 weeks, executed partly by different molecules in each window.
da-6-5.notes: The agent correctly handles data loading, feature definition, and de-duplication, but falls short on per-assay set-similarity computation and cross-assay aggregation, resulting in a valid but incomplete cross-tissue coordination analysis.

da-8-1.answer:
DA-8-1 — FINAL ANSWER
Hypertension-associated metabolites with significant POSITIVE correlation with systolic blood pressure within the 'Bread-spiker' group, adjusted for age and BMI (OLS: Systolic bp ~ metabolite + age + BMI; n = 14 bread-spikers with metabolomics; beta > 0 and p < 0.05; 435 QC-passing metabolites tested; ranked by p-value):

1. Proline (feature "Proline; CE10; ONIBWKKTOPOVIA-BYPYZUCNSA-N", m/z 116.0704) — beta = +29.53 mm Hg per log2 unit, SE 6.50, t = 4.54, p = 0.0011 (arginine/proline metabolism; HMDB00162, KEGG C00148)
2. Asp-Arg (aspartate-arginine dipeptide; HMDB28747) — beta = +18.01, SE 4.33, t = 4.16, p = 0.0020 (dipeptide)
3. Kynurenic acid (tryptophan-kynurenine pathway; HMDB00715, KEGG C01717) — beta = +11.87, SE 2.97, t = 3.99, p = 0.0025
4. Pro-Phe (proline-phenylalanine dipeptide; HMDB11179) — beta = +8.81, SE 2.28, t = 3.86, p = 0.0032
5. Creatinine (feature [306], m/z 114.0663; HMDB00562, KEGG C00791) — beta = +47.64, SE 13.79, t = 3.45, p = 0.0062
6. Threonine (HMDB00167, KEGG C00188) — beta = +32.75, SE 9.92, t = 3.30, p = 0.0080
7. Creatinine (feature [141], m/z 112.0519; HMDB00562, KEGG C00791) — beta = +56.79, SE 18.15, t = 3.13, p = 0.011
8. D-Malic acid (TCA cycle; HMDB00156, KEGG C00149) — beta = +62.81, SE 20.48, t = 3.07, p = 0.012
9. Deoxycholic acid 3-glucuronide (feature [412]; HMDB02596, KEGG C03033) — beta = +12.51, SE 4.16, t = 3.01, p = 0.013
10. Acetylcarnosine (feature [166], m/z 267.1104; HMDB12881) — beta = +24.02, SE 8.73, t = 2.75, p = 0.020

Bread-spiker definition used: per-subject mean of (per-meal peak post-meal CGM glucose minus mean pre-meal baseline, t = -25..0 min) over replicate PLAIN bread meals (mitigator NA); cohort median of that mean = 56.46 mg/dL across the 37 subjects with plain-bread meals (67 meals; 16 mitigated bread meals excluded); 18 subjects were above median, 14 of whom have metabolomics data and complete age/BMI/SBP (SBP 91.0-146.0 mm Hg, mean 119.8; age 25.2-79.0; BMI 20.7-34.4).

Next in line beyond the top 10 (also beta > 0, p < 0.05): Citrulline (p = 0.021), Acetylcholine (p = 0.022), hydroxybutyrylcarnitine C4:0,OH (p = 0.023), chenodeoxycholic acid 24-acyl-beta-D-glucuronide (p = 0.025), acetylcarnosine 2nd feature (p = 0.025), linoleylcarnitine C18:2 AC (p = 0.027), Proline 2nd feature (p = 0.037), Homoarginine (p = 0.039), Valine (p = 0.042), CAR 18:2 (p = 0.044), Thyroxine (p = 0.044). In total 21/435 metabolites passed beta > 0 & p < 0.05; 16 additional metabolites were significant in the negative direction and were excluded by the direction criterion.

Key caveats:
- NO metabolite survives Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across the 435 tests (minimum q = 0.180); all findings are nominally significant only, and 21/435 (4.8%) passing p<0.05 is close to the 5% type-I rate expected under a global null.
- n = 14 (10 residual df per model): ranks 1-4 (Proline, Asp-Arg, Kynurenic acid, Pro-Phe) are stable across scale (log2 vs raw), replicate aggregation (mean vs median) and also significant in the full metabolomics cohort (n = 35); ranks 5-10 are preprocessing-sensitive.
- Specificity to the bread-spiker phenotype is NOT statistically demonstrated: a metabolite x spiker-group interaction test (n = 26) gives minimum BH q = 0.895, so these are SBP associations observable within bread-spikers, not proven bread-spiker-specific effects.
- 4 of the 18 classified bread-spikers (XB16, XB19, XB48, XB69) have no metabolomics data and could not be tested; only 38 of the 74 cohort participants have metabolomics at all.
- Associations are cross-sectional and adjusted only for age and BMI (not sex, medications, or renal function); creatinine in particular most plausibly reflects renal filtration/hemodynamic covariation rather than a causal BP mechanism.
- "Hypertension-associated" is operationalized as a positive association with continuous systolic BP; the dataset contains no hypertension diagnosis variable.

Analysis trace: ./trace.md. Full result tables and the reproducible pipeline: da81-sbp-metabolites/ (scripts/run_analysis.py, scripts/make_figure.py, output/tables/, output/figures/, README.md).
da-8-1.notes: The agent performed a rigorous and transparent analysis; most computational steps satisfy top-level criteria. Docking levels in criteria 5 and 8 is due to omission of R-squared extraction/reporting and incomplete statistics for all passing metabolites, respectively, not methodological errors.

da-8-2.answer:
FINAL ANSWER — DA-8-2: Interaction effect size between baseline insulin resistance status and peak glucose reduction (protein vs fiber preloaded rice challenges)

Setup
- Data: CGM traces for rice challenges (Rice, Rice+Protein, Rice+Fiber); 167 traces, 38 subjects; 23 subjects completed BOTH Rice+Protein and Rice+Fiber (42 and 43 replicate traces averaged per subject/condition).
- Outcome: peak glucose increment above each trace's own pre-load baseline (mean glucose over -25 to 0 min; peak over 0-170 min).
- Insulin resistance (IR) status: HOMA-IR = fasting glucose (mg/dL) x fasting insulin (uU/mL)/405; IR+ defined as HOMA-IR >= 2.5 (6 IR+, 17 IR-; fasting labs complete in all 23).
- Contrast: (Protein - Fiber) peak increment within subject; "peak glucose reduction protein vs fiber" is the negative of this contrast.

Primary result (2x2 interaction)
- 2x2 cell means of peak increment (mg/dL, mean +/- SD):
  IR-: Fiber 54.96 +/- 32.76, Protein 52.03 +/- 26.06
  IR+: Fiber 81.79 +/- 29.25, Protein 77.05 +/- 23.77
- Interaction (difference-in-differences) = -4.74 - (-2.93) = -1.81 mg/dL
  i.e., IR+ subjects' protein-vs-fiber peak-increment advantage is only 1.81 mg/dL larger (more negative) than in IR- subjects.
- OLS ipeak ~ preload*IR: interaction beta = -1.81 mg/dL (95% CI -41.0 to +37.4; SE 19.43), t = -0.09, p = 0.926.
- Effect sizes: Cohen's d = -0.096; Hedges g = -0.093; partial eta^2 = 0.0002 (Type-II ANOVA F = 0.009, p = 0.926); two-sample t(21) = -0.20, p = 0.841; Mann-Whitney p = 0.919; permutation test (20,000 resamples) p = 0.840.
- Replicate-level cluster-robust model (85 traces, 23 subjects): interaction beta = 0.73 (SE 7.69), p = 0.924 (consistent null).

Context
- Main preload effect (Protein vs Fiber) on peak increment: -3.40 mg/dL (protein blunts slightly more), t(22) = -0.89, p = 0.383, paired dz = -0.186.
- Main effect of IR status on peak increment: IR+ ~ +26.8 mg/dL higher than IR- (p = 0.058) — IR subjects spike higher overall, but the protein-vs-fiber differential is not modified by IR status.

Sensitivity (interaction effect size under alternative IR definitions)
- HOMA-IR >= 2.0 (8/15): DiD = +4.10 mg/dL, d = +0.22, p = 0.621
- HOMA-IR median split >= 1.37 (12/11): DiD = +8.91 mg/dL, d = +0.49, p = 0.254
- SSPG >= 148.5, 75th pct (4/19): DiD = +22.32 mg/dL, d = +1.35, p = 0.023 (only nominally significant cell; 4 subjects, post hoc)
- Continuous HOMA-IR interaction: beta = +1.81 mg/dL per HOMA-IR unit (SE 5.82), p = 0.757 (r = 0.154)
- Continuous SSPG interaction: beta = +0.118 mg/dL per SSPG unit (SE 0.146), p = 0.426 (r = 0.446, p = 0.055, n = 19)
- Raw peak outcome (not baseline-adjusted): interaction beta = 0.46 (SE 26.5), p = 0.986

Conclusion
The interaction effect size between baseline insulin-resistance status and the magnitude of peak glucose reduction (protein-preload vs fiber-preload rice meals) is essentially ZERO and not statistically significant: standardized effect size d = -0.10 (Hedges g = -0.09; partial eta^2 = 0.0002), unstandardized interaction beta = -1.81 mg/dL (95% CI -41 to +37), p ~ 0.84-0.93. Baseline insulin resistance strongly predicts higher peak glucose increments overall, but it does not significantly modify the relative peak-lowering benefit of a protein preload versus a fiber preload in this dataset. Only a post hoc SSPG-high subgroup (n = 4) hints that the most insulin-resistant individuals might benefit relatively more from protein (d = 1.35, p = 0.023), which should be treated as hypothesis-generating. Main limitation: only 23 participants (6 IR+) completed both preload arms; the confidence interval cannot exclude moderate interactions.
da-8-2.notes: The agent's peak metric computation and two-way ANOVA execution are sound, but primary IR classification and the reduction contrast direction deviate from the rubric.

da-8-3.answer:
FINAL ANSWER — Task DA-8-3 (Individual Variations in Glycemic Responses)

BACKGROUND / METHOD IN ONE PARAGRAPH
The spiker labels are not shipped in data_meta.csv, so they were reconstructed from the CGM data:
per (participant, food, replicate) curve, baseline = mean glucose over minutes -25..-5 and iAUC =
incremental 0-120 min area above baseline; replicates averaged; each food's iAUC standardized
across the 38 CGM participants; a participant is an "X-spiker" when that food's z-iAUC >= +0.5 SD.
This yields 6 potato-spikers with omics data (XB21, XB38, XB42, XB70, XB94, XB111) and 4
grape-spikers (XB33, XB79, XB100, XB115). Metabolite abundances were log2-transformed, replicates
averaged to subject level, and each of the 974 metabolites tested by Welch t-test (6 vs 4), with
Mann-Whitney cross-check and BH-FDR (nothing survives FDR at this n; all findings are nominal).

(1) TOP 10 DIFFERENTIALLY ABUNDANT METABOLITES, POTATO-SPIKERS vs GRAPE-SPIKERS
(rank by Welch p, after de-duplicating compound names; log2FC = potato minus grape)

 #  Metabolite                       Direction          log2FC   Welch p   MW p
 1  PC 35:2 [PC(17:0/18:2)]          higher in potato   +0.46    0.0030    0.0095
 2  PC 40:6 [PC(18:0/22:6)]          higher in potato   +0.74    0.0046    0.0190
 3  Ephedrine                        higher in potato   +0.49    0.0056    0.0095
 4  Carnitine                        higher in potato   +0.42    0.0085    0.0095
 5  S-Allylcysteine                  lower in potato    -0.23    0.0175    0.0190
 6  PC 16:0/16:0 (DPPC)              higher in potato   +0.98    0.0188    0.0190
 7  LPC 18:0                         lower in potato    -0.59    0.0203    0.0381
 8  LPC P-18:0 or LPC O-18:1         lower in potato    -0.60    0.0225    0.0095
 9  2-Pyrrolidinone-5-carboxylic acid higher in potato  +0.29    0.0246    0.0190
10  3-Acetyl-11-keto-beta-boswellic acid lower in potato -0.75    0.0268    0.0381

Pattern: potato-spikers show higher diacyl phosphatidylcholines (PC 35:2, PC 40:6, PC 16:0/16:0)
plus higher free carnitine, whereas grape-spikers show higher lysophosphatidylcholines
(LPC 18:0, LPC P-18:0/O-18:1) — i.e. an elevated PC/LPC ratio in potato-spikers. Six of the ten
(PC 35:2, PC 40:6, Carnitine, PC 16:0/16:0, LPC 18:0, LPC P-18:0/O-18:1) are lipid species.

(2) LIPID SPECIES MEDIATING INSULIN RESISTANCE / BETA-CELL DIFFERENCES
Mediation model: X = spiker group (potato=1, grape=0); M = lipid species (lipidomics measurement
at subject level, log2); Y = SSPG or HOMA-IR (insulin resistance) or DI or IE (beta-cell
function). Indirect effect a*b with Sobel test and 10,000-resample bootstrap percentile CIs.

 -> STATISTICALLY SIGNIFICANT MEDIATOR (bootstrap 95% CI for a*b excludes 0, stable across seeds):
    PC(18:0/22:6) — the lipidomics species corresponding to metabolomics feature "PC 40:6".
       * HOMA-IR:  a = +0.68 (p=0.037), b = -2.80, indirect a*b = -1.90, 95% CI [-4.75, -0.19]
       * IE (insulin efficiency): a = +0.64 (p=0.068), b = +36.3, indirect a*b = +23.2,
         95% CI [+4.54, +46.28]
       * SSPG: a*b = -19.7, CI [-108, +93] — NOT significant
       * DI:   a*b = +0.44, CI [-0.37, +1.55] — NOT significant
    Interpretation: potato-spikers have significantly higher PC(18:0/22:6); conditional on group,
    higher PC(18:0/22:6) tracks lower HOMA-IR and higher insulin efficiency, so this lipid acts as
    a suppressor/offsetting pathway (total HOMA-IR effect 0.85 becomes direct 2.75 after
    adjustment) rather than an explanatory pathway. This is the ONLY top-10 lipid species with a
    statistically significant mediated pathway for insulin resistance or beta-cell function.

 -> NOT significant as mediators of the group difference:
    PC(17:0/18:2) ("PC 35:2"), PC(16:0/16:0), LPC(18:0) (both the "LPC 18:0" and the
    "LPC P-18:0 or LPC O-18:1" features): all bootstrap CIs for a*b crossed 0 for every outcome
    (e.g. LPC(18:0)->HOMA-IR a*b = -1.17, CI [-3.60, +0.33]). Notably LPC(18:0) is strongly
    associated with the outcomes themselves across all 38 omics participants (vs SSPG r=-0.46,
    p=0.012; vs HOMA-IR r=-0.34, p=0.044; vs DI r=+0.47, p=0.013) but is not sufficiently
    different between spiker groups to mediate the group contrast (a-path p=0.53 in the
    continuous analysis).

 -> Supporting context: potato-spiking itself is associated with insulin resistance in this cohort
    (potato iAUC z vs SSPG r=+0.57, p=0.005; vs HOMA-IR r=+0.47, p=0.015; vs DI r=-0.33;
    potato-minus-grape contrast vs SSPG r=+0.51, p=0.013, n=23), which is the association the
    mediation analysis decomposes. An unbiased lipidome-wide screen found only two
    bootstrap-significant mediators of SSPG — the free fatty acids FFA(22:1) (a*b=+17.9,
    CI [+3.4, +36.9]) and FFA(16:0) (a*b=+16.9, CI [+3.8, +31.9]) — neither of which is among
    the top-10 metabolites.

CAVEATS (important)
 * Very small groups (6 potato vs 4 grape spikers with omics; 5 vs 4 with SSPG/DI). No metabolite
   survives BH-FDR (min q=0.88); the top-10 list and both significant mediations are
   nominal-p, hypothesis-generating results.
 * Spiker labels were reconstructed from CGM (cohort-z iAUC >= +0.5 SD); other defensible rules
   (argmax of iAUC, within-person z, rank-based) give different memberships — under argmax the
   grape-spikers have no omics data at all.
 * Statistical mediation only; cross-sectional fasting samples cannot establish causality or
   temporal order, and confounders (BMI, sex, diet pattern) could not be adjusted at n=10.
 * "PC 35:2"/"PC 40:6" are sum-composition assignments mapped to the only matching species in the
   lipidomics panel (PC(17:0/18:2), PC(18:0/22:6)); the ether LPC feature maps ambiguously to
   LPC(18:0).
da-8-3.notes: The analysis is technically sophisticated and well-documented, but deviations from the rubric's specific spiker-classification method, incomplete phenotype correlation coverage, and lack of per-metabolite FDR reporting prevent full marks on several criteria.

da-9-1.answer:
ANSWER — Baseline circulating T cell populations associated with 1-year overall survival in patients receiving nivo/chemo (anti-PD-1 nivolumab + gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel), PRINCE/PICI0002 phase-2 trial.

COHORT: Of 108 randomized patients, 36 were as-treated with nivolumab + chemo without the CD40 agonist (Actual Arm A1; all Efficacy Population). 27 of these had baseline (C1D1) CyTOF and formed the analysis set (16 deaths; 4 censored before 1 year at days 43/43/163/213). Median OS 467 days; Kaplan-Meier 1-year OS = 0.61. Baseline T-cell markers were tested by univariate/adjusted Cox regression (continuous, per +1 SD), median-split log-rank with KM 1-year OS, tertile dose-response, and alive-at-1-year logistic regression, with BH-FDR control across 7 tested populations.

FINDINGS (ranked; better 1-year OS unless stated):

1) Tbet+ TCRgd+ T cells (% of TCRgd T cells) - strongest overall. Higher baseline = better OS.
   Cox HR per +1 SD = 0.36 (95% CI 0.20-0.67), p = 0.0012, BH q = 0.008; adjusted for age, ECOG, prior chemo HR = 0.34 (0.18-0.64), p = 0.0008. Median split (cut 0.792): 1-year OS 90% (n=13, only 1 death within 1 year) vs 38% (n=14, 8 deaths), log-rank p = 0.007, hi-vs-lo HR 0.24 (0.08-0.74); tertiles 38% -> 63% -> 86%. Retains independent significance in a 4-marker multivariable Cox (HR 0.40, p = 0.017; model C-index 0.78). Also significant in the randomized-A1 set (p = 0.0007) and pooled nivolumab-receiving set (HR 0.63, p = 0.008), but equally strong in the no-nivolumab (sotigalimab/chemo) arm (HR 0.33, p = 0.0001) - i.e., it behaves as a PROGNOSTIC marker of survival irrespective of PD-1 blockade (innate-like cytotoxic gd T-cell fitness).

2) NKT cells (% of leukocytes) - best 1-year separation and the most PD-1-relevant signal.
   Cox HR per +1 SD = 0.42 (0.20-0.90), p = 0.026; adjusted HR = 0.21 (0.07-0.59), p = 0.0029. Median split (cut 0.0164): 1-year OS 90% vs 38%, log-rank p = 0.0036 (BH q = 0.023), hi-vs-lo HR 0.21 (0.07-0.66); tertiles 33% -> 62% -> 100% (zero 1-year deaths in the top tertile). Alive-at-1-year OR = 16.1 per +1 SD (p = 0.056, n = 23 evaluable). Independent in the multivariable model (HR 0.23, p = 0.043). Holds in pooled nivolumab-receiving patients (HR 0.42 median-split, p = 0.013) but is NULL in the no-nivolumab arm (HR 1.04, p = 0.88), consistent with an association more specific to PD-1-blockade-containing treatment (formal interaction test underpowered, p = 0.22).

3) Tbet+ T cells (% of CD3+) - supportive, same direction (higher = better): continuous HR 0.57 (0.30-1.09), p = 0.091; median-split log-rank p = 0.0097 with 1-year OS 81% vs 46%; tertiles 33% -> 75% -> 83%; adjusted p = 0.079. Not independent of NKT (r = 0.78) in multivariable analysis.

4) Ki-67+ T cells (% of CD3+) - RISK marker (higher = worse 1-year OS): continuous HR 1.68 (0.89-3.17), p = 0.11; median-split log-rank p = 0.031, 1-year OS 33% (hi) vs 91% (lo); top quartile HR 10.7 (p = 0.009), 6/7 patients dead within 1 year; adjusted HR 2.32 (1.02-5.32), p = 0.046. Strongly inversely correlated with NKT (r = -0.81). Null in the no-nivolumab arm.

NULL (no baseline association in this arm): HLA-DR+ T cells (% of leukocytes) p = 0.21; HLA-DR+ non-naive CD4 T cells p = 0.42; HLA-DR+ non-naive CD8 T cells p = 0.40 - baseline activated (HLA-DR+) or non-naive CD4/CD8 abundance does not stratify 1-year OS here.

INTERPRETATION: Under nivo/chemo for metastatic pancreatic cancer, a baseline peripheral T-cell compartment enriched for innate-like effector lineage cells (NKT, Tbet+ T cells, Tbet+ gd T cells) accompanies markedly better 1-year survival, whereas a high fraction of cycling Ki-67+ T cells accompanies poor 1-year survival. NKT and Ki-67+ T cells look more nivolumab-specific; Tbet+ gd T cells look generally prognostic (also predictive of OS in the CD40-agonist arm).

LIMITATIONS: single-arm subgroup, n = 27 with 16 events and 9 one-year deaths; hypothesis-generating associative biomarkers only, no external validation; predictive-vs-prognostic cannot be formally distinguished (interaction tests n.s. at n = 80); 4/27 censored before 1 year add classification uncertainty (results directionally stable when counted as failures); the dataset lacks total CD3/CD4/CD8/Treg frequencies and any on-treatment measurement of the Tbet/Ki-67/NKT/TCRgd panel; unmeasured confounders (disease burden, CA19-9, steroids, lines of therapy) cannot be adjusted for.
da-9-1.notes: The agent performed a thorough and mostly accurate analysis, loading and filtering correctly, selecting T-cell features, and applying survival methodology. The only notable deficiency is that the reported log-rank p-values differ from expected due to using >/< median split rather than >=/<, so full marks are not warranted on results accuracy.

da-9-7.answer:
ANSWER (DA-9-7): Do circulating immune-cell frequencies correlate with serum protein levels on-treatment at C2D1 in the PRINCE trial?

SHORT ANSWER: No — at C2D1 there is no statistically significant cross-platform correlation between circulating immune-cell frequencies (CyTOF) and serum protein levels (Olink) after multiple-testing correction. The only notable trend is a modest INVERSE association between the frequency of CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells and the IFN-gamma-inducible chemokines CXCL9 and CXCL10, which does not survive FDR correction.

ANALYSIS SET
- The two platforms share 73 patients with paired C2D1 samples (CyTOF 75 samples/73 patients; Olink 90 samples/90 patients; overlap 73).
- Critically, at C2D1 the dataset contains only 4 of 16 CyTOF cell-population labels (Conventional DC, CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells, HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD4 T Cells, HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD8 T Cells) and only 4 of 30 Olink proteins (CXCL9, CXCL10, IFN-gamma, Soluble PD-1). The remaining analytes are baseline-only (C1D1/C1D15), and the CyTOF MSI epitote file is C1D15-only. The question is therefore answerable for 16 testable pairs.
- After de-duplicating 303 technical replicate Olink rows (IL-10/IL-6/LAMP3, C1D1 only) and averaging the 2 patients with duplicate C2D1 CyTOF aliquots, the merged C2D1 matrix is 73 patients x 8 analytes (n=65 pairs for B-cell/T-cell rows, n=73 for Conventional DC rows).

PRIMARY RESULT (Spearman rank correlation, pairwise-complete, BH-FDR over 16 tests)
- CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells vs CXCL9: rho = -0.233, 95% CI [-0.451, +0.011], p = 0.062, q = 0.535 (n=65)
- CCR7+ CD11b+ CD27- B cells vs CXCL10: rho = -0.222, 95% CI [-0.442, +0.023], p = 0.076, q = 0.535 (n=65)
- All other 14 pairs: |rho| <= 0.164, p >= 0.19 (e.g., HLA-DR+ Non-Naive CD8 T cells vs Soluble PD-1 rho = +0.164, p = 0.19; Conventional DC vs Soluble PD-1 rho = -0.152, p = 0.20)
- NO pair is significant at nominal p < 0.05 or BH q < 0.05 (minimum q = 0.535).

SENSITIVITY ANALYSES (all support the null)
1) log10-log10 Pearson: same pattern (B cells x CXCL9 r = -0.265, p = 0.033, q = 0.42; all q >= 0.42).
2) Arm-stratified (A1 GEM/NP/nivolumab, B2 GEM/NP/sotigalimab, C2 triple): B-cell x CXCL9 direction consistent in all three arms (rho = -0.138 / -0.330 / -0.399), none individually significant at n = 21-23.
3) Arm-adjusted partial Spearman: B cells x CXCL9 rho = -0.273 (p = 0.028); B cells x CXCL10 rho = -0.213 (p = 0.088) — the trend is not arm-driven but still fails multiplicity correction.
4) Paired C1D1 -> C2D1 change analysis (n = 53-54 cross-platform): no correlation between on-treatment changes in cell frequencies and protein changes (all |rho| <= 0.13, q >= 0.95). The proteins themselves rise on treatment (median dNPX, Wilcoxon: Soluble PD-1 +1.04, p = 7.7e-9; IFN-gamma +0.95, p = 1.7e-5; CXCL10 +0.27, p = 7.7e-4; CXCL9 +0.16, p = 0.031; n = 71) while the paired cell populations do not shift (all p >= 0.14, n = 54).
5) Baseline benchmark at C1D1 (78 patients, 364 testable pairs from 13 populations x 28 proteins): the same pipeline DOES detect cross-platform structure — HLA-DR+ T cells x IL-8 (rho = -0.433, q = 0.030) and Tbet+ T cells x IL-8 (rho = -0.413, q = 0.035), with a near-threshold myeloid-suppression cluster (CD14+ HLA-DRlo m-MDSC x IL-10 rho = +0.406, q = 0.052; m-MDSC x CAH9; HLA-DR+ T x HGF; NKT x HCLS1). Those analytes are absent at C2D1 in this dataset.

INTERPRETATION
- For the analytes measurable at C2D1, circulating cell frequencies and serum proteins vary largely independently across patients on treatment; the on-treatment IFN-gamma/PD-1 proteomic response is not mirrored by (or correlated with) the four on-treatment CyTOF populations.
- The B-cell x CXCL9/CXCL10 inverse trend is biologically coherent (CXCL9/CXCL10 are myeloid-derived IFN-gamma-inducible CXCR3 ligands, so an inverse relation with a circulating activated/terminally-differentiated B-cell subset is plausible) and direction-consistent across arms, but with n = 65 it remains a hypothesis-generating signal, not a validated correlation.

LIMITATIONS
- The C2D1 conclusion covers only 4 cell populations x 4 proteins; the trial's MDSC, pDC, Ki-67+ T, Tbet+ T, NKT populations and 24 additional serum proteins are simply not present at C2D1 in this data release, so nothing can be said about them on-treatment.
- Power: with n = 65-73, only correlations of roughly |rho| >= 0.35 would be detected reliably; moderate true correlations could be missed.
- Cross-sectional correlation cannot establish causality or mechanism; arm adjustment cannot remove all treatment-related heterogeneity.
- Baseline (C1D1) findings quoted as context are themselves exploratory (364 tests) and would need independent validation.

Files: full trace in trace.md; grids and merged matrix in outputs/ (c2d1_spearman_grid.csv, c2d1_logpearson_grid.csv, c2d1_delta_spearman_grid.csv, c1d1_spearman_grid.csv, c2d1_merged_matrix.csv); figures c2d1_correlation_heatmap.png and c2d1_toppair_scatter.png.
da-9-7.notes: The analysis is largely solid but deviates from the expected feature set and per-arm FDR, missing the Arm C2 finding.

da-10-1.answer:
DA-10-1 FINAL ANSWER
ML screening of membraneless-organelle participants: amino-acid composition of PS-Self (SaPS) vs PS-Part (PdPS) proteins, and benchmark of phase-separation predictors against non-PS (NoPS) proteins.

DATA
sequence_prediction_filtered.xlsx: 48,504 proteins x 23 columns (UniProt index, Organism, Sequence, scores for catGRANULE / PLAAC / PScore, SaPS-8fea / PdPS-8fea / SaPS-10fea / PdPS-10fea classifier probabilities, and 0/1 labels SaPS / hSaPS / PdPS / hPdPS / NoPS / hNoPS). idr_ranges.xlsx: 55,056 IDR segments for 24,451 proteins (UniProt, start, end). Set sizes used: SaPS 128 (58 human), PdPS 214 (93 human), NoPS 48,158 (8,799 human), hSaPS 59, hPdPS 96, hNoPS 8,799; labels mutually exclusive, 4 unlabelled rows excluded. NO FUZDROP SCORES EXIST in the provided data and FuzDrop cannot be installed or reached from this environment (no PyPI package, web server DNS-unreachable); the task rules forbid consulting the source paper. FuzDrop is therefore reported as NOT EVALUABLE; no number below is attributed to it. The dataset's own SaPS/PdPS 8- and 10-feature ML classifiers were analysed as surrogates/comparators (clearly not FuzDrop).

PART 1 - AMINO-ACID COMPOSITION: PS-SELF vs PS-PART
Method: pooled residue fractions per set; per-protein Mann-Whitney U per amino acid; Benjamini-Hochberg FDR over 20 tests; replicated in the human-only sets.

PS-Self (SaPS) are significantly enriched (BH q < 0.05, pan-species) in: Gly (8.88% vs 6.40%, log2FC +0.47), Pro (7.33% vs 6.24%, +0.23), Thr (6.49% vs 5.36%, +0.28, q=0.052), Ser (10.28% vs 9.13%, +0.17), Gln (+0.12); grouped Gly+Pro 16.2% vs 12.6% (p<1e-4) and polar STNQ 27.1% vs 24.0% (p<1e-4).
PS-Part (PdPS) are significantly enriched in: Cys (1.36% vs 0.91%, log2FC -0.57 for SaPS/PdPS), Ile (-0.28), Leu (-0.26), Glu (-0.25), Lys (-0.23), Arg (-0.22), His (-0.22), Asp (-0.15), Val (-0.11); grouped acidic DE 12.7% vs 11.1% (p<1e-4), basic KR 12.4% vs 10.6% (p<1e-4), hydrophobic LIVAM 28.2% vs 25.6% (p<1e-4). Aromatic FYW does not differ (6.6% vs 6.4%, p=0.40).
Human-only replication (hSaPS 59 vs hPdPS 96): same directions for all |log2FC|>0.1 residues - G +0.37 (q<1e-4), P +0.41 (q=3e-4), Q +0.14 (q=0.019), K -0.25 (q=5e-4), E -0.19 (q=0.008), L -0.20 (q=2e-4), I -0.31 (q=1e-4), V -0.09 (q=0.029); Cys and His lose significance at this smaller n.
Against NoPS: BOTH PS classes are Cys-depleted (SaPS/NoPS log2FC -1.10; PdPS/NoPS -0.53; both q<1e-4) and depleted of bulky hydrophobics/aromatics (W -0.71/-0.58; L -0.42/-0.16; I -0.41/-0.13) and enriched in Pro/Q/Ser; but the Gly enrichment (+0.53) is specific to PS-Self (PdPS vs NoPS Gly p=0.83), whereas significant D/E/K/R enrichment vs NoPS is specific to PS-Part (all p<=3e-2, three of them <1e-4).
Disorder: mean annotated IDR fraction SaPS 0.311 > PdPS 0.216 > NoPS 0.110 (human 0.326 / 0.267 / 0.138); >=1 IDR in 90.6% / 81.3% / 50.1% (human 94.9 / 84.4 / 58.4%).
Charge: fraction of charged residues SaPS 0.222 < PdPS 0.261 (MWU p=7.95e-08), but net charge per residue does not differ (p=0.25) - PS-Part carries MORE charge while staying net-neutral; PS-Self is weakly charged.
Interpretation: PS-Self proteins carry the classic self-assembling low-complexity signature (Gly/Ser/Pro/Thr/Gln-rich, Cys-poor, weakly charged, highly disordered) consistent with sticker-spacer self-multivalency; PS-Part proteins are compositionally intermediate toward non-PS proteins - disordered but more hydrophobic (L/I/V) and more strongly charged (K/E/D/R), i.e. they look like ordinary binding proteins carrying partner-interaction motifs, consistent with partner-dependent condensation. Examples (top PScore per class; genes from UniProt): PS-Self TAF15 (18.5), HNRNPDL (16.8), HNRNPA3 (15.7), PRNP (12.9), CIRBP (10.8); PS-Part DDX3X (7.9), SFPQ (7.7), RBMX (6.9), TRA2B (6.9), CAPRIN1 (6.8).

PART 2 - PREDICTOR PERFORMANCE (distinguishing each PS type from non-PS)
Method: ROC-AUC with 2,000-resample bootstrap 95% CI, PR-AUC with prevalence, sensitivity/specificity/PPV at published operating thresholds (PScore >= 4, PLAAC > 0, catGRANULE > 0, classifiers >= 0.5), Mann-Whitney p, Youden-optimal thresholds, IDR-matched-negative sensitivity analysis, IDR-fraction-only naive baseline.

Human benchmark (positives vs hNoPS n=8,799):
- hSaPS (n=59) vs hNoPS: PLAAC AUC 0.831 (0.764-0.894), catGRANULE 0.814 (0.761-0.865), PScore 0.813 (0.754-0.871); at published thresholds PScore>=4: sens 0.424/spec 0.954/PPV 0.064 (8.7x enrichment); PLAAC>0: 0.593/0.926/0.051 (7.6x); catGRANULE>0: 0.966/0.385/0.010 (1.6x). PR-AUC 0.12-0.13 at 0.7% prevalence.
- hPdPS (n=96) vs hNoPS: catGRANULE 0.726 (0.676-0.773), PScore 0.689 (0.636-0.742), PLAAC 0.639 (0.567-0.698); PScore>=4 detects only 19.6% of PdPS (spec 0.954, PPV 0.047, 4.1x); catGRANULE>0 sens 0.875 but spec 0.385 (1.4x enrichment).
- Every published predictor ranks hSaPS significantly above hPdPS (median PScore 3.24 vs 1.98, p=6.8e-04; PLAAC 0.13 vs -0.13, p=1.4e-06; catGRANULE 0.97 vs 0.70, p=7.8e-03); hSaPS vs hPdPS AUCs: PLAAC 0.731, PScore 0.664, catGRANULE 0.628.
- Pan-species replication (SaPS 128 / PdPS 214 / NoPS 48,158): SaPS-vs-NoPS AUC PScore 0.831, PLAAC 0.834, catGRANULE 0.817; PdPS-vs-NoPS 0.663 / 0.644 / 0.706; SaPS-vs-PdPS 0.702 / 0.719 / 0.665.
- Dataset ML classifiers (surrogate for sequence-feature propensity models; likely trained on these labels, so optimistic): SaPS-8fea AUC 0.987 and SaPS-10fea 0.990 for SaPS vs NoPS; PdPS-8fea 0.984 and PdPS-10fea 0.990 for PdPS vs NoPS; cross-type SaPS-8fea separates SaPS from PdPS at AUC 0.918 while PdPS-8fea is anti-correlated (AUC 0.137), i.e. the two classes are nearly disjoint in feature space.
- Youden-optimal cuts (human): PScore 2.12 (hSaPS sens 0.746/spec 0.780), 1.54 (hPdPS 0.620/0.664); PLAAC -0.068 / -0.133; catGRANULE 0.771 / 0.369.
Robustness: restricting negatives to proteins with >=1 IDR lowers AUCs modestly and preserves the ordering (hSaPS: PLAAC 0.790, PScore 0.755, catGRANULE 0.763; hPdPS: catGRANULE 0.695, PScore 0.655, PLAAC 0.613). A naive baseline using only annotated IDR fraction achieves AUC 0.779 (hSaPS) and 0.689 (hPdPS), i.e. most of the published predictors' discrimination is disorder content; the type-specific ML classifiers add ~0.2 AUC beyond disorder (Spearman rho with IDR fraction only 0.36-0.56).

BOTTOM LINE
1) PS-Self and PS-Part proteins differ compositionally, not just in mechanism: PS-Self is Gly/Pro/Ser/Thr(Gln)-rich, Cys-poor, weakly charged and the most disordered; PS-Part is more hydrophobic (L/I/V) and more strongly charged (K/E/D/R) with higher charged-residue fraction but unchanged net charge, sitting between PS-Self and non-PS proteins. Gly enrichment and Cys depletion are the sharpest single-residue discriminators (log2FC +0.47 and -0.57 between the two PS classes).
2) All three evaluated published predictors (PScore, PLAAC, catGRANULE) discriminate PS-Self from non-PS well (AUC 0.81-0.83 human, 0.82-0.83 pan-species) but discriminate PS-Part substantially worse (AUC 0.64-0.73), and all three systematically score PS-Self above PS-Part (p <= 7.8e-03). At the canonical PScore >= 4 cut, ~42% of PS-Self but only ~20% of PS-Part proteins are detected. Absolute PPVs stay low (<= 6%) because positives are rare (0.7-1.1% prevalence).
3) FuzDrop could not be evaluated: no FuzDrop scores are present in the provided files, no installable implementation exists, and its server is unreachable; per task rules the source paper was not consulted. The dataset's own SaPS/PdPS ML classifiers (0.98-0.99 AUC, likely optimistically biased by training-set overlap) show that the self- vs partner-dependent distinction is learnable from sequence features and is nearly symmetric-disjoint, far exceeding the published predictors' 0.63-0.73 AUC for that contrast.
4) Limitations: predictor benchmarking partly measures disorder (IDR fraction alone gives AUC 0.78/0.69); NoPS is "not observed to phase-separate", not "cannot"; the ML classifiers' near-perfect AUCs are likely circular; human-only sets are small (59/96 positives, AUC CIs ~0.10 wide); whole-sequence pooling dilutes low-complexity regions.

Full methods, code, intermediate counts and references: trace.md. Figure: outputs/fig1_composition_predictors.png. Tables: analysis/*.csv. Scripts: analysis/step1_composition.py, step2_predictors.py, step3_figures.py.
da-10-1.notes: The agent performed a mostly thorough analysis with correct data loading, set construction, composition computation, AUC evaluation, and summary, but missed IDR-based amino-acid ordering entirely and did not fully replicate fold-change versus NoPS on human sets.

da-10-3.answer:
FINAL ANSWER — ML screening of membraneless organelle (MLO) participants (DA-10-3)

Question: do phase-separation (PS) predictors screen MLO participant datasets consistently better than membrane-bound organelle control datasets, against a fixed non-PS background?

VERDICT: YES in aggregate — every predictor performs better on (nearly) every MLO dataset than on the membrane-bound control, and on the membrane-bound control itself the predictors are at or BELOW chance. The consistency is strong across datasets but NOT across predictors: individual predictors differ widely and several are near chance on specific MLO sets.

SETUP
- Analysis frame: 20,375 human proteins with predictor scores from sequence_prediction.xlsx (catGRANULE, PLAAC, PScore, SaPS-8fea, PdPS-8fea) joined to DeepPhase and class flags (hSaPS 59, hPdPS 96, hNoPS 8,801) from h_combined_with_flags.xlsx and to the six 0/1 dataset flags from List_of_proteins_for_comparing_MLO_enrichment.xlsx (header on row 2; Original data sheet).
- Negative/background = hNoPS (the fixed "hNoPS-test" set), n=8,799 with complete catGRANULE/SaPS-8fea/PdPS-8fea (8,655 PLAAC, 7,970 PScore, 5,202 DeepPhase).
- Positives: OpenCell nuclear punctae 140, DACT1-particulate proteome 264, G3BP1 proximity labeling 285, PhaSepDB high-throughput 1,866, Amyloid fiber-forming 68 (5 MLO/particulate datasets); membrane-bound control = Proteomics of human mitochondri 1,125. Metric: ROC-AUC + AUPRC + one-sided Mann-Whitney p, bootstrap 95% CI (2,000 resamples), plus fold enrichment above the hNoPS 99th/95th percentile.

MAIN RESULTS (ROC-AUC vs hNoPS, Original data sheet)
                  OpenCell  DACT1  G3BP1  PhaSepDB  Amyloid | Mito(control)
PLAAC               0.551   0.353  0.510   0.517    0.453  | 0.433
PScore              0.572   0.423  0.486   0.540    0.514  | 0.422
catGRANULE          0.607   0.641  0.739   0.686    0.515  | 0.523
DeepPhase           0.602   0.536  0.487   0.615    0.522  | 0.479
SaPS-8fea           0.705   0.648  0.669   0.670    0.509  | 0.469
PdPS-8fea           0.732   0.680  0.675   0.696    0.546  | 0.477

1) MLO vs membrane-bound control (paired comparison)
- 28 of 30 (dataset x predictor) pairs have MLO AUC > mitochondrial AUC; exact sign test p = 4.3e-07; Wilcoxon signed-rank p = 1.0e-07; median delta AUC = +0.117 (mean +0.113).
- Per predictor (MLO mean AUC vs mito AUC; wins/5 MLO datasets, exact sign test):
  PdPS-8fea 0.666 vs 0.477 (5/5, p=.031); SaPS-8fea 0.640 vs 0.469 (5/5, p=.031); catGRANULE 0.637 vs 0.523 (4/5, p=.19, loses only Amyloid); DeepPhase 0.552 vs 0.479 (5/5, p=.031); PScore 0.507 vs 0.422 (5/5, p=.031); PLAAC 0.477 vs 0.433 (4/5, p=.19, loses only DACT1).
- Per-dataset median advantage over the control: OpenCell +0.136, G3BP1 +0.137, PhaSepDB +0.149, DACT1 +0.087, Amyloid +0.041.

2) On the membrane-bound (mitochondrial) control the predictors are at or below chance
- PLAAC 0.433, PScore 0.422, SaPS-8fea 0.469, PdPS-8fea 0.477: all significantly BELOW 0.5 (one-sided p >= 0.99 against "greater"); catGRANULE 0.523 is the only one marginally above chance (p=.006); DeepPhase 0.479 (p=.94). Median SaPS-8fea in mitochondrial proteins 0.092 vs hNoPS 0.099 — no enrichment, slight depletion.
- Screening-relevant top-1% fold enrichment (vs hNoPS 99th percentile): MLO datasets 1.9x–11.1x (e.g., PScore x OpenCell 11.1x, PdPS-8fea x G3BP1 10.5x, catGRANULE x Amyloid 10.3x) versus mitochondrial control 0.2x–0.6x (all at or below random expectation). Top-5%: MLO 1.8x–5.6x vs control 0.29x–0.68x.
- Example capture rates above the hNoPS 95th percentile: SaPS-8fea OpenCell 27.9%, PdPS-8fea G3BP1 22.5%, catGRANULE G3BP1 19.3% vs SaPS-8fea mitochondrial 1.6%.

3) Best predictor per dataset differs (predictor consistency is the weak point)
- G3BP1 proximity labeling: catGRANULE best (AUC 0.739, CI 0.713–0.765, p<1e-20); PLAAC/PScore at or below chance (0.510/0.486). PScore and PLAAC are significantly INVERTED on DACT1 (0.423/0.353).
- PhaSepDB high-throughput (n=1,866): PdPS-8fea 0.696 > SaPS-8fea 0.670 ~ catGRANULE 0.686.
- OpenCell nuclear punctae: PdPS-8fea 0.732 > SaPS-8fea 0.705.
- Amyloid fiber-forming (n=68): NO predictor reaches significance (best PdPS-8fea 0.546, p=.097) — the only MLO set with no detectable PS-signal separation, while its top-1% enrichment can still be 9–10x for PScore/SaPS-8fea/catGRANULE.
- The two 8-feature classifiers (SaPS-8fea, PdPS-8fea) dominate overall, but they also separate their own training classes almost perfectly (SaPS-8fea hSaPS-vs-hNoPS AUC 0.987; PdPS-8fea hPdPS-vs-hNoPS AUC 0.984), so part of their MLO advantage is training-class overlap (24–41 PhaSepDB and 8–11 G3BP1 members are curated hSaPS/hPdPS proteins).

4) Robustness
- With the "Training proteins removed" sheet the pattern persists at lower absolute levels: PdPS-8fea MLO mean 0.637 vs mito 0.474 (5/5 datasets), SaPS-8fea 0.607 vs 0.468 (4/5), catGRANULE 0.609 vs 0.522 (4/5), PScore 0.469 vs 0.421 (4/5), PLAAC 0.441 vs 0.432 (3/5), DeepPhase 0.478 vs 0.479 (2/4; its positives drop to 8–35 per dataset).
- Restricting positives to non-background (non-hNoPS) members sharpens the contrast further: catGRANULE 0.663 vs 0.549, DeepPhase 0.662 vs 0.459, SaPS-8fea 0.658 vs 0.480, PdPS-8fea 0.682 vs 0.494 (all 5/5), PScore 0.511 vs 0.428 (4/5), PLAAC 0.472 vs 0.445 (3/5).
- Overlap note: 515 of 1,125 mitochondrial positives and 16–41 MLO positives are themselves flagged hNoPS; this can only depress AUCs and hits the Mito set hardest. When positives are restricted to non-background members the contrast sharpens (e.g., PdPS-8fea 0.682 vs 0.494, SaPS-8fea 0.658 vs 0.480, catGRANULE 0.663 vs 0.549; each winning 5/5 MLO datasets), so the MLO > Mito gap is not an artifact of the self-comparison.

INTERPRETATION
Phase-separation predictor scores are enriched in participants of condensate-type (membraneless) organelle datasets — nuclear puncta, DACT1 particulates, G3BP1-labeled stress-granule neighbors, PhaSepDB high-throughput MLO components — relative to the same fixed non-PS background, while mitochondrial (membrane-bound organelle) proteins are depleted relative to that background. This is the expected signature if the scores capture condensate-forming biophysics (prion-like/low-complexity character, pi-pi contacts, granule propensity) rather than generic "being in a proteomics list" or generic disorder/hydrophobicity: membrane-bound-organelle residents are not enriched for condensation propensity.

LIMITATIONS (what this analysis cannot conclude)
- Only ONE membrane-bound control dataset (human mitochondrial proteome) exists in the data; "membrane-bound controls" generalization rests on n=1 control dataset, and per-predictor sign tests rest on 5 paired datasets.
- The 30-pair p-values are anti-conservative (predictors share datasets and datasets share predictors); the descriptive 28/30 pattern and per-predictor counts carry the argument.
- Correlation only — no mechanistic claim; the Amyloid fiber-forming set (n=68) shows no significant separation by any predictor, so the conclusion does not extend to amyloid-type aggregates.
- PhaSepDB high-throughput mixes many organelles and 706 of its 2,572 members have no human predictor score (86 are Xenopus entries), so its AUC describes the scorable subset only.
- DeepPhase is scored for only 59% of the background and 15–59 positives per dataset; conclusions using it are fragile.
- SaPS-8fea/PdPS-8fea were trained on curated classes that overlap the evaluation lists; the leakage-reduced sheet mitigates but does not remove this circularity.

BOTTOM LINE
Against a fixed non-PS (hNoPS) background, all six predictors screen MLO participant datasets better than the membrane-bound mitochondrial control (28/30 dataset-predictor pairs; median AUC advantage +0.12; sign-test p = 4.3e-07), and on the membrane-bound control they perform at or significantly below chance (AUC 0.42–0.52, top-1% enrichment <= 0.6x). Consistency holds across datasets but not uniformly across predictors: catGRANULE dominates G3BP1 where PLAAC/PScore fail, PdPS-8fea/SaPS-8fea dominate OpenCell/DACT1/PhaSepDB, and no predictor significantly separates the small amyloid fiber-forming set.
da-10-3.notes: The agent performed a comprehensive and methodologically sound screening evaluation, with minor limitations in overlap removal from primary labels and verification of some source citations preventing a perfect score.

da-11-1.answer:
ANSWER — Cell-cell communication between KIR+CD8 T cells and pathogenic (gliadin-specific-like) CD4 T cells in active celiac lesions (GSE193442, 10 duodenal samples: 6 active CeD, 4 healthy controls)

DATA PROCESSED
72,177 raw cells -> QC (300-6,000 genes, >=500 UMIs, <=15% mt) and per-sample Scrublet doublet removal -> 64,567 cells x 18,468 genes. Harmony integration on sample, Leiden clustering. The capture is essentially a T/NK compartment (CD3D+ cells dominate; LYZ, MZB1, COL1A1, EPCAM, MS4A1 all ~0), so all communication reported is T-T.
Populations defined by cell-level gating on detected genes:
- KIR+CD8 T cells: 1,354 cells (752 CeD / 602 HC); 100% CD3D+, 94% CD8A+, 0% TRDC; GZMB 77%, PRF1 84%, GNLY 78%; KIR2DL3 39%, KIR3DL1 38%, KIR3DL2 32%; KLRC2 (NKG2C) 22%, KLRC1 (NKG2A) 11%, LILRB1 17%.
- Activated/pathogenic-like CD4 T cells: CD4+CD3+CD8-TRDC- and HLA-DRA/HLA-DRB1+ (surrogate for gliadin-specific HLA-DQ-restricted effector CD4 clones; no TCR/tetramer data exist in count matrices) = 561 cells (424 CeD / 137 HC).

METHOD
LIANA 1.10 rank-aggregate (CellPhoneDB + Connectome + NATMI + SingleCellSignalR + log2FC consensus; 500 permutations, seed 0) on log-normalised data, using the OmniPath "consensus" resource (4,620 pairs) augmented with 60+ curated KIR/MHC-II/NKG2D/effector pairs that the stock resource lacks; all KIR_CD8 <-> CD4_act/CD4_T directed pairs extracted (613 interactions, 231 non-MHC-I). Independent cell-level evidence: % ligand+ source cells and % receptor+ target cells; Wilcoxon DE (KIR+CD8 vs other CD8, CeD patients).

REFERENCE AXIS CONFIRMED (excluded from the answer by construction)
MHC-I:KIR was the top-scoring axis in the focus set (CD4_act->KIR_CD8 B2M:KLRD1 magnitude_rank 0.0034, B2M:KIR3DL1 0.0051, B2M:KIR2DL3 0.0106 in the CeD-only run), and KIR3DL1 was the most KIR+CD8-enriched gene in CeD (53.7% CeD vs 18.9% HC positive). This validates the pipeline before asking what lies beyond MHC-I.

TOP NON-MHC-I PATHWAYS PREDICTED TO MEDIATE SUPPRESSION AND CYTOTOXIC TARGETING

1) MHC class II (HLA-DP/DR/DQ) : CD4  - KIR+CD8 -> pathogenic CD4
   Ligand prevalence in KIR+CD8 (CeD): HLA-DPA1 61.2%, HLA-DPB1 60.3%, HLA-DRB1 22.5%, HLA-DQB1 10.1%; receptor CD4 on 100% of activated CD4 cells. LIANA magnitude_rank 0.38 (all samples) / 0.45 (CeD-only), CellPhoneDB permutation p < 1e-3. HLA-DPA1 (score 16.1) and HLA-DPB1 (15.9) are among the most highly enriched genes in KIR+CD8 vs other CD8 T cells (BH-adj p ~ 0). Mechanism: MHC-II on the KIR+CD8 cell engages the CD4 co-receptor/TCR complex of the gliadin-reactive CD4 cell - a suppressor-APC-like interaction that complements MHC-I:KIR and provides the antigen-specific interface for the suppressive phenotype seen in vitro.

2) CCL5/CCL4 : CXCR3 (CC-chemokine axis) - KIR+CD8 -> pathogenic CD4
   CCL5 in 98.8% of KIR+CD8 cells (top-5 DE gene, score 32.1), CCL4 in 76.4%; CXCR3 on 17.9% of activated CD4 cells. LIANA magnitude_rank 0.281 (best secreted axis), CellPhoneDB p < 1e-3. Mechanism: positions/recruits CXCR3+ Th1-type gliadin-reactive CD4 cells and stabilises cell-cell contact so that KIR/MHC-II engagement and granule delivery can occur; CCL4 also signals through CCR5.

3) TGFB1 : TGFBR2 - KIR+CD8 -> pathogenic CD4
   TGFB1 in 52.6% of KIR+CD8 cells (DE score 11.6, BH-adj p < 0.01), TGFBR2 on 22.6% of activated CD4 cells; LIANA magnitude_rank 0.488, p < 1e-3. Mechanism: canonical contact-dependent immunosuppression of the target CD4 cell - the strongest classical suppressive cytokine axis detected.

4) CD48 : CD2 and CD58 : CD2 (bidirectional adhesion/costimulation)
   CD48 68.4% / CD58 15.8% on KIR+CD8; CD2 73.1% on activated CD4 (and 60% on KIR+CD8). LIANA magnitude_rank 0.77 (CD48:CD2) and 0.69 (CD58:CD2), p < 1e-3. Mechanism: high-affinity adhesion and costimulatory signalling that builds the immunological synapse between the KIR+CD8 cell and its CD4 target.

5) Cytotoxic execution - perforin/granzyme dominant, death-receptor and NKG2D minor
   GZMB 82.2%, PRF1 91.2%, GNLY 81.3% in KIR+CD8 (CeD), all strongly enriched vs other CD8 T cells (scores 31.4/31.6/31.8); FAS on 17.2% of activated CD4 cells. FASLG (7.3%) and TNFSF10/TRAIL (7.2% vs TNFRSF10B 2.8%) are low; NKG2D (KLRK1) is ~0% on CD4 cells and NKG2D-ligands are rare in KIR+CD8 (MICA 1.6%, MICB 3.6%, ULBP2 0.4%; ULBP1 absent from the gene list), so granzyme-mediated killing of CD4 targets via synapse delivery (assisted by CD48:CD2 adhesion) is the supported cytotoxic route; NKG2D-ligand recognition of CD4 cells is NOT supported.

6) Secondary/supporting signals (reported for completeness)
   - GRN : TNFRSF1A/B (best raw non-MHC magnitude_rank 0.023 but CellPhoneDB p = 0.43-1.0, low lr_means 0.31) - anti-inflammatory/tissue-repair modulation of TNF signalling; not statistically significant after permutation.
   - HLA-E : KLRC1 (NKG2A)/CD94 on the KIR+CD8 cell itself (HLA-E in 99.3% of KIR+CD8, KLRC1 10.8%) and B2M:LILRB1 - inhibitory self-inputs that tune the KIR+CD8 cell's activation threshold rather than acting on the CD4 cell.
   - HLA-DPA1/DPB1 : LAG3 appears only in the CD4_T->KIR_CD8 direction at low rank and was not significant.

DISEASE CONTEXT
Within CeD biopsies the same axes hold with the same ordering (CeD-only run: B2M:KIR3DL1/2DL3 first, then MHC-II:CD4, CCL5:CXCR3). KIR+CD8 cells from CeD patients are more armed than those from controls: PRF1 91.2% vs 75.5%, GZMB 82.2% vs 71.0%, CCL4 76.4% vs 52.3%, KLRC2 27.5% vs 14.6%, LILRB1 20.4% vs 13.2%, KIR3DL1 53.7% vs 18.9%. Population frequencies did not differ (KIR+CD8 1.58% CeD vs 2.37% HC, Mann-Whitney p = 0.61; activated CD4 1.13% vs 0.56%, p = 0.26; n = 6 vs 4).

CONCLUSION
Beyond MHC-I:KIR, the predicted suppressive interface between KIR+CD8 T cells and pathogenic CD4 T cells in active celiac lesions is dominated by (1) MHC class II (HLA-DP > HLA-DR/DQ) on the KIR+CD8 cell engaging CD4, (2) the CCL5/CCL4:CXCR3 chemokine axis that brings the two cells together, (3) TGFB1:TGFBR2 contact-dependent suppression, and (4) CD48/CD58:CD2 synapse adhesion, with (5) perforin/granzyme-B (rather than FASL/TRAIL or NKG2D-ligand) execution of cytotoxic targeting of the CD4 cells.

LIMITATIONS
Count matrices carry no TCR/gliadin-tetramer data, so pathogenic CD4 cells are proxied by HLA-DR+ activated CD4 cells; mRNA is not protein and dissociated biopsies provide no spatial proof of contact; n = 6 vs 4 gives no power for abundance claims; the dataset lacks myeloid/epithelial/B/stromal compartments, so the wider celiac communication network is not modelled; several axes (XCL1:XCR1, IL15:IL2RB, FASLG:FAS, LGALS9:HAVCR2, MICA/B:KLRK1) fell below the 10% expression-prevalence filter and are quantified only at cell level; ULBP1 is absent from the gene list; KIR-gene percentages confound donor KIR genotype with regulation.

Analysis trace with all code, intermediate tables and figure: ./trace.md (module outputs in ced_scRNA/output/tables/, figure ced_scRNA/output/figures/fig_kir_cd4_communication.png).
