da-17-5.answer:
YES — SLE-associated immune-cell changes differ between Asian and European American patients, mainly in MAGNITUDE rather than direction, in this 1.26M-cell PBMC cohort (255 donors analysed: 83 Asian SLE, 23 Asian control, 75 European American SLE, 74 European American control; 1,242,138 cells). Three findings, all donor-level tests with age/sex adjustment:

1) SHARED SLE PHENOTYPE (both ancestries, all q<0.05): expansion of classical monocytes (+0.68 log-odds Asian / +0.51 EUR; ~16.5%->28.2% and 18.8%->28.6% of PBMCs), non-classical monocytes, and proliferating cells (~4-5x); collapse of naive CD4 T cells (-1.49 / -0.80 log-odds), MAIT cells (-1.69 / -1.42), memory B cells and pDCs; and induction of a 29-gene type-I interferon (IFN) module in every cell type (e.g. classical monocytes +1.66 / +1.37 log2CPM).

2) ANCESTRY-DIFFERENTIAL COMPOSITION: the SLE-associated CD4 T-cell loss is about TWICE AS LARGE in Asian patients (CD4 T: 41.4%->21.9% [-19.4 pp] vs 36.0%->28.3% [-7.7 pp]; disease x ancestry interaction +0.58 log-odds, p=2.1e-4, q=0.0023 at the annotation-complete coarse level; naive CD4 interaction +0.69, q=0.0064). This survives adjustment for processing cohort (p=0.0046) and exclusion of all cohort-1 donors (p=0.0057). Conversely, effector-memory CD4 T cells expand in European American SLE (+0.28, p=3e-4) but not in Asian SLE (interaction p=0.016, q=0.074). Monocyte, dendritic-cell and NK changes are statistically indistinguishable between ancestries (all interaction q>0.18).

3) ANCESTRY-DIFFERENTIAL EXPRESSION — STRONGER IFN SIGNATURE IN ASIAN SLE: the IFN-module induction is significantly stronger in Asian patients in 16/17 cell types (sign test p=2.8e-4), with interaction magnitudes of 0.44–1.05 log2CPM (bright NK -1.05, GZMK+ CD8 T -0.72, memory B -0.67, MAIT -0.90; 5 types at q<0.05, e.g. GZMK+ CD8: 3.75->5.35 in Asian vs 3.95->4.65 in EUR). The result persists after cohort adjustment (GZMK+ CD8, bright NK, MAIT q<=0.03) and after adjusting for disease-activity state (16/17 still negative). Individual IFN-stimulated genes are upregulated in both ancestries (cM IFI27 log2FC +4.29 Asian / +5.08 EUR, both FDR<1e-4) with no single-gene ancestry interaction surviving correction — the ancestry difference is in coordinated module amplitude, not in which genes respond. Gene-by-gene interactions elsewhere (e.g. cM ARHGAP30, B_naive CTAG2) are abundant before cohort adjustment but largely disappear after it (0–4 genes/type at FDR<0.05), so they are batch-fragile.

CLINICAL READING: shared mechanisms (monocyte/IFN-axis activation) justify IFN-axis-targeted therapy such as anifrolumab across both populations, but IFN-score and CD4/naive-CD4 biomarker thresholds calibrated in European-ancestry cohorts will miscalibrate for Asian patients, who show a stronger IFN transcriptional response and deeper naive-CD4 lymphopenia on average.

CAVEATS: ethnicity is self-reported (African American n=3 and Hispanic n=2 donors were untestable; "Asian" is not further resolved); only 23 Asian controls; processing cohort is strongly confounded with ancestry x disease (46/74 European controls in cohort 1, no Asian donors there); no medication/serology data beyond disease_state (managed/flare/treated); fine cell labels (ct_cov) are missing for all myeloid cells and ~9% of lymphoid cells (the authoritative composition result uses annotation-complete coarse labels); per-type logit models are not a full Dirichlet-multinomial compositional model; and this is a cross-sectional PBMC study, so no causal or treatment-response claims are possible.
da-17-5.notes: The agent performed a thorough donor-level ancestry-stratified analysis with appropriate statistical testing and generally reported results in line with the rubric, though the exact CD4 T fold-change values are slightly outside the expected ranges, leading to a B for criterion 4.

da-18-1.answer:
FINAL ANSWER — How the genomic landscape differs across breast-cancer receptor subtypes (MSK-IMPACT targeted-panel cohort, 1,814 assigned samples: HR+/HER2- n=1,362; HR+/HER2+ n=132; HR-/HER2+ n=70; TNBC n=250; 104 samples with unknown/equivocal receptors excluded)

1) TP53 IS THE STRONGEST DISCRIMINATOR — AN ORDERLY GRADIENT WITH HR/HER2 STATUS
   TP53 mutation frequency: HR+/HER2- 23.2% -> HR+/HER2+ 47.0% -> HR-/HER2+ 78.6% -> TNBC 81.2% (chi-square p = 5.5e-83, Bonferroni q = 1.1e-80). TNBC TP53 mutations are more often truncating (53.8% nonsense/frameshift/splice) than in HR+ tumors (33-38%). PIK3CA and TP53 are mutually exclusive overall (co-occurrence 208, OR = 0.54, p = 1.5e-09), consistent with two alternative evolutionary routes (PI3K-driven luminal vs p53-deficient).

2) HR+/HER2- (LUMINAL) DISEASE IS PI3K-DRIVEN WITH LUMINAL TF/EPIGENETIC DRIVERS
   PIK3CA is the top gene in HR+/HER2- at 42.5% (hotspots H1047R n=207, E545K n=128, E542K n=75 within that subtype) versus 31.8% (HR+/HER2+), 32.9% (HR-/HER2+) and only 18.8% in TNBC (q = 2.5e-09). The whole PI3K pathway (PIK3CA/PIK3R1/PTEN/AKT1/2/3/MTOR) is mutated in 55.1% of HR+/HER2- vs 35.2% of TNBC. HR+-enriched drivers: CDH1 18.1%, GATA3 18.0% (vs ~3% in HER2+/TNBC; q = 3.0e-07), MAP3K1 9.8%, AKT1 6.4% (92/109 are E17K, 87 in HR+/HER2-), TBX3 5.3%, CBFB 4.7%, FOXA1 4.7%.
   Copy number: 11q13 and 8p11 amplicons are the luminal signature — CCND1 amplification 21.6% (with co-amplified FGF3 17.8% / FGF4 18.3%; 84 samples co-amplify CCND1+FGFR1), FGFR1 amplification 14.0%, versus 1.4-7.6% in HER2+ and TNBC; MDM2 amp 4.5%. The cyclinD-CDK4/6-CDKN2A-RB axis is altered in 26.9% of HR+/HER2-, mostly via cyclin/CDK amplification rather than RB1 loss.
   ACTIONABLE SUBCOHORT: 42.5% of HR+/HER2- are PIK3CA-mutant (alpelisib-eligible); ~6% carry AKT1 E17K; CCND1/FGFR1-amplified disease (~25% union).

3) ESR1 ACTIVATING MUTATIONS = A THERAPY-ACQUIRED, HR+-ONLY RESISTANCE SUBCOHORT
   ESR1 mutation: HR+/HER2- 10.3%, HR+/HER2+ 6.1%, HR-/HER2+ 0.0%, TNBC 0.4% (q = 2.4e-05); 164 mutated samples, 79% at the classic ligand-binding-domain hotspots D538G (57), Y537S/C/N (60 combined), E380Q (17). Exposure matters more than subtype: in HR+ tumors, ESR1 mutations occur in 1.6% (11/701) of treatment-naive primary samples versus 17.3% (137/793) of post-treatment/metastatic samples (OR = 0.08, p = 5.1e-28); within HR+/HER2- specifically 2.6% (primary) vs 19.2% (metastasis). ESR1 amplification (n=24) occurs exclusively in HR+/HER2-. Other exposure-associated gains in HR+ tumors: ERBB2 mutation 2.3% -> 5.8%, NF1 1.4% -> 5.5%, TP53 22.0% -> 28.2%, while PIK3CA is stable (45.1% vs 38.5%).

4) HER2+ DISEASE (BOTH HR+ AND HR-) IS DEFINED BY THE 17q12 AMPLICON AND TP53
   ERBB2 amplification: 79.5% (HR+/HER2+) and 90.0% (HR-/HER2+) vs 0.4%/0.0% in HER2- subtypes (p ~ 1e-310), with frequent co-amplification of CDK12 (54.5%/60.0%), RARA (25.0%/11.4%), SPOP (12.9%/20.0%), STAT3/STAT5A. HER2+ samples carry far more amplifications per sample (5.69 HR+/HER2+, 4.64 HR-/HER2+) than HER2- subtypes (2.85, 2.56); >91% of HER2+ samples have at least one amplification vs ~52% of HER2- samples (Kruskal-Wallis H = 110.1, p = 1e-23). ERBB2 point mutations are rare and NOT subtype-specific (3.9-6.8%, NS): L755S (19), S310F (8), E770_A771insGIRD (8), V777L (7) etc. HR-/HER2+ additionally shows NF1 alteration (11.4% mutation + 5.7% amplification).

5) TNBC HAS THE HIGHEST MUTATIONAL BURDEN AND AN RB1/PTEN-LOSS GENOMIC SIGNATURE
   Median TMB (nonsynonymous mut/Mb): TNBC 0.167 vs HR-/HER2+ 0.133 vs HR+/HER2- 0.100 and HR+/HER2+ 0.100 (Kruskal-Wallis p = 1.8e-09; TNBC > both HR+ subtypes after Bonferroni, q < 1e-06); mean panel mutations/sample 5.8 vs 3.7 in HR+/HER2+. Absolute TMB remains low in all subtypes (only 1 sample >= 5 mut/Mb). TNBC-enriched alterations: RB1 loss (mutation 11.2% + deep deletion 5.6%; q = 1.7e-12), PIK3R1 (8.0% mutation + 1.6% deep deletion; q = 2.7e-10), PTEN (8.8% mutation + 4.4% deep deletion), NF1 (8.0%, mostly loss-of-function), MYC amplification (15.6% vs 7.3% in HR+/HER2-), CCNE1 and KDM5A amplification, MAP3K1 deep deletion (2.4%). The cell-cycle axis is altered in 30.8% of TNBC but through RB1/CDKN2A loss rather than cyclin-D amplification (CCND1 amp only 6.4%) — biologically the opposite route to CDK4/6 dependence and a plausible CDK4/6-inhibitor-resistance mechanism.

6) ACTIONABLE PATHWAY SUBCOHORTS CROSS SUBTYPE BOUNDARIES
   Homologous-recombination repair gene loss (LOF mutation or deep deletion in BRCA1/2, PALB2, ATM, CHEK2, RAD51D, BRIP1, FANCA): 3.5% of HR+/HER2-, 5.3% of HR+/HER2+, 2.9% of HR-/HER2+ and 4.4% of TNBC — HR-deficient, PARP-inhibitor/platinum-relevant tumors are NOT confined to TNBC in this cohort. BRCA1 amplification appears in 3.8% of HR+/HER2+. ERBB2-mutant tumors exist in every subtype (~4-7%), as do PI3K-pathway-mutant tumors (35-55%).

7) RECEPTOR CONVERSION IS VISIBLE IN THE GENOMICALLY PROFILED SAMPLES
   Grouping by the sequenced sample's receptors (rather than the primary tumor's) captures conversion in advanced disease: of primary HR+/HER2- tumors, 1,250/1,356 with assignable status remain HR+/HER2- but 81 are sequenced as HR-/HER2- and 25 as HR+/HER2+; 156/166 primary triple-negative tumors remain HR-/HER2-.

CONCISE SUMMARY
   - HR+/HER2-: PIK3CA-high (42.5%) / TP53-low (23.2%), luminal drivers (GATA3, CDH1, MAP3K1, AKT1 E17K), CCND1/FGFR1/11q13 amplicons, ESR1 resistance mutations after endocrine therapy (17% post-therapy), highest PI3K-pathway actionability (55%).
   - HR+/HER2+: intermediate — TP53 ~47% + PIK3CA ~32% coexisting, ERBB2/CDK12/RARA amplicon (~80% ERBB2-amplified), highest amplification burden (5.7/sample), retains GATA3/CDH1/ESR1.
   - HR-/HER2+: TP53-dominant (78.6%) + ERBB2 amplicon (90%), PIK3CA still ~33%, highest ERBB2/CDK12 co-amplification, NF1 alterations.
   - TNBC: TP53 ~81% with more truncating mutations, highest TMB (median 0.167 vs 0.100 mut/Mb in HR+/HER2-), lowest PIK3CA (18.8%), enriched for RB1/PTEN/PIK3R1/NF1 loss and MYC/CCNE1/KDM5A amplification, near-absent ESR1/GATA3, and the highest deep-deletion burden.

KEY LIMITATIONS: targeted 474-gene panel (no genome-wide CNAs, fusions or SVs; CNA matrix encodes only high-level events, so aneuploidy differences are underestimated); cohort enriched for treated/metastatic disease (subtype vs exposure confounding for ESR1/ERBB2/NF1/TP53); small HR-/HER2+ (n=70) and HR+/HER2+ (n=132) subgroups; 144 patients contribute >1 sample (partial non-independence); no treatment-response or survival data, so actionability is pathway-level inference, not demonstrated efficacy.
da-18-1.notes: The agent performed a comprehensive and correct analysis that meets all advanced criteria for data loading, subtype classification, TMB analysis, driver gene identification, ERBB2 alteration analysis, biological interpretation, and source reliability.

da-18-5.answer:
FINAL ANSWER (Task DA-18-5)

Cumulative frequency of MAPK pathway alterations in post-hormonal therapy HR+/HER2- tumors:

    116 / 705 = 16.5%  (95% CI 13.7%-19.2%)

Cohort definition
- Receptor subtype from the sequenced sample: HR_STATUS = Positive AND OVERALL_HER2_STATUS = Negative -> 1,362 of 1,918 samples.
- Therapy exposure: any sample that is NOT a "Treatment Naive Primary" (i.e., all metastases plus "Post-Treatment Primary" and "Post-Neo Primary" biopsies), because no explicit endocrine-therapy column exists in the clinical file. Index group n = 705 (629 metastases, 40 post-treatment primaries, 36 post-neoadjuvant primaries); treatment-naive HR+/HER2- primary reference group n = 657.
- Positive control that this grouping captures endocrine exposure: ESR1 mutations 18.6% (131/705) in the post-therapy group vs 1.4% (9/657) in treatment-naive tumors.

Event definition
- MAPK pathway alteration = nonsynonymous SNV/indel (MAF) OR amplification (CNA = 2) OR deep deletion (CNA = -2) in a MAPK-pathway gene covered by the panel.
- Primary gene set (19 genes, canonical Ras-Raf-MEK-ERK cascade + direct regulators): KRAS, NRAS, HRAS, BRAF, RAF1, ARAF, MAP2K1, MAP2K2, MAPK1, MAPK3, NF1, RIT1, SOS1, PTPN11, RASA1, SPRED1, SHOC2, RRAS, RRAS2.

Result and comparison (post-therapy HR+/HER2- vs treatment-naive HR+/HER2-)
- 116/705 = 16.5% vs 53/657 = 8.1%; OR = 2.24, Fisher exact p = 2.4e-06. The twofold enrichment supports MAPK pathway activation as an acquired/selected endocrine-resistance mechanism.
- Main contributing events in the post-therapy group: NF1 loss 6.0% (42 samples, mostly truncating), KRAS 1.7% (hotspot p.G12* plus amplification), RIT1 2.0% (mostly amplification), RASA1 1.4%, MAPK1 1.1%, RAF1 1.0%, SOS1 0.9%, BRAF 0.7%.

Sensitivity to gene-set breadth (same 705 samples)
- Canonical 10-gene RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK cassette only: 47/705 = 6.7% (naive 5.0%, p = 0.21).
- Adding MAP3K1/MAP2K4: 203/705 = 28.8% (naive 23.0%, p = 0.016).
- Adding MAP3K13/14, DUSP4, ERRFI1, RPS6KA4 (25 genes): 215/705 = 30.5% (naive 24.5%, p = 0.015).
- Broadest MAPK + upstream RTK definition (45 genes, includes FGFR1 amplification at 17.6%): 415/705 = 58.9% (naive 42.0%, p = 5.8e-10) - upper bound only.
- Cohort-definition sensitivity: using primary-tumor receptor status (n = 762 post-therapy) gives 16.7% vs 8.0%; restricting to metastases only (n = 629) gives 16.4%. The ~16.5% estimate is robust.

Interpretation
Roughly one in six post-endocrine-therapy HR+/HER2- tumors (about 30% if the upstream MAP3K kinases MAP3K1/MAP2K4 are included) carries a genomic MAPK-pathway alteration, dominated by NF1 loss and RAS-pathway activating events; NF1-mutant tumors alone are the largest genomically defined, potentially MEK/ERK-inhibitor-targetable subgroup.

Key caveats
- Hormonal-therapy exposure is inferred from sampling context (no explicit therapy column), so some post-therapy tumors may have received chemotherapy only.
- Cross-sectional comparison of different patients, not paired serial biopsies: clonal selection vs de novo resistance cannot be distinguished.
- MAP3K1/MAP2K4 losses are frequent in both therapy groups and are biologically ambiguous as "activation" events.
- Targeted 474-gene panel; non-genomic MAPK activation (phospho-ERK) is not measured.

Files: analysis script mapk_analysis.py; per-gene table mapk_per_gene_posttherapy_HRposHER2neg.csv; full trace trace.md.

However, it did not use the exact MAPK gene set specified in the rubric, did not report MAPK alteration frequencies stratified by ESR1 status, and did not establish the expected mutual exclusivity between MAPK and ESR1 alterations.

da-18-7.answer:
ANSWER: In post-hormonal-therapy HR+/HER2- tumors from this MSK-IMPACT cohort, ESR1 mutations and MAPK-pathway alterations are NEITHER significantly mutually exclusive NOR significantly co-occurring - they are statistically LARGELY INDEPENDENT, and they demonstrably co-exist within individual resistant tumors.

COHORT (n = 705 post-therapy HR+/HER2- samples): 1,918 profiled samples -> 1,111 sampled after therapy (1,000 metastases + 111 post-treatment/post-neoadjuvant primaries) -> 705 with sequenced-sample HR+/HER2- receptor status (629 metastases, 76 post-treatment primaries).

EVENT DEFINITIONS: ESR1 mutation = any non-silent/splice-altering ESR1 variant (131/705 = 18.6%; 92% at canonical ligand-binding-domain hotspots: D538G 53, Y537S/C/N 49, E380Q 13, L536x 8). MAPK-pathway alteration = non-silent mutation or amplification (+2) or deep deletion (-2) in a curated 28-gene core RAS/MAPK set (KRAS, NRAS, HRAS, BRAF, RAF1, ARAF, MAP2K1/2, MAPK1, MAP3K1, MAP2K4, NF1, NF2, RASA1, SOS1, PTPN11, SPRED1, RIT1, CBL, GNAQ, GNA11, etc.; 21/28 genes on the panel): 203/705 = 28.8% (MAP3K1 63, MAP2K4 53, NF1 42, plus RASA1, SOS1, RAF1, BRAF, KRAS, RIT1 amp, MAPK1 amp, ...).

MAIN RESULT (2x2, n = 705):
- ESR1-mutant AND MAPK-altered (double-positive): 33 tumors (4.7% of cohort; 25.2% of ESR1-mutants; 16.3% of MAPK-altered) vs 37.7 expected under independence (-13% deficit).
- ESR1-only 98; MAPK-only 170; neither 404.
- Fisher's exact OR = 0.80 (95% CI 0.52-1.23), p = 0.34 (Pearson chi-square p = 0.31; phi = -0.04). MAPK alteration rate 25.2% in ESR1-mutant vs 29.6% in ESR1-wild-type tumors.

SENSITIVITY ANALYSES (same conclusion): mutations-only OR = 0.63, p = 0.08; tight 18-gene RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK cassette OR = 0.61, p = 0.09; CNA-only OR = 1.37, p = 0.30; metastases-only (n = 629) OR = 0.84, p = 0.51; patient-level deduplication (n = 641) OR = 0.85, p = 0.56. Per-gene, only NF1 shows a nominal exclusivity signal (2/42 NF1-altered tumors ESR1-mutant, OR = 0.21, p = 0.014) that does not survive correction for 10 genes tested. A significant-looking exclusivity when subtype is defined by the PRIMARY tumor instead of the sequenced sample (OR = 0.43, p = 0.001) is an artifact: that definition admits ER-negative/converted metastases, which almost never carry ESR1 mutations, and excludes 17 genuine double-positive tumors.

BIOLOGICAL INTERPRETATION: The two resistance mechanisms do not substitute for one another (no significant mutual exclusivity) and are not significantly cooperative; they assort independently, with a mild, non-significant exclusivity trend for mutation-based events (notably NF1 loss). About 1 in 4 ESR1-mutant resistant tumors also carries a MAPK-pathway alteration (e.g., P-0000152-T02-IM5: ESR1 p.D538G + MAP2K4 splice truncation; P-0000288-T01-IM3: ESR1 p.Y537S + MAP3K1 frameshift), consistent with combined constitutive-ER signaling plus parallel MAPK drive and supporting combination of ER-directed therapy with MAPK-pathway blockade rather than using ESR1 mutation status to rule out MAPK targeting. Context validation: ESR1 mutation is 16-fold enriched post-therapy (18.6% vs 1.4% in treatment-naive HR+/HER2- primaries, p = 1e-29) and MAPK alteration is modestly enriched (28.8% vs 22.8%, p = 0.013; driven by NF1 1.8%->6.0% and RIT1 0.6%->2.0%).

LIMITATIONS: n = 705 excludes only strong effects (OR >= ~1.7 or <= ~0.55 detectable at 80% power); hormone-therapy exposure is inferred from sampling context (no per-patient therapy records); 8 curated MAPK genes are absent from the 474-gene panel and no expression/phospho/fusion data exist, so functional MAPK activation via upstream RTKs is not measured; the Hotspot flag column is unpopulated and MAPK mutations were not individually curated for functional class; 45 cohort samples come from patients with multiple profiled samples (patient-level analysis gives the same result); association only - no response/survival data, so clinical impact of the double-positive state cannot be assessed.
da-18-7.notes: The agent's analysis is thorough and well-documented, but it diverges from the rubric in key specification areas: it uses all ESR1 mutations rather than LBD-restricted, omits ERBB2/EGFR from MAPK, uses two-sided Fisher instead of one-sided, and interprets the result as independence rather than mutual exclusivity. The cohort also mixes post-treatment primaries with metastases. While results reporting and source reliability are strong, several criteria are only partially met and interpretation fails to match the required conclusion.

da-19-3.answer:
FINAL ANSWER — How RUNX1 chromatin occupancy changes upon CBFβ-SMMHC inhibition (AI-10-49) in ME-1 inv(16) AML cells

Overall: RUNX1 chromatin occupancy increases massively and is redistributed to thousands of new, predominantly promoter-proximal sites on active chromatin. The change is overwhelmingly "gain", not loss, and includes de novo promoter binding at MYC and other survival/apoptosis loci — consistent with AI-10-49 freeing native RUNX1 from sequestration by the CBFβ-SMMHC fusion, so that RUNX1 can re-occupy its canonical targets.

1) Global occupancy increases ~7-fold
- MACS2 (q<0.05, IP vs matched input) RUNX1 peaks: DMSO (GSM2715537) 1,329 -> AI-10-49 (GSM2715538) 9,169 (canonical chromosomes 1,311 -> 8,971; +584%).
- Peak quality also rises: median MACS2 fold enrichment 5.4 -> 7.2; median -log10q 12.2 -> 15.7; fraction of peaks with FE>=4: 85.0% -> 95.2%.
- Control comparison with the same pipeline on H3K27ac (GSM2715535/36) shows a near-stable landscape (56,227 -> 54,837 peaks; ~50% shared), so the RUNX1 expansion is not a pipeline artifact.

2) The change is de novo site acquisition, not loss of existing sites
- Reciprocal-overlap >=0.5 classification: 712 shared peaks; 8,259 gained (92.1% of all AI-10-49 RUNX1 peaks); 599 DMSO peaks not re-called.
- Of those 599 "lost" DMSO sites, 504 (84.1%) still have >=1 bp of AI-10-49 RUNX1 signal; only 95 sites genome-wide are fully vacated.
- Shared sites are the strongest in both samples (median FE 10.7 vs 7.0 for gained in the AI sample, Mann-Whitney p = 1.2e-72).
- RUNX1-bound promoters (peak within +/-2 kb of TSS): 367 (DMSO) -> 3,100 (AI-10-49); gained 2,771, retained 329, lost 38.

3) Gained binding is promoter-biased and lands on already-active chromatin
- 38.6% of gained peaks are within +/-2 kb of a TSS (GENCODE v19), vs 3.71% promoter sequence in the canonical genome (binomial p << 1e-300); promoter fraction of all RUNX1 peaks rises 29.1% -> 37.6%; median distance-to-TSS 10.9 -> 7.4 kb.
- 86.2% of gained RUNX1 sites overlap an H3K27ac peak in the AI-10-49 sample (90.2% vs the DMSO H3K27ac map), significantly more than shared sites (Fisher OR 2.71, p = 5.1e-27). Promoters that gain RUNX1 were already H3K27ac-positive in ~90% of cases — RUNX1 is redistributed onto active regulatory elements, not into silent chromatin.

4) Specific therapeutic-candidate targets (de novo RUNX1 upon AI-10-49)
- MYC: no RUNX1 peak anywhere within +/-50 kb in DMSO; in AI-10-49 a single peak (chr8:128,747,329-128,747,624, summit 128,747,409, FE 4.1, -log10q 5.9) sits +57 bp from the MYC TSS, i.e. directly on the MYC promoter. The broad MYC promoter H3K27ac peak is retained (FE 15.1 -> 15.3) but with lower confidence (-log10q 178 -> 77) and two new flanking H3K27ac peaks at -4.6/-6.1 kb.
- Other loci with 0 -> multiple RUNX1 peaks (all gained): MCL1 (4), BCL2 (3), BCL2L1 (2, intronic), BAD (6), CDKN1A (2), FLT3 (4), CCND2 (6), SPI1/PU.1 (1 -> 4), CEBPA (2 -> 4). ITGAM promoter RUNX1 is retained (shared).

5) The gained cistrome is bona fide RUNX1 and leukemia-relevant
- Enrichr on the 2,432 protein-coding genes whose promoters gain RUNX1: top ChEA_2022 hit is an independent RUNX1 ChIP-seq cistrome (RUNX1, megakaryocytes, PMID 21571218; 1,036/4,172 genes, adj p = 1.0e-147), followed by SPI1 (adj p = 1.6e-139) and FLI1 (adj p = 1.0e-136) cistromes.
- KEGG_2021_Human: "Acute myeloid leukemia" 22/67 genes, adj p = 4.8e-04 (CEBPA, FLT3, STAT5A, BAD, ZBTB16); "Transcriptional misregulation in cancer" 45/192, adj p = 4.8e-04.
- GO BP: transcription by RNA polymerase II (54/192, adj p = 2.6e-06), regulation of autophagy (65/241, adj p = 7.3e-07), proteasomal/ubiquitin-dependent catabolism.

Mechanistic interpretation: CBFβ-SMMHC sequesters RUNX1 off DNA in untreated inv(16) cells; AI-10-49 disrupts the CBFβ-SMMHC-RUNX1 interaction, restoring DNA binding by the native RUNX1 protein. The result is a ~7-fold expansion of the RUNX1 cistrome concentrated at promoters and active enhancers of transcription/apoptosis/protein-turnover genes. De novo promoter-proximal RUNX1 at MYC — together with re-organized (retained-but-weakened, with new flanking) H3K27ac at the MYC locus — provides a direct chromatin mechanism for MYC down-regulation and apoptosis, identifying RUNX1 re-occupancy as the effector arm of AI-10-49's therapeutic effect and MYC as a direct drug-induced RUNX1 target.

Caveats: single RUNX1 ChIP replicate per condition (no IDR); no BAM/bigWig signal tracks in this workspace, so occupancy change is quantified from peak calls and MACS2 fold enrichment rather than normalized read counts (a global detection increase cannot be statistically separated from redistribution); no RNA-seq/ATAC matrices available here, so expression/accessibility consequences are not recomputed; gain/loss calls depend on the overlap convention (permissive 1-bp rule would call 92.8% of DMSO sites retained); no reference FASTA for de novo motif validation (RUNX1-target authenticity rests on the independent ChEA RUNX1 cistrome enrichment).

Key numbers: RUNX1 peaks 1,329 -> 9,169; shared 712; gained 8,259 (92.1% of AI-10-49 peaks); fully vacated DMSO sites 95; promoters bound 367 -> 3,100 (gained 2,771 / retained 329 / lost 38); gained peaks in promoters 38.6% vs 3.71% genomic background (p << 1e-300); gained sites overlapping H3K27ac 86.2%; MYC promoter RUNX1 +57 bp from TSS, FE 4.1, -log10q 5.9.

Analysis code, tables and figures: analysis/runx1_occupancy/ (scripts 01-14; output/tables, output/figures/fig1_runx1_occupancy.png, fig2_promoters_myc.png); full trace in trace.md.
da-19-3.notes: The agent's data selection and biological interpretation are strong, but the differential peak method uses reciprocal overlap at the peak level rather than cluster-based merge, leading to quantitative and enrichment analysis deviations from the full-score rubric.

da-19-6.answer:
FINAL ANSWER
============

Question: Does AI-10-49 treatment (CBFβ-SMMHC inhibition) lead to global changes
in chromatin accessibility in inv(16) AML (ME-1) cells?

ANSWER: YES. AI-10-49 causes a marked, genome-wide reorganization of chromatin
accessibility - dominated by a broad LOSS of distal (enhancer-like)
accessibility, with promoter accessibility largely preserved and slightly
reinforced. The effect is pervasive and moderate rather than a handful of large
locus-specific changes.

Key quantitative evidence (ATAC-seq, n=2 DMSO vs n=2 AI-10-49; MACS2 q<=0.05
narrowPeak calls; 101,424-peak condition-blind union set; hg19/GRCh37):

1. FEWER ACCESSIBLE SITES DESPITE DEEPER LIBRARIES. Called peaks per sample drop
   from 66,990 / 64,874 (DMSO rep1/2) to 48,644 / 53,076 (AI-10-49 rep1/2) on
   canonical chromosomes (-28% of accessible loci: 90,184 -> 64,561 on the union
   set). The AI-10-49 libraries are ~1.7x DEEPER (4.14M / 4.40M vs 2.52M / 2.46M
   nucleosome-free fragments, from MACS2 headers), so this contraction is not a
   sampling/depth artifact.

2. LOSS OUTWEIGHS GAIN 3.3:1. Of 101,424 union peaks: 53,321 shared (52.6%),
   36,863 lost i.e. accessible only in DMSO (36.3%), 11,240 gained i.e. only in
   AI-10-49 (11.1%). McNemar exact test on the discordant calls: p < 1e-300
   (stricter both-replicate consensus sets: 12,360 lost vs 8,070 gained,
   p = 2.7e-199). Jaccard(DMSO set, AI set) = 0.526 vs within-condition replicate
   Jaccard 0.479 (DMSO) / 0.603 (AI): the landscape is clearly shifted but the
   strong core is shared.

3. THE LOSS IS SELECTIVE, NOT RANDOM. Lost peaks are overwhelmingly weak and
   distal: median DMSO pileup 3.7 (vs 7.0 in shared peaks); 85.7% had DMSO pileup
   <5; they carried only 18.8% of total DMSO peak signal. Of strong
   DMSO-reproducible peaks (pileup >=5/10/20 in both reps), 83.6% / 86.2% / 85.0%
   are RETAINED after treatment. Promoter-proximal peaks (<=2 kb of a TSS) are
   4-5x under-represented among lost peaks (5.3% promoter vs 22.6% in shared;
   Fisher OR 5.20, p ~ 0): 86.0% of DMSO-accessible promoters remain accessible
   vs only 54.2% of distal sites.

4. RETAINED SITES ARE MILDLY REINFORCED, NOT WEAKENED. At the 53,321 shared
   peaks, median log2FC (AI/DMSO) = +0.162 with 63.7% of peaks increasing
   (Wilcoxon p < 1e-16); at peaks reproducible in all 4 samples, +0.182 (71.7%
   increasing). Aggregate peak signal does not collapse (total pileup 450k/414k
   DMSO vs 410k/464k AI); instead, per-fragment peak signal re-concentrates into
   fewer, stronger loci (pileup share at shared loci / library size: 14.6%/13.6%
   DMSO -> 9.2%/9.7% AI).

5. THE CHANGE IS GLOBAL AND GRADED. A properly powered per-peak test (limma-
   eBayes on log2 pileup, 101,424 peaks) finds NO single peak at FDR<0.05
   (minimum FDR = 0.26) - expected at 2 vs 2 - while 9,547 peaks show nominal
   p<0.05 (2x the null rate) with a 2.4:1 down:up ratio among |log2FC|>=1. The
   genome-wide one-sample Wilcoxon on per-peak log2FC is p < 1e-16. So the
   accessibility change is broad and individually modest, but collectively
   unmistakable. (A naive DESeq2-style NB GLM on pileup flagged 98.6% of peaks
   "significant"; this was rejected as a variance-misspecification artifact and
   is documented as such.)

6. NOT MOTIF-TARGETED. Consensus-motif scanning (RUNX1/CBF, PU.1/SPI1, AP-1,
   C/EBPbeta, E-box; summit +/-100 bp, chr 8/16/19/21/22) shows NO RUNX1-motif
   enrichment among lost peaks (lost 7.9% vs shared 7.6%, OR 0.96, p=0.59).
   Lost/gained peaks are mildly DEPLETED of PU.1 (p_bonf=0.010), AP-1
   (p_bonf=0.005) and E-box (p_bonf=0.022) motifs relative to shared peaks - a
   peak-strength effect, not selective closing of RUNX/CBF sites.

7. LOCUS VIGNETTES. MYC locus (chr8:128.74-128.81 Mb, hg19): accessibility is
   maintained or slightly increased (mean called-peak pileup ~6.7 -> ~9.0;
   median per-peak log2FC +0.08), so the drug's effect on MYC in this system is
   not executed via gross loss of MYC-locus accessibility. Largest nominal
   changes include promoter-proximal
   losses at PYCRL (DMSO pileup 29.4 -> absent), RNF139, SLC26A6, STX4, HOXA13,
   and promoter-proximal gains at GTF2E2, PARP11, CNOT4, STT3B, CDC45, EMR3,
   ATF7IP.

BIOLOGICAL INTERPRETATION. Acute pharmacologic inhibition of the inv(16) fusion
product CBFβ-SMMHC in ME-1 cells contracts the accessible chromatin landscape
globally, preferentially erasing weak distal enhancer-like sites while sparing
promoters and the strongest enhancers (which are mildly reinforced). This is the
accessibility signature expected when a leukemia fusion transcription-factor
complex that nucleates enhancer architecture is acutely disabled, with a
likely contribution from apoptosis-associated chromatin condensation at the
treatment dose. The absence of RUNX1-motif enrichment among lost peaks argues
against a simple "all RUNX sites close" mechanism; redistribution, not site-
specific gating, dominates.

CAVEATS / WHAT THIS ANALYSIS CANNOT CONCLUDE.
- No raw reads/BAMs were provided: fragments-in-peak counts, TSS enrichment,
  nucleosome periodicity and proper TMM/RLE normalization were impossible; the
  quantitative signal used is MACS2 pileup (monotone but not a count), so
  absolute fold changes are approximations (presence/absence calls and rankings
  are robust).
- n=2 per condition: no individual peak reaches FDR<0.05 in a defensible
  per-peak test; locus-level claims (e.g., PYCRL promoter loss) are nominal.
  The GLOBAL conclusions rest on aggregate tests over 10^4-10^5 loci and are
  robust.
- "Lost" calls are threshold-dependent (MACS2 q<=0.05, no control track); at
  stricter signal thresholds the loss shrinks to ~14-16% of strong
  reproducible peaks, but the loss>>gain asymmetry holds at every threshold
  tested.
- Single treatment condition, no time course/dose response: primary
  (CBFβ-SMMHC-directed) versus secondary (apoptosis-associated) chromatin
  changes cannot be separated.
- RNA-seq and ChIP-seq (H3K27ac, RUNX1) processed files from the same cohort
  were not provided, so accessibility changes could not be tied to
  acetylation or expression here.

BOTTOM LINE: Yes - AI-10-49 triggers a global, highly significant
(p < 1e-199, McNemar; p < 1e-16, Wilcoxon) reorganization of chromatin
accessibility in ME-1 inv(16) AML cells: ~36% of the union accessible-site set
(weak, distal, enhancer-like loci) is closed, ~11% is newly opened, promoters
and strong enhancers are retained and mildly strengthened, and no single
transcription-factor motif class (including RUNX1/CBF) is selectively lost.
da-19-6.notes: The agent correctly identifies samples/conditions and delivers a defensible aggregate analysis of ATAC-seq accessibility changes, reporting strong evidence for global chromatin closing upon AI-10-49 treatment. The main methodological gap is the lack of true read-coverage quantification and explicit CPM normalization, which prevents a full score on the region-level quantification workflow (Criterion 2). All other criteria are met at the highest level.

da-20-1.answer:
ANSWER (Task DA-20-1): Baseline transcriptional signatures of the four primary cell types (GDPx2 Drug-seq)

Bottom line: The four cell types are DISTINCT — each vehicle (DMSO) well is unambiguously
identifiable by its transcriptome — but they also share a large common core program, so
their global profiles overlap substantially (pairwise Pearson r = 0.88-0.94). The most
similar pair is DERMAL FIBROBLAST + SKELETAL MUSCLE MYOBLASTS (r = 0.935 by profile
correlation; SkMM-AoSMC is the closest pair by profile distance/UPGMA), and MELANOCYTES
are the clear outlier relative to the three mesenchymal/myogenic types.

Analysis basis (all computed from the provided files only):
- 576 DMSO vehicle-control wells (4 cell types x 3 DMSO volumes x 48 wells); 572 passed
  QC (UMI>=100k, genes>=4000, mapped>=50%, mito<=20%): AoSMC 141, HDF 144, melanocytes
  143, SkMM 144. Matrix: 59,427 genes x 11,808 samples; filtered to 23,536 informative
  genes (rRNA/mito/snRNA/ribosomal-protein genes removed; >=10 UMI and detected in >=2%
  of vehicle wells); CPM-normalized, log1p, per-gene standardized.

1) Distinctness
- PCA of the 572 vehicle wells: PC1 14.5%, PC2 12.5%, PC3 8.0% of variance (PC4 drops to
  0.7%) — the first three PCs are the cell-type axes. Silhouette on PC1-2 = 0.888;
  group SDs are 5-25x smaller than between-group distances; the four clouds are
  essentially non-overlapping.
- PERMANOVA (PC1-10, 9,999 permutations): global F = 1,884.8, P = 1e-4; all six pairwise
  contrasts P = 0.001 (F = 1,376-3,257).
- Well-level correlations: within-type median r = 0.961 vs between-type 0.870.
- Generalization: projecting ALL 11,683 QC-pass wells (i.e., ~450 compounds x 6
  concentrations + positive controls) onto the DMSO PCA basis and classifying by nearest
  vehicle centroid gives 99.81% correct cell-type calls (22/11,683 wrong). Cell identity,
  not treatment or batch, dominates the baseline structure -> the platform is validated
  for compound profiling.
- Marker programs are lineage-correct and non-overlapping (0 shared genes among the four
  top-200 marker lists). Examples (one-vs-rest Welch t, BH-FDR<0.05, log2FC>1):
  * Melanocytes (2,306 selective genes): TYR (t=622; 1,464 vs ~0 CPM), MLANA (t=417;
    15,673 CPM), SOX10, DCT, PMEL, TYRP1, OCA2, S100B, PLP1 — canonical melanosome/
    melanocyte-lineage program.
  * Dermal fibroblasts (2,753): FBLN1 (t=171), SPON1, ADH1B, JCAD, RBPJ, SFRP2, TNC,
    plus a dominant collagen/proteoglycan core (DCN 4,957 CPM, COL1A1 601 CPM, LUM).
  * Skeletal muscle myoblasts (1,262): ADGRF5, LYVE1, TRIM58, ANKRD1 (1,930 vs 14 CPM),
    TINAGL1, PPP1R14A, GATA3; retains myogenic regulators MYF5, MYOD1, DES, MYPN, NEBL.
  * AoSMC (1,452): IL1B (t=342; 2,129 vs 0.2 CPM), SFRP4, CYP2S1, PI3, ANXA10, CD24,
    IL6 (t=199; 1,233 vs 1.0 CPM), FGL2, CA9, plus TAGLN and a MFAP5-dominated
    microfibrillar program (1,755 CPM vs <=96 elsewhere); the IL1B/IL6-high tone is
    present in all 141 vehicle wells (IL1B IQR 1,850-2,346 CPM), i.e. it is a consistent
    culture-activated secretory phenotype, not outlier wells.

2) Overlap and similarity ranking (pairwise Pearson r of mean log1p-CPM profiles,
   23,536 genes; Spearman and well-level medians give the identical ordering):
     HDF - SkMM          0.935   <-- most similar
     AoSMC - SkMM        0.926
     AoSMC - HDF         0.915
     HDF - melanocyte    0.895
     melanocyte - SkMM   0.889
     AoSMC - melanocyte  0.880   <-- least similar
   Euclidean distance on mean standardized profiles gives the same topology:
   AoSMC-SkMM 128.5 < HDF-SkMM 133.7 < AoSMC-HDF 152.5 < melanocyte-SkMM 155.0 <
   HDF-melanocyte 156.7 < AoSMC-melanocyte 157.0.
   UPGMA clustering: (AoSMC + SkMM) merge first at d=128.5, then HDF joins at d=143.1,
   melanocyte joins last at d=156.2 -> {(AoSMC, SkMM), HDF} vs melanocytes as outgroup.
   Robustness: the ranking is identical in split-half analyses (20 random splits, both
   halves rank HDF-SkMM first at r~0.935) and when recomputed within each DMSO-volume
   stratum (0.0625%, 0.1875%, 0.625% v/v; top pair HDF-SkMM each time), so it is not an
   artifact of normalization or vehicle dose. 10,934/23,536 genes are detectable (CPM>1)
  in at least 3 of the 4 types, explaining the high global overlap.

Interpretation: the three mesoderm-derived, ECM-rich types (aortic smooth muscle,
skeletal myoblasts, dermal fibroblasts) form one similarity cluster — with HDF-SkMM and
AoSMC-SkMM its two closest edges (statistically close to each other; r = 0.935 vs 0.926)
— while melanocytes (neural-crest-derived, melanosome program) are transcriptionally
the most distinct background. For compound profiling this means each cell type is a
valid, separable reference baseline, but melanocyte responses should be analyzed as a
distinct lineage context rather than pooled with the mesenchymal types.

Limitations: bulk 3' RNA-seq of single commercial lots — cell type is confounded with
donor/lot and batch (the within-cluster ordering could shift with donor variation); a
single 24 h timepoint and DMSO-exposure regime define "baseline"; only relative (CPM)
expression is interpretable because the h5 matrix excludes unassigned/multimapping
reads; the AoSMC IL1B/IL6 tone is a property of this culture condition, not in-vivo
physiology; the "most similar pair" call is metric-dependent at the margin (HDF-SkMM by
correlation vs AoSMC-SkMM by distance), whereas the mesenchymal-cluster-vs-melanocyte
split is robust.
da-20-1.notes: The agent performed a thorough exploratory analysis with strong biological interpretation and limitations, but it deviated from the required pipeline by not restricting to 0.0625% DMSO, not using variance-based top-gene filtering/TruncatedSVD, and not implementing K-means k=4, leading to B/C ratings on those criteria.

da-20-3.answer:
ANSWER — MSigDB Hallmark pathways suppressed by Brefeldin-A (BFA) across cell types (Task DA-20-3)

Method: preranked GSEA (GSEApy 1.3.1, 1,000 permutations) of the provided DESeq2 results
(BFA vs DMSO; 4 primary human cell types x 6 doses) against MSigDB Hallmark v7.5.1
(50 gene sets). Genes ranked by sign(log2FC) x -log10(p). A pathway was called
"suppressed across cell types" when NES < 0 with FDR q < 0.05 at >=2 of the 5
transcriptionally active doses (28.5-3000 nM; 9.5 nM was inactive) in ALL FOUR cell
types (aortic smooth muscle cells, dermal fibroblasts, melanocytes, skeletal muscle
myoblasts).

Fourteen Hallmark pathways are consistently suppressed by BFA in all four cell types
(ordered by median NES over 20 active cell x dose runs; strongest NES per cell type):

 1. HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITION  median NES -2.20 (per-cell min NES -2.31/-2.26/-1.91/-2.21)
 2. HALLMARK_UV_RESPONSE_DN                     -2.01 (-2.01/-2.08/-1.78/-2.10)
 3. HALLMARK_APICAL_JUNCTION                    -1.88 (-2.02/-1.99/-1.69/-1.88)
 4. HALLMARK_COAGULATION                        -1.80 (-1.82/-1.99/-1.88/-1.67)
 5. HALLMARK_TGF_BETA_SIGNALING                 -1.75 (-1.88/-1.84/-1.67/-1.79)
 6. HALLMARK_TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB            -1.75 (-1.97/-1.83/-1.75/-1.72)
 7. HALLMARK_ANGIOGENESIS                       -1.72 (-1.85/-1.86/-1.52/-1.68)
 8. HALLMARK_KRAS_SIGNALING_UP                  -1.71 (-1.80/-1.81/-1.77/-1.77)
 9. HALLMARK_COMPLEMENT                         -1.66 (-1.70/-1.84/-1.75/-1.64)
10. HALLMARK_APICAL_SURFACE                     -1.65 (-1.74/-1.76/-1.62/-1.68)
11. HALLMARK_IL2_STAT5_SIGNALING                -1.65 (-1.77/-1.85/-1.58/-1.62)
12. HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS                          -1.62 (-1.67/-1.82/-1.68/-1.60)
13. HALLMARK_MYOGENESIS                         -1.57 (-1.78/-1.61/-1.65/-1.50)
14. HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY            -1.48 (-1.52/-1.51/-1.50/-1.54)

(cell order: AoSMC / dermal fibroblast / melanocyte / skeletal muscle myoblast;
all contributing runs FDR q < 0.05, max q among contributing runs <= 0.049.)

Near-miss pathways suppressed in 3 of 4 cell types (same direction, weaker in
melanocytes): INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE, HYPOXIA, IL6_JAK_STAT3_SIGNALING,
HEDGEHOG_SIGNALING, MITOTIC_SPINDLE, INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE,
WNT_BETA_CATENIN_SIGNALING, NOTCH_SIGNALING.

Key biological reading — the suppressed programs are overwhelmingly secreted /
membrane effector programs whose products depend on ER-Golgi export: ECM and EMT
genes (COL3A1, COL5A2, SPARC, VCAN, PRRX1), TGF-beta ligands (THBS1, SERPINE1, BMP2,
ENG), inflammatory/chemokine output (IL6, IL1B, CXCL1/2/3/6/8, PTX3), angiogenic
factors (VEGFA, NRP1, FGFR1, TIMP1), coagulation factors (SERPINE1/PAI-1, THBS1,
TFPI2, PLAT), and junction/adhesion molecules (CDH6, CDH11, MPZL1, MSN, ZYX).
BFA blocks ARF1/GBF1-dependent ER-Golgi trafficking (Golgi collapse; cargo secretion
block), and the data confirm the MoA directly: rather than the secretion machinery
being repressed, BFA simultaneously INDUCES HALLMARK_UNFOLDED_PROTEIN_RESPONSE in
all four cell types (NES +1.67 to +2.46, FDR < 0.05; HSPA5/BiP +4.34, HSP90B1/GRP94
+2.33, PDIA4 +1.63, CANX +0.88, XBP1 +0.79 log2FC; and up-regulation of SEC61A1,
SRPRB, RPN1, DDOST, SEC24D) while HALLMARK_PROTEIN_SECRETION is not significantly
suppressed. Suppression of secreted-effector programs + UPR induction = the
transcriptional signature of a secretory-pathway disruptor.

Controls and robustness: (i) all 14 pathways recovered unchanged when ranking by
plain log2FoldChange (14/14, Spearman rho of NES between metrics = 0.906);
(ii) the same rule applied to the comparator compounds gives 0 pathways for
Dexamethasone and 3 unrelated cell-cycle pathways for Trichostatin A (G2M_CHECKPOINT,
MYC_TARGETS_V1, MYC_TARGETS_V2; zero overlap with the BFA set) — the BFA suppression
list is compound-specific; (iii) suppression is dose-dependent, absent at 9.5 nM
(0-38 DE genes) and maximal from 28.5-3000 nM (~4-5.5k DE genes per cell type).
da-20-3.notes: The agent executes a thorough GSEA workflow with specificity controls and robustness checks, but it misses the rubric's expected pan-cellular suppression of HALLMARK_INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE (treating it as near-miss) and uses a signed p-value-weighted ranking metric as the primary ranking rather than pure log2FoldChange, so it should receive partial credit on criteria 2 and 5.

da-20-4.answer:
DIVERGENT OVERALL, WITH ONE CONSISTENT SHARED CORE — that is the answer for dabrafenib across the four primary cell types (AoSMC, dermal fibroblast, melanocyte, skeletal-muscle myoblast) in the GDPx2 Drug-seq cohort (24 h, 6 concentrations 9.5-3000 nM vs volume-matched DMSO, n~27-32 drug and 41-48 DMSO wells per cell type after QC/outlier removal; 16,574 genes tested by limma-voom with plate blocking).

THE CONSISTENT CORE
All four cell types mount the same dose-dependent ATF4-centered integrated stress response (ISR): ATF4, DDIT3, ATF5, TRIB3, ASNS, PSAT1, PHGDH, PSPH, SHMT2, MTHFD2, SLC7A5/SLC7A11/SLC3A2/SLC6A9, CHAC1, SESN2, GDF15, STC2, NAMPT. Example log2FC at 900 nM (AoSMC/HDF/melanocyte/SkMM): ATF4 +2.20/+2.04/+1.01/+2.12; TRIB3 +3.77/+2.86/+1.91/+3.58; CHAC1 +3.40/+3.02/+2.73/+4.33. A proliferation cassette (MKI67, TOP2A, UBE2C, RRM2, CCNB1, PLK1, AURKB, CENPF) is coordinately repressed in all four (mean -0.7 to -2.3 log2). DEG-set overlaps are hypergeometrically significant in every cell-type pair (p <= 1.1e-05 at 3000 nM; <= 1e-39 at 900 nM), genome-wide log2FC correlations are positive (0.31-0.55 at 900 nM), and 31 genes are DE (FDR<0.05, |log2FC|>=1) in >=3 of 4 cell types. So the response is genuinely shared in direction.

THE DIVERGENCE (dominant)
1) Magnitude: AoSMC ~ SkMM > HDF >> melanocyte (ISR module score at 900 nM: 2.44 / 2.30 / 2.17 / 1.38; DEG threshold 95 nM in AoSMC vs 300 nM elsewhere; DEGs at 900 nM: 716 / 401 / 393 / 123).
2) Dose-position/shape: AoSMC, HDF and SkMM peak at 900 nM and partially rebound at 3000 nM (ATF4 change -0.76/-0.42/-0.02 log2, TRIB3 -2.13/-1.29/-0.98, all FDR<0.05, tested as a difference of volume-matched contrasts); the melanocyte instead shows its largest response at 3000 nM and the weakest at 900 nM. All 8 independent plates per cell type reproduce these shapes.
3) Cell-type-specific programs (3000 nM unless noted):
   - Melanocyte-only: activation of the melanogenesis/differentiation program - TYR +0.76, TYRP1 +1.04, DCT +0.66, PMEL +0.65, RAB32 +0.89, MITF +0.27 (FDR <= 7e-19) - with strong repression of SLC7A8 -1.62, CD36 -1.99, JUN -1.76, MEF2C -1.63, HRH2 -2.04, SEMA3E -2.63, RASGRP3 -2.09. None of these change in the other three types (|log2FC| <= 0.6).
   - AoSMC-selective inflammatory/vascular arm: CXCL3 +1.46, CXCL2 +1.59, CSTA +1.58, GDF15 +1.91, PTGS2 -0.78, and AoSMC-only repression of NPPB -3.41, SOST -3.01, DHRS9 -2.89, CSF2RB -2.41.
   - HDF-selective ECM/remodeling arm: strongest collagen/ECM suppression (COL1A1 -0.83, TIMP3 -0.70, CAV1 -0.96, CRABP2 -1.22, PRSS23 -1.35) with IL1RL1 +3.30 and AREG +2.82 (flat in melanocytes).
   - SkMM-selective arm: strongest per-gene ISR induction (CHAC1 +4.33, GDF15 +2.61 at 3000 nM) plus repression of KRTAP1-5 -2.74, KRTAP2-3 -2.70, HSPB1, CRYAB, RGS4, and the weakest anti-proliferative response (-1.19 vs -2.29 in HDF at 900 nM).
4) Formal test: a joint cell-type x dabrafenib interaction model (pooled 300-3000 nM vs DMSO, plate blocked) finds 2,106-4,252 genes with significantly different drug effects (FDR<0.05) in EVERY pairwise cell-type comparison - divergence is genome-wide, not a thresholding artifact. Only 2 genes pass the strict DEG filter in all four cell types at 3000 nM (CHAC1, OXTR), and Jaccard overlap of DEG sets is only 0.03-0.26.

MECHANISTIC AND SAFETY/EFFICACY READING
The shared ISR is the canonical eIF2a-ATF4 amino-acid/stress response reported for BRAF/MEK-pathway blockade. Response magnitude does NOT track basal MAPK-module expression (HDF highest, melanocyte lowest; response order AoSMC~SkMM>HDF>melanocyte), and no clean ERK-output decrease is seen in any type - consistent with BRAF-wild-type primary cells (paradoxical/neutral RAF-MAPK effects) rather than BRAF-V600-like ERK collapse. The melanocyte-specific TYR/TYRP1/DCT induction at the top dose parallels the known paradoxical RAF activation that underlies dabrafenib's cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma and melanocytic-lesion signal in BRAF-WT tissues. For safety assessment: the consistent ISR + anti-proliferative core (GDF15, NAMPT, SESN2 as candidate circulating biomarkers) is a whole-body exposure consequence at clinically achieved concentrations (dabrafenib Cmax ~1.4-2.3 uM at 150 mg BID, so the 0.9-3 uM wells span therapeutic exposure), while tissue-specific risk logic differs - strongest stress/inflammatory responses in aortic smooth muscle and dermis at ~900 nM (NPPB/SOST and collagen/IL1RL1/AREG arms respectively), and a qualitatively different, differentiation-directed switch in melanocytes at ~3000 nM.

LIMITATIONS
Single 24 h time point (no early ERK or late apoptosis phases); RNA only (no phospho-protein or kinase-activity confirmation of paradoxical MAPK signaling); no mutation/genotype annotation (BRAF-WT status assumed); donors not annotated (plates are the only replicate unit, though all 8 plates per cell type agree); DMSO volume co-varies with concentration bin and was controlled by volume-matched contrasts (DMSO volume alone alters 1,410-2,995 genes, e.g. TYRP1 -0.74 at 0.625% vs 0.0625%); DEG counts depend on FDR/|log2FC| thresholds (threshold-free log2FC correlations reported alongside); no other BRAF/MEK inhibitor in the library for class-vs-compound comparison; the AoSMC arm lost 5 drug + 3 DMSO failed wells to the depth filter.

BOTTOM LINE
Dabrafenib is NOT transcriptionally consistent across the four primary cell types. A single ATF4-centered stress-response core plus anti-proliferative signaling is shared by all, but its magnitude, dose position (900 nM peak vs 3000 nM switch), and most of the individual target genes are cell-type-specific, with statistically significant cell-type x drug interactions for thousands of genes in every pairwise comparison. Tissue-specific safety and efficacy assessment is therefore warranted: the same exposure produces a stress/inflammatory response profile in muscle and dermis but a differentiation-program switch in melanocytes.
da-20-4.notes: The agent performed a thorough limma-voom differential expression and custom gene-module analysis, but did not run the required GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark or interpret the three target pathways, leading to several C grades.

da-24-3.answer:
SHARED GENETIC FACTORS AMONG NEONATAL METABOLITES (from discovery + replication GWAS summary statistics; 13 traits x 20,474 SNPs each, plus 8,737-sample metabolite matrix)

HEADLINE FINDINGS - three loci are genuine shared genetic factors (associated with >=2 metabolites in BOTH cohorts, concordant direction):

1) ACADM, chr1:75.7 Mb - THE dominant shared factor, affects 4 traits simultaneously.
   Traits sharing it: C6, C8, C8/C2 and (C3DC+C4-OH)/C10.
   Evidence: lead SNP chr1:75727547 A>G (EAF 0.70) - C6 p=2.9e-13 disc / 3.4e-21 rep; C8 1.8e-10 / 1.0e-19; C8/C2 6.3e-10 / 2.2e-22; (C3DC+C4-OH)/C10 1.2e-12 / 2.3e-18. Within-locus z-profile correlations +0.998 to +0.999 among C6/C8/C8:C2 (one shared causal signal) and -0.995 to -0.997 between the ratio and each acylcarnitine (opposite direction). The allele that lowers C6/C8/C8:C2 raises (C3DC+C4-OH)/C10 (z +6.68 vs -7.31 at the anchor, consistent in replication). 481 SNPs in the panel associate with >=2 traits; the top ones hit exactly these 4 traits and all 4 replicate.
   Biology: ACADM = medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase, first step of mitochondrial beta-oxidation; it sets the steady-state level of the C6-C8 acylcarnitines measured at heel-prick.

2) CRAT/DOLPP1 locus, chr9:129.1 Mb - shared by C4DC+C5-OH and C6.
   Strongest signal in the data (C4DC+C5-OH p=1.3e-63 disc / 8.7e-92 rep) also affects C6 (2.2e-5 / 3.6e-5); within-locus profile r = +0.996 (disc) and +0.994 (rep). Removing this locus drops the C4DC+C5-OH - C6 genetic correlation from 0.321 to 0.225 - the largest single-locus attribution in the panel. Candidate gene CRAT (carnitine acetyltransferase, 10 kb from lead), which buffers the acylcarnitine pool.

3) CPT2, chr1:53.2 Mb - shared by C6 and C6DC with OPPOSITE direction.
   Anchor chr1:53192788 G>A lowers C6 (z -3.72 disc / -4.28 rep) but raises C6DC (+6.15 / +6.12); within-locus profile r = -0.858. CPT2 (carnitine palmitoyltransferase 2) gates acylcarnitine flux back into mitochondria - consistent with opposite effects on two acylcarnitine species.

GENOME-WIDE POLYGENIC SHARING (beyond single loci):
- A single genetic module of six medium-chain acylcarnitines: C4, C6, C6DC, C8, C8:1, C10:1 (pairwise z-score correlations 0.25-0.81, all FDR q<5.4e-4, replication sign-concordance 82%, corr(r_disc, r_rep)=0.92 across all 78 pairs). Top pair C6-C8 r=0.811 disc / 0.835 rep; after deleting every associated locus r is still 0.768 (permutation p<5e-4), so most of this sharing is polygenic (many weak variants in the same beta-oxidation pathway), not an ACADM artefact.
- Aromatic amino-acid module: PRO-TYR r=0.327 disc / 0.313 rep, also background-driven (0.364 after lead-locus removal).
- 76/78 trait pairs show significant sharing at FDR<0.05; 28 pairs |r|>0.2. Only C0 and ORN/CIT sit outside the acylcarnitine module.

SINGLE-TRAIT (non-shared) LEAD LOCI for context - all replicate:
C0 <- chr11:68.64 Mb nearest CPT1A (3.6e-20 / 4.6e-13); C4 <- ACADS chr12:120.73 Mb (5.4e-25 / 2.2e-23); TYR <- HPD chr12:121.86 Mb (9.5e-34 / 5.3e-11); PRO <- PRODH chr22:18.92 Mb (9.1e-42 / 4.0e-9); C8:1 <- ACSM2A chr16:20.47 Mb (2.8e-12 / 2.2e-6); C10:1 <- CYP4A11 chr1:46.92 Mb (1.8e-10 / 5.2e-15); replicated secondary signals at ETFA (C4) and TM9SF4 (ORN/CIT). 30 index SNPs (p<1e-5); 15/30 replicate at p_rep<0.05 with same direction (14/30 at p_rep<1e-3).

GENETIC vs PHENOTYPIC CORRELATION: Spearman rho between the 78 genetic-sharing values and the 78 phenotypic correlations (log10 abundances, 8,737 newborns) = 0.942 (p=7.8e-75). The sharing structure detected in the GWAS matches the measured metabolite co-regulation almost perfectly - it is biological, not a summary-statistics artefact.

INTERPRETATION: The shared genetic factors are the shared enzymes of mitochondrial fatty-acid oxidation and carnitine shuttling. Newborn-screening acylcarnitines are not independent biomarkers: one ACADM haplotype moves C6, C8, C8/C2 and a dicarboxylic ratio at once (oppositely for the ratio), and one CPT2 haplotype moves C6 vs C6DC in opposite directions. Screening that treats correlated markers as independent will over-call "multiple abnormalities" when a single enzymatic step carries a variant; ratios anchored at the shared locus (e.g. C8/C2 at ACADM) are better-isolated indicators.

NON-REPLICATING (excluded): the chr5:50.16 Mb C6DC/C10:1 signal (p up to 4.6e-10 in discovery) has p_rep 0.23-0.94 and is NOT called shared.

LIMITATIONS: no LD reference panel or rsIDs were available, so clumping is distance-based (1 Mb), fine-mapping is impossible and formal Bayesian colocalization (coloc/eCAVIAR) could not be run - "same causal variant" rests on identical lead positions plus within-locus profile r>0.99, which cannot exclude two linked causal variants; the 20,474-SNP panel is locus-enriched and not genome-wide (47.6% of SNPs have min-p<0.05 across traits vs 5% null), so genetic correlations are panel-weighted approximations and the count of shared loci is a property of this panel; genome build inferred as GRCh38 from gene-position agreement; implied per-cohort N is only ~146, so null sharing (e.g. C0 vs C4DC+C5-OH) is not proof of no shared genetics.

All numbers above come from the three provided files; full code and intermediate tables in gwas-share/scripts/ and gwas-share/output/tables/, figures in gwas-share/output/figures/.
da-24-3.notes: The agent performed a thorough exploratory analysis with replication checks and biological contextualization, but it did not conduct the formal fixed-effects meta-analysis or Bayesian colocalization required by the rubric, leading to low scores on those specific criteria.

For context, under the looser cBioPortal-style "all non-silent" filter the top genes are
TP53 61 (12.2%), SPOP 57 (11.4%), TTN 63, MUC16 38, MUC17 33, KMT2C 30, KMT2D 29, FOXA1 28
(5.6%), SYNE1 27, ATM 22 (4.4%), CHEK2 21. FRG1B nominally ranks #1 there (97 samples, 19.4%)
but is an artefact: 138/138 calls have VAF <= 0.40 (median 0.05) vs TP53 median 0.39, 56/138
carry dbSNP rsIDs, and the counts collapse onto recurrent identical changes (p.A41T x17,
p.L82S x16, p.A83T x14) at the copy-variable 20qter FRG1B locus; after VAF >= 0.20 +
artifact-mode filtering it drops to 0 samples and the ranking becomes TP53 > SPOP > TTN >
FOXA1 > MUC4 > MUC16 > KMT2D > ATM > KMT2C. Long genes (TTN, MUC16, SYNE1, LRP1B, OBSCN)
remain high partly due to gene-length mutation-rate bias.

(2) VISUALISATION
-----------------
Yes - three figures were produced (300 dpi, saved under module-mut-landscape/output/figures/):
- fig1_mutation_landscape.png: (a) top-20 genes by non-silent mutation frequency with
  CGC/pathogenic genes highlighted in a distinct colour, sample counts and % on the bars;
  (b) the strict pathogenic/oncogenic subset; (c) effect-class composition (missense /
  truncating / in-frame indel / splice) per top gene.
- fig3_oncoprint.png: oncoprint (gene x sample matrix) of the 15 most frequent
  pathogenic/oncogenic genes across all 498 mutated patients, colour = effect class, darker
  shade = >1 event, columns ordered by pathologic T stage then mutation burden, with per-gene
  frequency labels.
- fig2_tstage_association.png: (a) mutation-burden strip/median by T stage, (b) TP53 mutation
  vs T2/T3-T4 stacked fractions, (c) volcano of all 96 testable genes vs advanced T.
The same views are obtainable interactively with cBioPortal's "Mutated Genes" bar chart +
oncoprint, or R/Bioconductor maftools (oncoplot / barplot).

(3) GENE ASSOCIATIONS WITH CLINICAL T STAGE
-------------------------------------------
Primary contrast: pathologic T2 (organ-confined, n=188) vs T3/T4 (extraprostatic, n=303);
per-gene 2x2 chi-square for the 96 genes mutated in >=10 staged patients, BH-FDR over 96 tests.

- TP53 is the leading (and only FDR-suggestive) gene-level association: of 60 TP53-mutated
  staged patients, 81.7% were T3/T4 vs 58.9% of TP53-wild-type patients; OR = 3.10,
  chi-square p = 6.9e-4 (Fisher exact p = 5.9e-4), BH-FDR q = 0.066. The association survives
  adjustment for total mutation burden (logistic regression OR = 2.93, p = 0.0021) and appears
  in the clinical-T sensitivity analysis (T2+ vs T1, p = 0.013).
- Secondary nominal hits (all q > 0.3, hypothesis-generating only): enriched in advanced T -
  SPTA1 (OR 4.6, p 0.0077), KMT2D (OR 2.5, p 0.044), ATM (OR 2.9, p 0.047); depleted in
  advanced T - KDM6A (OR 0.27, p 0.020), RP1 (OR 0.27, p 0.011), ZNF845 (OR 0.23, p 0.017).
- Overall mutation burden itself rises with T stage: median non-silent mutations 31 (T2) ->
  36 (T3) -> 55.5 (T4); Kruskal-Wallis H = 22.3, p = 1.4e-5; Spearman rho = 0.19, p = 2.2e-5.
  (With clinical T the gradient is absent, rho = 0.05, p = 0.28, because clinical T saturates
  at T1c/T2.)
- No single gene reached FDR q < 0.05. With 491 staged primary tumours and a low-mutation
  genome, only TP53 approaches significance (q = 0.066); it should be reported as the top
  candidate association, not a confirmed discovery.

CAVEATS: mutation-only analysis - copy-number events (8q24/MYC, PTEN deletion, AR
amplification), ETS fusions, methylation and expression are not in the MAF, so purely
CNV-driven drivers cannot appear; the strict CGC-based definition excludes known non-CGC PRAD
drivers (SPOP, FOXA1, CHD1, MED12), which is why both rankings are given; no MutSigCV/dNdScv
background model was possible (no coverage file); T4 has only 10 patients; residual
confounding of the TP53-T association by grade/aggressiveness cannot be excluded without
multivariable clinical modelling.

Files: trace.md (full methods, code, intermediate counts), analysis module
module-mut-landscape/ (scripts, output tables in output/tables/, figures in output/figures/).
da-25-1.notes: The analysis is strong but has method/reference deviations in pathogenic definition, top gene ranking, and FDR significance; T stage handling and source reliability are excellent.

da-26-2.answer:
FINAL ANSWER — Patient-specific biomarkers of TCGA predicted DepMap scores in BRCA (task DA-26-2)

QUESTION
Using CCLE cancer cell-line gene expression and DepMap scores in cell lines and patients, identify biomarkers that are statistically significant in BRCA when predicting TCGA patient-level DepMap scores but do not manifest in cell-line models.

WHAT WAS DONE
- Cohorts assembled from the provided files: 1,099 BRCA tumors (meta type="tumor", disease="Breast Cancer"; all present in sub_TCGA_depmapscore.txt and, after normalizing dot-barcode sample ids, in sub_TCGA_exp.txt) vs 35 breast cancer cell lines having both CCLE expression (sub_CCLE_exp.Rdata) and CRISPR dependency scores (sub_CCLE_depmapscore.txt; 36 lines have scores, 35 also expression).
- Candidate biomarkers = the 528 genes profiled in sub_TCGA_exp.txt (5S_rRNA dropped); kept genes expressed in >=50% of BRCA tumors (179) and measured in CCLE (82; 49 protein-coding-like, 33 lncRNA-like).
- Analysis A: Spearman correlation of each biomarker's expression vs each dependency gene's score, in patients (predicted DepMap score, n=1,099) and in breast cell lines (measured CRISPR score, n=35). Dependency targets with IQR>0.05 in patients: 1,070 genes; 87,740 patient pairs tested. Significance in patients: BH-FDR q<0.05 and |rho|>=0.3. "Manifests in cell lines" = raw p<0.05 and |rho|>=0.3 (lenient on purpose so patient-specific means the lines show no even nominal signal). Fisher r-to-z (BH q<0.05) used to confirm the effect is significantly STRONGER in patients.
- Analysis B: per dependency gene, Mann-Whitney U of predicted patient scores vs measured line scores with essentiality fraction at score<-0.5.
- Robustness: partial Spearman controlling PC1 of the BRCA expression matrix (14.3% variance, subtype/purity axis) and split-half replication.

HEADLINE NUMBERS
- 2,493 (biomarker x dependency) associations significant in BRCA patients (BH q<0.05, |rho|>=0.3).
- Only 363 (14.6%) of these reproduce in the 35 breast cell lines.
- 2,130 associations across 39 biomarker genes are PATIENT-SPECIFIC (significant in patients, no cell-line counterpart).
- 363 of those pairs (25 biomarkers) also show a significantly stronger effect in patients by Fisher-z (BH q<0.05) — the strictest, power-aware core.
- All 15 top pairs survive partialling out PC1 (|partial rho| 0.26-0.56) and replicate in both split halves (|rho|>=0.40 each half).
- Analysis B: marginal essentiality is conserved (mean patient median -0.454 vs lines -0.447; 166/1,965 genes differ at BH q<0.05 but 0 meet a strict patient-specific-essentiality definition, 11 meet the cell-line-specific one) — the patient-vs-cell-line divergence in this dataset lies in association structure, not in which genes are pan-essential.

TOP PATIENT-SPECIFIC BRCA BIOMARKERS (number of dependency genes predicted in patients but not in cell lines; best partner; rho patient (BH q) vs rho cell line (p)):
1. AC005355.2 (lncRNA) — 264 — ESR1: rho -0.566 (q=5.6e-90) vs CL -0.172 (p=0.32)
2. ABAT — 247 — TXNRD1: +0.590 (q=1.6e-99) vs CL +0.285 (p=0.10)
3. A2ML1 — 192 — LDB1: +0.511 (q=6.8e-71) vs CL +0.085 (p=0.63)
4. ABCC11 — 176 — MAPK14: +0.482 (q=8.6e-62) vs CL +0.239 (p=0.17)
5. AC005863.1 (lncRNA) — 171 — LDB1: +0.476 (q=3.7e-60) vs CL +0.210 (p=0.23)
6. AC009303.2 (lncRNA) — 144 — TXNRD1: -0.452 (q=1.5e-53) vs CL +0.103 (p=0.56) [sign flips]
7. ABCA13 — 142 — ZNF559: +0.482 (q=4.8e-62) vs CL +0.052 (p=0.77)
8. ABTB2 — 133 — SSB: -0.445 (q=8.5e-52) vs CL -0.104 (p=0.55)
9. AAAS — 120 — ESR1: -0.467 (q=8.6e-58) vs CL -0.129 (p=0.46)
10. AAGAB — 118 — EMC7: +0.458 (q=4.3e-55) vs CL +0.325 (p=0.056)
11. AC009495.2 (lncRNA) — 97 — PCGF3: +0.488 (q=1.6e-63) vs CL +0.022 (p=0.90)
12. ABCC12 — 73 — RICTOR: -0.426 (q=3.9e-47) vs CL -0.140 (p=0.42)
13. ABCA12 — 36 — CDC42: +0.404 (q=3.7e-42) vs CL +0.307 (p=0.073)
14. ABCD4 — 31 — ATP6V1D: +0.527 (q=5.0e-76) vs CL +0.303 (p=0.077)
15. ABCB1 (MDR1) — 27 — TBX3: -0.382 (q=2.4e-37) vs CL -0.072 (p=0.68)
Further genes with >=5 patient-specific predictions: ABHD2 (35; ENO1), ABCA9 (24; CMPK1), AARS (19; SMARCE1), AASDH (9; EXOC1), ABHD11 (9; COX6B1), ABCC10 (9; RNASEH2A), ABHD10 (7; ELP2), A2M (7; TRPM7), AACS (6; SUDS3), ABCC6P2 (5; WDR26). Full ranked list: 39 genes in brca_biomarkers/output/tables/biomarker_summary_patient_specific.tsv; all 2,493 pairs in assoc_pairs_patient_sig.tsv.

BIOLOGICAL READ
- ER-axis block: ten biomarkers (AC005355.2, AAAS, ABCA13, A2ML1, ABHD2, ABTB2, AC005863.1, AC007365.1, AC009303.2, AC009495.2) predict ESR1 dependency in patients (rho -0.33 to -0.57) with no significant cell-line counterpart; the 35-line panel has shallow ESR1 CRISPR scores (median -0.11, only 22% below -0.5) while 17% of patients are predicted ESR1-dependent. Coherent with ER-positive breast dependency biology (Marcotte et al., Cell 2016, PMID 26775101; Krall et al., Nat Commun 2017, PMID 28252007) and with the patient cohort being ~70% ER-positive while the small line panel under-represents that phenotype.
- Redox/secretory machinery: ABAT and AC009303.2 both isolate TXNRD1 (thioredoxin reductase); AAGAB -> EMC7 (ER membrane complex); AASDH -> EXOC1; ABCD4 -> ATP6V1D (vacuolar ATPase); ABCB1/MDR1 -> TBX3. Dependency partners most often predicted by patient-specific biomarkers: RMI2 (14 biomarkers), VEZT (13), HECTD1, HUS1, RAD9A, BRPF1, DR1, ENO1, GGT1, PPM1G, RBM10, TFAP2C, TXNRD1, ESR1, MDM2.
- Direction: 20 biomarkers positive (higher expression -> stronger predicted dependency), 19 negative (higher expression -> weaker dependency, dominated by the ESR1 block). Several pairs flip sign between cohorts (e.g. AC009303.2->TXNRD1: -0.45 in patients vs +0.10 in lines) — the clearest form of "does not manifest in cell lines".

LIMITATIONS
- The TCGA scores are model-PREDICTED from expression, so expression->predicted-dependency associations partly restate the predictive model; they are not validated causal vulnerabilities.
- n=35 cell lines only: "absent in cell lines" means not detectable at p<0.05 with |rho|>=0.3; borderline CL p-values (AAGAB-EMC7 0.056; ABCA12-CDC42 0.073; ABCD4-ATP6V1D 0.077) could flip with a larger panel. The Fisher-z subset (363 pairs, 25 biomarkers) is the defensible core.
- The biomarker panel is limited to the 528 genes in sub_TCGA_exp.txt (an A->C genomic block); ESR1, PGR, ERBB2, GATA3 are NOT available as expression rows, only ESR1 appears as a dependency target.
- 97 of 179 usable genes lack CCLE expression measurements and could not be tested cross-cohort.
- No clinical endpoints are in these files, so no prognostic/predictive claims are made.

FILES
- Trace: trace.md; analysis module: brca_biomarkers/ (scripts 02-06, README, output/tables/*.tsv, output/figures/patient_specific_biomarkers.png).
da-26-2.notes: The agent performed a comprehensive association analysis but deviated from the required normality likelihood ratio test, did not classify distributions, did not compute SSD, and did not integrate a druggable gene list; however, data loading, BRCA filtering, comparative logic, and source grounding were strong, and BRCA-known genes were included though PTPN11 was not identified.

da-26-4.answer:
FINAL ANSWER — Synthetic-lethal (SL) partners for loss-of-function (LOF) events in TCGA/CCLE breast cancer (BRCA)

SUMMARY OF METHOD
=================
I defined an SL partner of a driver D as a gene whose measured CRISPR dependency (sub_CCLE_depmapscore.txt) is significantly MORE NEGATIVE in breast cancer cell lines carrying a damaging mutation of D (BRCA_damaging_mut.csv, 74 lines collapsed from 128 replicate rows) than in D-wild-type lines (one-sided Welch t; BH-FDR over ~18,000 targets), and then integrated: (i) lasso regression of each partner's dependency on CCLE expression (top-5,000 MAD features, 5-fold LassoCV alpha, 30x70% subsample stability selection); (ii) mutual-exclusivity testing of (D, partner) damaging mutations across the 74 lines (one-sided Fisher exact); (iii) paralog priors (Ensembl Compara hsapiens_paralog_*) and PPI priors (STRING v12.0, combined_score>=700, proteins mapped to symbols via mygene.info); and (iv) translational relevance = prevalence of predicted dependency (score <= -0.5) among the 1,099 TCGA BRCA tumors (sub_TCGA_depmapscore.txt). Integrated score = 0.50*z_SL + 0.25*z_TCGA + 0.15*prior(paralog 1.0 / PPI 0.5) + 0.10*z_mutex. All effects are LOO-stable in direction (4/4 folds BRCA1, 3/3 BRCA2) and confirmed by Mann-Whitney.

Data QC that shaped the analysis: the provided TCGA expression matrix (sub_TCGA_exp.txt) is alphabetically truncated (528/529 genes start with "A"; BRCA1, BRCA2, RAD51, PARP1 absent) and the provided damaging-mutation matrix is cell-line-based, so a patient-level BRCA1/2-LOF association was impossible; the patient side was therefore used for translational scoring (predicted-dependency prevalence), not for association. 36 breast lines have measured dependency; BRCA1 n=4 and BRCA2 n=3 mutants.

TOP-RANKED SL PARTNERS BY DRIVER (delta = dependency in mutants minus wild type; p = one-sided; prev = fraction of 1,099 TCGA BRCA tumors predicted dependent)

--- BRCA1 LOF (n=4 mutant lines; 913 candidates p<0.05, 85 at BH q<0.25) ---
1. ABCB7        delta=-0.372, p=1.8e-6, q=0.008 (strongest effect)
2. ANKRD39      delta=-0.259, p=1.6e-8, q=0.00015 (top-ranked overall)
3. SCN4B        delta=-0.167, p=1.5e-8, q=0.00027
4. CHMP5 (ESCRT-III) delta=-0.300, p=6.0e-5, prev=1.00 — best translational profile
5. TSG101 (ESCRT-I)  delta=-0.277, p=5.0e-4, prev=1.00
6. USP37        delta=-0.285, p=6.7e-4, prev=1.00, mutual-exclusivity p=0.048
Prior-supported (STRING PPI with BRCA1): CDK12 delta=-0.165 p=2.7e-4; DNMT1 delta=-0.187 p=1.4e-3; MCM10 delta=-0.384 p=1.9e-3; RAD50 p=2.1e-3; RFC2 p=6.5e-3; BRCC3 p=6.6e-3; RB1 p=7.6e-3; ABRAXAS2 p=1.5e-2; STAG1 p=1.7e-2; KIF2C p=1.4e-2.
Interpretation: the BRCA1-deficient dependency program centers on replication-fork protection/MRN (RAD50, ABRAXAS2, RFC2), CDK12 (HR-deficiency phenocopy), and ESCRT/ubiquitin turnover (CHMP5, TSG101, USP37); PARP1 shows the expected direction (delta=-0.201) but is not significant at n=4 mutants.

--- BRCA2 LOF (n=3 mutant lines; 812 candidates, 116 at q<0.25) ---
1. RPA2 (RPA32; STRING PPI with BRCA2) delta=-0.318, p=3.0e-9, q=5.5e-5 — top hit and best-mechanism hit (BRCA2-null cells rely on RPA-coated ssDNA processing; RPA2 state tracks HRd/PARP-inhibitor response)
2. HYPK          delta=-0.330, p=1.3e-6
3. RWDD1         delta=-0.149, p=5.9e-9, q=5.3e-5
4. SEC61B        delta=-0.142, p=2.6e-5, prev=1.00 (translational)
5. MINOS1        delta=-0.301, p=4.1e-5, prev=1.00 (translational)
6. VPS13D        delta=-0.270, p=7.8e-6
Prior-supported PPI partners: MYC delta=-0.141 p=7.4e-3; CDC45 delta=-0.208 p=7.6e-3.
BRCA2 effects hold in both basal and non-basal strata (RPA2 -0.354 non-basal / -0.300 basal), so they are not subtype artefacts.

--- ARID1A LOF (n=3; 729 candidates, 100 at q<0.25) — most prior-coherent list ---
1. RUVBL2        delta=-0.337, p=1.1e-9, q=2.0e-5
2. LAMTOR3       delta=-0.312, p=4.0e-7, prev=1.00
3. VIRMA         delta=-0.222, p=2.5e-5, prev=1.00, mutex p=0.018
Validated literature hits recovered: EZH2 delta=-0.222 p=7.4e-5 q=0.031 (PPI; established ARID1A-mutant vulnerability); SMARCA4 delta=-0.306 p=2.8e-3 (SWI/SNF same-complex); SMARCB1 delta=-0.195 p=4.2e-3 prev=1.00; CCND1 delta=-0.622 p=1.4e-2 prev=0.961; PIK3CA delta=-0.380 p=1.6e-2 prev=0.649; (ARID1A's Compara paralog ARID1B, 50.8% id, shows delta=-0.327 p=0.124 — right direction, underpowered at n=3).

--- TP53 LOF (n=27; only 2 hits survive q<0.25 due to common-essential power loss) ---
Prior-supported: MRE11 delta=-0.170 p=8.1e-3; NBN delta=-0.181 p=6.6e-3 WITH mutual exclusivity p=6.3e-4 (0/2 double mutants); GPX4 delta=-0.403 p=4.9e-3 prev=0.883; HSP90AB1 p=1.2e-3; HMGA1 p=1.4e-3; MYCN p=8.1e-3; XPA p=1.3e-2; HIF1A p=1.2e-2. Best data-driven hit: MOB4 delta=-0.247 p=1.2e-5 prev=1.00.

--- PTEN LOF (n=6) ---
1. PXN (PPI, prev=0.815)        delta=-0.382, p=1.1e-3
2. POT1 (prev=0.77)             delta=-0.396, p=1.0e-3
3. FERMT2 (prev=0.92)           delta=-0.535, p=7.5e-4
4. PIK3CB (PPI; PIK3CA paralog) delta=-0.435, p=7.9e-3 — the established PTEN-null dependency
5. PRKCZ (PPI)                  delta=-0.178, p=5.4e-3
6. PPP1R12B delta=-0.30 p=7.5e-4 with mutex p=0.011

--- NF1 LOF (n=5) ---
1. TSC2 (PPI; mTOR axis)        delta=-0.466, p=9.1e-3
2. RASAL3 (Compara PARALOG of NF1, RAS-GAP family) delta=-0.127, p=3.7e-3
Data-driven: ZNF319 q=0.006; SETD5 q=0.024; WIZ q=0.037 (mutex p=0.022).

CROSS-DRIVER TRANSLATIONAL SHORTLIST (p<0.01 AND predicted dependent in >=50% of the 1,099 BRCA tumors — the largest druggable patient fractions):
ARID1A->LAMTOR3 (prev 1.00), ARID1A->VIRMA (1.00), ARID1A->COG8 (1.00), ARID1A->NAPA (1.00), ARID1A->DCTN2 (1.00), BRCA2->SEC61B (1.00), BRCA2->MINOS1 (1.00), BRCA2->MRPL33 (1.00), BRCA1->CHMP5 (1.00), BRCA1->TSG101 (1.00), BRCA1->USP37 (1.00), TP53->MOB4 (1.00), TP53->TUBA1B (0.999), TP53->CHMP7 (0.999), PTEN->PXN (0.815, PPI), PTEN->FERMT2 (0.924), PTEN->POT1 (0.77), PTEN->NCAPG2/NCAPD3/EIF2B5 (1.00), NF1->GLE1 (0.999), NF1->PPP1R7 (1.00).

MUTUAL-EXCLUSIVITY HIGHLIGHTS (one-sided Fisher, 74 lines): TP53-NBN p=6.3e-4; TP53-SMCP p=6.3e-4; ARID1A-NF1 p=7.0e-4; PTEN-FLT4 p=7.3e-4; BRCA1-MUC4 p=1.3e-3; PTEN-SORL1 p=3.7e-3; ARID1A-CDKN2A p=5.6e-3; BRCA2-NUMA1 p=0.022; BRCA1-USP37 p=0.048. These depletions of double LOF corroborate the SL calls.

PARALOG/PPI PRIOR FINDINGS: Ensembl Compara returns NO paralogs for BRCA1 or BRCA2 (so no paralog-buffering prior exists for them; their partners are PPI-supported instead). Paralog-supported hits in the final list: NF1->RASAL3 (RAS-GAP family), TP53 paralog pairs TP73/TP63 identified but not significant partners, PTEN paralogs TPTE/TPTE2/TNS3 identified (TPTE2 not a dependency hit). STRING v12 (>=700) supported 84 of the scored pairs, including BRCA1-RAD50/RFC2/BRCC3/CDK12/DNMT1, BRCA2-RPA2/MYC/CDC45, ARID1A-EZH2/SMARCA4/SMARCB1/CDKN2A/CCND1/PIK3CA, PTEN-PXN/PIK3CB/PRKCZ, NF1-TSC2, TP53-MRE11/NBN/GPX4/HSP90AB1/HMGA1.

LASSO FINDINGS (used as supporting evidence only): dependency of top partners is only weakly predictable from expression at n=35 lines (5-fold CV R^2 <= 0.03; e.g. CHMP5 0.028, MOB4 0.013, RPA2 -0.109), and the driver's own mRNA is never selected as a predictor of partner dependency (selection frequency 0.00 for BRCA1/BRCA2/ARID1A/PTEN/NF1, max 0.067 for TP53) — i.e. the LOF state, not driver expression, drives the dependencies, and lasso cannot replace the mutation-association test here.

BOTTOM LINE (best-supported candidates): For BRCA2 LOF: RPA2 (p=3e-9, STRING-PPI-supported, mechanistically aligned with HR deficiency). For BRCA1 LOF: ABCB7/ANKRD39/SCN4B (strongest statistics), CHMP5/TSG101/USP37 (statistics + predicted dependency in ~100% of BRCA tumors), CDK12/DNMT1/MCM10/RAD50 (PPI-prior supported). For the other frequent BRCA LOF events: ARID1A->EZH2/RUVBL2/LAMTOR3, PTEN->PXN/PIK3CB/PRKCZ/POT1, NF1->TSC2/RASAL3, TP53->MRE11/NBN (with mutual exclusivity)/GPX4.

KEY LIMITATIONS: (1) BRCA1 effects rest on 4 mutant lines, all basal-like (Fisher p=0.045 vs basal proxy), so BRCA1-vs-subtype confounding cannot be excluded in this panel; BRCA2 effects survive stratification. (2) TP53/PTEN lose multiple-testing power (thousands of common-essential targets) and their shortlists rest on nominal p plus priors. (3) TCGA dependency is model-predicted, not measured, so translational scores are not independent validation. (4) Patient-level BRCA1/2 LOF phenotypes could not be built (truncated TCGA expression file; cell-line-only mutation matrix). (5) Common-essential partners (CHMP5, TSG101, SEC61B) indicate differential dependency; clinical selectivity windows cannot be inferred. Full tables: analysis/final_ranked.tsv (5,486 scored pairs), analysis/shortlist.tsv, per-driver screens analysis/sl_screen_*.tsv.
da-26-4.notes: The analysis implemented cross-validated lasso, Fisher-based mutual exclusivity testing, curated paralog/PPI resources, translational prevalence scoring, and comprehensive source documentation. However, it did not refine lasso candidates with a dual effect-size/FDR threshold, did not use iterative mutual-exclusivity prioritization, lacked a sequence-similarity paralog filter, and failed to report canonical BRCA paralog pairs or observed-vs-expected co-occurrence tables.

da-1-3.answer:
Across the 957,342 cells from the three requested compartments (58 tumor, 52 adjacent-normal, and 56 blood samples), broad lineage composition differed markedly by tissue. Pooled proportions (with median per-sample proportions in parentheses) were:

- Tumor: T 42.50% (39.35%), epithelial 28.22% (28.71%), B 17.03% (15.30%), stromal 6.23% (4.87%), myeloid 4.15% (3.35%), ILC 1.87% (1.75%).
- Adjacent normal: epithelial 35.62% (35.96%), T 27.89% (26.25%), B 24.85% (23.88%), stromal 8.89% (6.80%), myeloid 1.82% (1.53%), ILC 0.93% (0.90%).
- Blood: T 67.08% (67.68%), myeloid 12.35% (11.14%), B 10.34% (8.82%), ILC 9.74% (7.80%), epithelial 0.35% (median 0%), stromal 0.14% (median 0%).

Thus, no broad lineage is uniquely and highly tumor-enriched relative to both normal tissue and blood. The tumor-specific signal occurs at subtype resolution.

Using samples as biological replicates, one-sided Mann–Whitney tests with Benjamini–Hochberg correction, and a stringent definition of high TME enrichment (q<0.05 versus both controls, >=5-fold higher mean fraction versus both, tumor median >=0.1%, and presence in >=25% of tumor samples), eight core subsets were identified. Values are median sample percentages in Tumor / Normal / Blood:

1. c13_CD4_Treg_TNFRSF9: 2.365 / 0.284 / 0%; 6.11-fold vs normal and 337.6-fold vs blood; q=1.41e-11 and 3.49e-20.
2. c23_CD8_Tex_LAYN: 1.628 / 0.061 / 0%; 17.15-fold and 617.6-fold; q=1.91e-11 and 3.49e-20.
3. c07_CD4_Th17_CTSH: 0.684 / 0.131 / 0%; 5.61-fold and 346.5-fold; q=7.72e-7 and 3.53e-20.
